    private val onSpeech: (SpeechInstruction) -> Unit,
) : NavigationListener {
    override fun onNavigationInstruction(instruction: NavigationInstruction) {
        onInstruction(instruction)
    }

    override fun onSpeechInstruction(speechInstruction: SpeechInstruction) {
        onSpeech(speechInstruction)
    }

    override fun onDeviationStatusChange(deviationStatusChange: DeviationStatusChange) {
        // Update your reroute affordance here.
    }

    override fun onNavigationPhaseChange(navigationPhaseChange: NavigationPhaseChange) {
        // Drive the navigation drawer's phase state here.
    }
}

val navigationController = Navigator()
val listener = GuidanceListener(onInstruction = ::showBanner, onSpeech = ::speak)

// One call subscribes the listener to all four topics; the returned
// subscription cancels every one of them.
val subscription = navigationController.addNavigationListener(listener)

// The four per-topic calls remain available when a screen needs only
// some of the channels:
//   navigationController.subscribeToNavigationInstructions(listener)
//   navigationController.subscribeToSpeechInstructions(listener)
//   navigationController.subscribeToDeviationStatus(listener)
//   navigationController.subscribeToPhaseChanges(listener)

A subscription is cancelled with its handle when your screen leaves; dropping the reference does not unsubscribe.

Start the trip

Use the default policies unless you measured different ones for your product:

import uniffi.rustic_maps.defaultDeviationPolicy
import uniffi.rustic_maps.defaultStepAdvancePolicy
import uniffi.rustic_maps.UnitSystem

navigationController.startNavigation(
    route,
    UnitSystem.METRIC,
    defaultStepAdvancePolicy(),
    defaultDeviationPolicy(),
)

The initial instruction payload dispatches before the call returns; the banner shows the first maneuver.

Deliver position fixes

Deliver one fix at a time, as a live location source or a recorded trace does:

import uniffi.rustic_maps.NavigationLocationUpdate

suspend fun replayFixes(
    navigationController: Navigator,
    samples: Sequence<GeographicCoordinate>,
    sampleIntervalMilliseconds: Long,
) {
    for (sample in samples) {
        navigationController.updateLocation(
            NavigationLocationUpdate(
                coordinate = sample,
                horizontalAccuracyMeters = 8.0,
                courseHeadingDegrees = null,
                timestampSeconds = null,
            ),
        )
        delay(sampleIntervalMilliseconds)
    }
}

Fixes without a reported accuracy never advance a step and are never judged for deviation, so a simulated source must carry its accuracy like a real fix does.

Draw the trip on the map

Navigation state is half the experience; the map also has to show the route and follow the vehicle. Two calls do it: the route polyline goes on as an overlay, and each fix rebuilds the camera.

// Once, when the route arrives: the route geometry as one polyline.
val routeOverlay = MapOverlay(
    kind = MapOverlayKind.ROUTE_POLYLINE,
    coordinates = route.legs.flatMap { leg -> leg.steps.flatMap { step -> step.shape } },
    rgbaColor = OverlayColor(red = 0.16, green = 0.47, blue = 1.0, alpha = 0.95),
    widthPixels = 6.0,
    ringCoordinates = null,
    pointMarkerPositions = null,
    pointMarkerRadiusPixels = null,
    trafficFlowSegments = null,
)
mapView.setOverlays(listOf(routeOverlay))

// On every fix (or every instruction, if you follow instructions instead
// of raw fixes): a 3D course-up camera over the vehicle.
val followCamera = MapCameraPose(
    latitudeDegrees = fix.coordinate.latitude,
    longitudeDegrees = fix.coordinate.longitude,
    zoomLevel = followZoomLevel,
    bearingDegrees = smoothedCourseHeadingDegrees,
    pitchDegrees = followPitchDegrees,
)
mapView.setLocationIndicator(locationIndicatorState, locationIndicatorStyle)
mapView.setCamera(followCamera)

Keep the bearing smoothed rather than raw: a fix-to-fix course jitters at low speed, and a camera that follows it reads as shaky. When the user pans away, stop drawing the follow camera until they tap the location control to re-center.

Voice the speech channel

The platform owns playback; the SDK owns when a line is newsworthy. When onSpeechInstruction delivers a SpeechInstruction, hand its verbatim text to the platform’s speech engine:

val textToSpeechEngine = TextToSpeech(context, this)
// onSpeechInstruction:
textToSpeechEngine.speak(
    speechInstruction.utteranceSpeechText,
    TextToSpeech.QUEUE_ADD,
    null,
    speechInstruction.utteranceId.toString(),
)

The utterance id is the contract’s monotonic id, so your dedup keeps its identity across repeats.

Reroute when guidance freezes

A deviating trip asks for a replacement route through the controller’s checks. Keep the state machine in your own coordinator:

if (tripState.deviation?.gradeKind == DeviationGradeKind.FULLY_OFF_ROUTE &&
    navigationController.beginRerouteCalculation()
) {
    coroutineScope.launch {
        val replacement = mapSdk.calculateRoute(
            listOf(currentFixCoordinate, originalDestination),
            routeOptions,
        )
        navigationController.applyReroute(replacement, defaultStepAdvancePolicy())
    }
} else {
    navigationController.cancelRerouteCalculation()
}

End the trip

// Clears the active trip and its state; later fixes and reroutes are
// dropped until the next startNavigation. Subscriptions stay registered
// and serve the next trip.
navigationController.stopNavigation()

Build the controller and subscribe first

The same four callbacks arrive on a Swift object that conforms to NavigationListener:

import RusticMapsSDK

final class GuidanceListener: NavigationListener {
    func onNavigationInstruction(instruction: NavigationInstruction) {
        // Update the banner instruction.
    }

    func onSpeechInstruction(speechInstruction: SpeechInstruction) {
        // Hand the verbatim text to your speech engine.
    }

    func onDeviationStatusChange(deviationStatusChange: DeviationStatusChange) {
        // Update the reroute affordance.
    }

    func onNavigationPhaseChange(navigationPhaseChange: NavigationPhaseChange) {
        // Drive the phase state.
    }
}

let navigationController = Navigator()
let listener = GuidanceListener()

// One call subscribes all four topics; cancel() removes all four.
let subscription = navigationController.addNavigationListener(listener: listener)

Start the trip

try navigationController.startNavigation(
    route: route,
    unitSystem: UnitSystem.metric,
    stepAdvancePolicy: defaultStepAdvancePolicy(),
    deviationPolicy: defaultDeviationPolicy()
)

Deliver position fixes

func deliver(_ fix: RecordedFix) {
    navigationController.updateLocation(
        locationUpdate: NavigationLocationUpdate(
            coordinate: fix.coordinate,
            horizontalAccuracyMeters: fix.horizontalAccuracyMeters,
            courseHeadingDegrees: fix.courseHeadingDegrees,
            timestampSeconds: nil
        )
    )
    if let tripState = navigationController.currentTripState() {
        updateReadouts(tripState)
    }
}

Draw the trip on the map

Put the route on the map once and follow it with every fix:

let routeOverlay = MapOverlay(
    kind: .routePolyline,
    coordinates: route.legs.flatMap { $0.steps.flatMap { $0.shape } },
    rgbaColor: OverlayColor(red: 0.16, green: 0.47, blue: 1.0, alpha: 0.95),
    widthPixels: 6.0,
    ringCoordinates: nil,
    pointMarkerPositions: nil,
    pointMarkerRadiusPixels: nil,
    trafficFlowSegments: nil
)
_ = mapView.setOverlays([routeOverlay])

let followCamera = MapCameraPose(
    latitudeDegrees: fix.coordinate.latitude,
    longitudeDegrees: fix.coordinate.longitude,
    zoomLevel: followZoomLevel,
    bearingDegrees: smoothedCourseHeadingDegrees,
    pitchDegrees: followPitchDegrees
)
mapView.setLocationIndicator(state: locationIndicatorState, style: locationIndicatorStyle)
mapView.setCamera(followCamera)

The camera follows the smoothed course, not the raw fix-to-fix bearing, and a pan gesture hands control back to the user until the location control is tapped again.

Voice the speech channel

let speechEngine = AVSpeechSynthesizer()
// In onSpeechInstruction:
let utterance = AVSpeechUtterance(string: speechInstruction.utteranceSpeechText)
utterance.voice = AVSpeechSynthesisVoice(language: "en-US")
speechEngine.speak(utterance)

Reroute when guidance freezes

if tripState.deviation?.gradeKind == .fullyOffRoute {
    if navigationController.beginRerouteCalculation() {
        let replacement = try await mapSdk.calculateRoute(
            waypoints: [currentFixCoordinate, originalDestination],
            routeOptions: routeOptions
        )
        try navigationController.applyReroute(
            route: replacement,
            stepAdvancePolicy: defaultStepAdvancePolicy()
        )
    } else {
        navigationController.cancelRerouteCalculation()
    }
}

The trip state readback (currentTripState()) carries the phase, the progress, and isCalculatingNewRoute so your UI can show the recalculation honestly.

End the trip

// Clears the active trip and its state; subscriptions stay registered.
navigationController.stopNavigation()

Build the controller and subscribe first

Subscribe before you start the trip, so you receive the initial instruction dispatch. The package exposes the same navigation controller to JavaScript:

import {
  Navigator,
  UnitSystem,
  defaultStepAdvancePolicy,
  defaultDeviationPolicy,
} from '@angoratek/rustic-maps-sdk';

const navigationController = new Navigator();

// One listener implements the four callbacks the contract carries; one call
// subscribes all four, and cancel() removes them together.
const listener = {
  onNavigationInstruction(instruction) {
    setNextManeuver({
      instructionText: instruction.activeManeuver.instruction.composedDisplayText,
      distancePhrase: instruction.activeManeuver.distancePhrase,
      isReroutingRequired: instruction.isReroutingRequired,
    });
  },
  onSpeechInstruction(speechInstruction) {
    speak(speechInstruction.utteranceSpeechText);
  },
  onDeviationStatusChange(deviationStatusChange) {
    setDeviation(deviationStatusChange);
  },
  onNavigationPhaseChange(navigationPhaseChange) {
    setPhase(navigationPhaseChange);
  },
};

const subscription = navigationController.addNavigationListener(listener);

Each callback delivers the same payloads the native platforms receive, with lower camel case field names. Cancel the subscription with its handle when your screen leaves; dropping the reference does not unsubscribe.

Start the trip

Use the default policies unless you measured different ones for your product:

navigationController.startNavigation(
  route,
  UnitSystem.Metric,
  defaultStepAdvancePolicy(),
  defaultDeviationPolicy(),
);

The initial instruction payload dispatches before the call returns; the banner shows the first maneuver.

Deliver position fixes

Deliver one fix per sample of your location source or its recorded trace:

navigationController.updateLocation({
  coordinate: { latitude: sampleLatitude, longitude: sampleLongitude },
  horizontalAccuracyMeters: 8.0,
  courseHeadingDegrees: undefined,
  timestampSeconds: undefined,
});

const tripState = navigationController.currentTripState();

Fixes without a reported accuracy never advance a step and are never judged for deviation, so a simulated source must carry its accuracy like a real fix does.

Draw the trip on the map

The package’s MapView handle exposes the overlay, camera and location-indicator members the contract carries. Put the route on once, then drive the next-maneuver card from the listener subscribed above and the follow camera from each accepted fix:

import {
  LocationIndicatorVisualKind,
  MapOverlayKind,
} from '@angoratek/rustic-maps-sdk';

// Once, when the route arrives: one polyline over the whole route.
const routeOverlay = {
  kind: MapOverlayKind.RoutePolyline,
  coordinates: route.legs.flatMap(
    (leg) => leg.steps.flatMap((step) => step.shape),
  ),
  rgbaColor: { red: 0.16, green: 0.47, blue: 1.0, alpha: 0.95 },
  widthPixels: 6.0,
};
mapView.setOverlays([routeOverlay]);

// On every accepted fix: the 3D course-up follow camera (z17, 45° pitch,
// the shared demo values). The handle takes the same five-value pose the
// other tabs use, and the guided arrow sits over the vehicle.
const FOLLOW_ZOOM_LEVEL = 17.0;
const FOLLOW_PITCH_DEGREES = 45.0;
const followCamera = {
  latitudeDegrees: fix.latitude,
  longitudeDegrees: fix.longitude,
  zoomLevel: FOLLOW_ZOOM_LEVEL,
  bearingDegrees: smoothedCourseHeadingDegrees,
  pitchDegrees: FOLLOW_PITCH_DEGREES,
};
mapView.setLocationIndicator(
  {
    coordinate: { latitude: fix.latitude, longitude: fix.longitude },
    courseHeadingDegrees: smoothedCourseHeadingDegrees,
  },
  { visualKind: LocationIndicatorVisualKind.GuidedCourseArrow },
);
mapView.setCamera(followCamera);

The camera follows the smoothed course, not the raw fix-to-fix bearing, and a pan gesture hands control back to the user until the location control is tapped again.

Voice the speech channel

The SDK triggers; your application voices. In the speech callback, hand the verbatim text to the platform’s speech engine (Expo’s Speech, or your own TTS wrapper), and use the delivery’s utteranceId for dedup:

function onSpeechInstruction(speechInstruction) {
  Speech.speak(speechInstruction.utteranceSpeechText, {
    language: 'en-US',
    onDone: () => markUtteranceComplete(speechInstruction.utteranceId),
  });
}

Reroute when guidance freezes

A deviating trip asks for a replacement route through the controller’s reroute checks. Keep the state machine in your own coordinator:

import { DeviationGradeKind } from '@angoratek/rustic-maps-sdk';

const tripState = navigationController.currentTripState();
if (
  tripState?.deviation?.gradeKind === DeviationGradeKind.FullyOffRoute &&
  navigationController.beginRerouteCalculation()
) {
  const replacement = await mapSdk.calculateRoute(
    [
      { latitude: fix.latitude, longitude: fix.longitude },
      destinationPlace.coordinate,
    ],
    routeOptions,
  );
  navigationController.applyReroute(
    replacement,
    defaultStepAdvancePolicy(),
  );
} else {
  navigationController.cancelRerouteCalculation();
}

The trip state readback carries the phase, the progress and isCalculatingNewRoute, so your UI can show the recalculation honestly.

End the trip

// Clears the active trip and its state; subscriptions stay registered.
navigationController.stopNavigation();

Start the navigator on the route

The browser Navigator carries the driving and readback calls: startNavigation, updateLocation, applyReroute, stopNavigation, and currentTripState, plus hasActiveTrip. addNavigationListener registers a JavaScript callback that receives one event per topic: instruction, phase, deviation, speech, or stop. removeNavigationListener removes it by id.

Create the navigator on the route you planned and drive it with the same walker the native tabs use. Each updateLocation returns the trip snapshot; the phase, the instruction payload, the progress numbers, and the deviation all come from that one call:

import { Navigator, RouteSimulator } from './web/map_web_bindings.js';

const navigationController = new Navigator();
navigationController.startNavigation(route, 'metric');

const navigationRouteSimulator = new RouteSimulator(route, {
  speedMetersPerSecond: 1.4,
  speedMultiplier: 20.0,
});

const navigationFix = navigationRouteSimulator.fixAtElapsedSeconds(0.0);
const tripSnapshot = navigationController.updateLocation({
  coordinate: navigationFix.coordinate,
  horizontalAccuracyMeters: 8.0,
  courseHeadingDegrees: navigationFix.courseHeadingDegrees,
  timestampSeconds: null,
});

// One snapshot is all the card needs.
const phase = tripSnapshot.phase;
const distancePhrase = tripSnapshot.instruction.activeManeuver.distancePhraseText;
const bannerText = tripSnapshot.instruction.activeManeuver.providerDisplayText
  ?? tripSnapshot.instruction.activeManeuver.displayText;
const thenText = tripSnapshot.instruction.upcomingManeuver?.displayText ?? '';
const metersToManeuver =
  tripSnapshot.instruction.progress.distanceToNextManeuverMeters;
const metersRemaining = tripSnapshot.instruction.progress.distanceRemainingMeters;
const secondsRemaining = tripSnapshot.instruction.progress.durationRemainingSeconds;
const deviationMeters = tripSnapshot.deviation?.distanceFromRouteMeters ?? null;

A fix without an accuracy is never judged and never advances a step, so a simulated source carries its accuracy like a real fix. stopNavigation ends the trip, and applyReroute swaps the route without restarting the navigator. The banner keeps two lines: distancePhraseText names the distance and providerDisplayText is the provider’s own sentence, so the distance is not printed twice.

Simulate the trip and follow it

Create the simulator once from the planned route and a pace, then ask it for a fix at an elapsed time. The fix carries a coordinate, the courseHeadingDegrees, the travelled and remaining meters, and isArrived. Draw the route, place the location indicator on the fix, and present a course-up camera frame:

import { RouteSimulator } from './web/map_web_bindings.js';

/** @type {any} */
const plannedRoute = route;
const routeOverlay = {
  kind: 'routePolyline',
  coordinates: plannedRoute.legs.flatMap(
    (leg) => leg.steps.flatMap((step) => step.shape),
  ),
  color: { red: 0.16, green: 0.47, blue: 1.0, alpha: 0.95 },
  widthPixels: 6.0,
};

const ROUTE_SIMULATOR_SPEED_METERS_PER_SECOND = 1.4;
const ROUTE_SIMULATOR_SPEED_MULTIPLIER = 20.0;
const FOLLOW_ZOOM_LEVEL = 17.0;
const FOLLOW_PITCH_DEGREES = 45.0;
const fieldOfViewDegrees = 60.0;
const elapsedSeconds = 0.0;

const routeSimulator = new RouteSimulator(plannedRoute, {
  speedMetersPerSecond: ROUTE_SIMULATOR_SPEED_METERS_PER_SECOND,
  speedMultiplier: ROUTE_SIMULATOR_SPEED_MULTIPLIER,
});
const fix = routeSimulator.fixAtElapsedSeconds(elapsedSeconds);

mapView.setOverlays([routeOverlay]);
mapView.setLocationIndicator(
  { coordinate: fix.coordinate, courseHeadingDegrees: fix.courseHeadingDegrees },
  { visualKind: 'guidedCourseArrow' },
);
await mapView.renderFrame(
  new MapCamera(
    fix.coordinate.latitude,
    fix.coordinate.longitude,
    FOLLOW_ZOOM_LEVEL,
    fix.courseHeadingDegrees ?? 0.0,
    FOLLOW_PITCH_DEGREES,
  ),
  fieldOfViewDegrees,
);

Advance elapsedSeconds on your own tick and call fixAtElapsedSeconds again for each frame; fixAtTravelledMeters is the distance-driven equivalent. totalDistanceMeters() and totalDurationSeconds() size the trip’s progress bar, and isArrived turns true exactly at the final coordinate. The route and step records are the same Route/RouteLeg/RouteStep objects the native surfaces return, so the polyline extraction is identical.

Offline maps

Keep map imagery and routing working without a network. Two independent layers do it: a disk response cache that holds raster tile imagery under your byte budget, and a compiled routing archive that returns routes with no network round trip.

Register the providers with a tile cache

One registration call installs the map-platform provider set and wraps the raster-tile contract in the disk response cache:

val tileCacheDatabaseFile = File(context.cacheDir, "reference-tile-cache.sqlite")
val tileCacheBudgetBytes = 16777216UL   // 16 MiB

mapSdk.setProviderCredentialWithTileCache(
    providerApiKey,
    tileCacheDatabaseFile.absolutePath,
    tileCacheBudgetBytes,
)

The call opens or creates the SQLite response cache at the path. A refusal, such as an unusable path or a non-positive budget, returns the reason verbatim.

Read and tune the caching terms

The cache starts at the tiles category’s default time-to-live of 30 calendar days, the imagery-provider terms ceiling. Tune the live value and read the value in force:

mapSdk.setRasterTileCacheTimeToLive(timeToLiveSeconds)
val terms = mapSdk.rasterTileCacheTerms()
// terms.effectiveTimeToLiveSeconds
// terms.providerTermsCeilingSeconds
// terms.defaultTimeToLiveSeconds

// The same calls through the offline facade:
// val offlineManager = OfflineManager(mapSdk)
// offlineManager.setTileTimeToLive(timeToLiveSeconds)
// val terms = offlineManager.tileCacheTerms()

A request above the provider’s declared ceiling is accepted, and the ceiling clamps what the cache retains; the readback shows the effective value, so display it in your offline-maps settings screen.

Pre-warm the tiles you need

Cached tile responses render whenever the network is unavailable: a cache miss goes to the network and back-fills, and a cache hit comes from disk. Render the regions your users expect to revisit once while online, and the cache holds them until the budget or time-to-live says otherwise.

Route without the network

The offline routing layer runs inside the SDK: a compiled routing archive — OpenStreetMap extract in, self-describing archive file out — returns routes with A* over the archive’s graph, honoring recorded turn restrictions and deriving maneuver text from the geometry’s bearing change.

The contract carries the route call on every surface. Pass the archive bytes, not a path, so the same call works on Android, iOS, React Native, and the browser.

import uniffi.rustic_maps.GeographicCoordinate
import uniffi.rustic_maps.offlineRouteFromArchiveBytes

// The compiled RMOG archive's bytes, bundled with the app or downloaded.
val archiveBytes: ByteArray = archiveFile.readBytes()
val plannedRoute = offlineRouteFromArchiveBytes(
    archiveBytes,
    GeographicCoordinate(latitude = 0.001, longitude = 0.0),
    GeographicCoordinate(latitude = 0.001, longitude = 0.002),
)

The request uses the archive profile’s default options: automobile, fastest, metric. A corrupt archive throws OfflineRoutingFailure. The SDK does not fall back to the archive when the online provider fails; catch the online failure and call the archive route yourself. Maneuver texts stay honest where the extract carries no street names.

Register the providers with a tile cache

let tileCacheDatabasePath = FileManager.default
    .urls(for: .cachesDirectory, in: .userDomainMask)[0]
    .appendingPathComponent("reference-tile-cache.sqlite")
    .path
let tileCacheBudgetBytes: UInt64 = 16_777_216   // 16 MiB

try mapSdk.setProviderCredentialWithTileCache(
    mapquestApiKey: providerApiKey,
    tileCacheDatabasePath: tileCacheDatabasePath,
    tileCacheAbsoluteMaximumBytes: tileCacheBudgetBytes
)

Read and tune the caching terms

try mapSdk.setRasterTileCacheTimeToLive(timeToLiveSeconds: timeToLiveSeconds)
let terms = try mapSdk.rasterTileCacheTerms()
// terms.effectiveTimeToLiveSeconds
// terms.providerTermsCeilingSeconds
// terms.defaultTimeToLiveSeconds

// The same calls through the offline facade:
// let offlineManager = OfflineManager(mapSdk: mapSdk)
// try offlineManager.setTileTimeToLive(timeToLiveSeconds: timeToLiveSeconds)
// let terms = try offlineManager.tileCacheTerms()

Pre-warm and render offline

Cached tiles render whenever the network is unavailable. Render the regions your users revisit while online; the cache serves them from disk.

Route without the network

The offline routing layer runs inside the SDK over a compiled archive: A* on the archive’s graph, recorded turn restrictions honored, maneuver text derived from the geometry. The contract call takes the archive bytes, not a path, so the same call works on every platform:

// The compiled RMOG archive's bytes, bundled with the app or downloaded.
let archiveURL = URL(fileURLWithPath: "routing_grid.rmog")
let archiveBytes = try Data(contentsOf: archiveURL)
let plannedRoute = try await offlineRouteFromArchiveBytes(
    archiveBytes: archiveBytes,
    start: GeographicCoordinate(latitude: 0.001, longitude: 0.0),
    end: GeographicCoordinate(latitude: 0.001, longitude: 0.002)
)

The request uses the archive profile’s default options: automobile, fastest, metric. A corrupt archive throws OfflineRoutingFailure. The SDK does not fall back to the archive when the online provider fails; catch the online failure and call the archive route yourself.

Register the providers with a tile cache

The package’s SDK handle installs the provider set and wraps the raster-tile contract in the disk response cache:

import { MapsSdk } from '@angoratek/rustic-maps-sdk/MapsSdk';

async function createMapSdkWithTileCache(providerKey, providerApiKey) {
  const mapSdk = await MapsSdk.create();
  const registration = await mapSdk.setProviderCredentialWithTileCache(
    providerKey,
    providerApiKey,
  );
  if (!registration.isApplied) {
    throw new Error(registration.detailText);
  }
  return mapSdk;
}

The package opens (or creates) the cache under the application’s caches directory with a 16 MiB budget; JavaScript passes the provider key and the credential, never a file path. A refusal resolves with isApplied: false and the provider’s verbatim detailText. Re-registration replaces the raster-tile slot, cache included.

Read and tune the caching terms

The cache starts at the tiles category’s default time-to-live of 30 calendar days, the imagery-provider terms ceiling. Tune the live value and read the value in force:

import { MapsSdk } from '@angoratek/rustic-maps-sdk/MapsSdk';

const mapSdk = await MapsSdk.create();
const oneWeekInSeconds = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60;
await mapSdk.setTileCacheTimeToLive(oneWeekInSeconds);
const terms = await mapSdk.tileCacheTerms();
if (terms !== null) {
  // terms.effectiveTimeToLiveSeconds
  // terms.providerTermsCeilingSeconds
  // terms.defaultTimeToLiveSeconds
}

A request above the provider’s declared ceiling is accepted, and the ceiling clamps what the cache retains; the readback shows the effective value, so display it in your offline-maps settings screen.

Pre-warm the tiles you need

Cached tile responses render whenever the network is unavailable: a cache miss goes to the network and back-fills, and a cache hit answers from disk. Render the regions your users expect to revisit once while online, and the cache holds them until the budget or time-to-live says otherwise.

Route without the network

The compiled routing archive returns routes with A* over its graph, honoring recorded turn restrictions and deriving maneuver text from the geometry. The generated bindings carry the contract’s archive-route call; pass the bytes, not a path:

import { offlineRouteFromArchiveBytes } from '@angoratek/rustic-maps-sdk';

// The compiled RMOG archive's bytes, bundled with the app or downloaded.
const archiveResponse = await fetch('routing_grid.rmog');
const archiveBytes = await archiveResponse.arrayBuffer();
const plannedOfflineRoute = await offlineRouteFromArchiveBytes(
  archiveBytes,
  { latitude: 0.001, longitude: 0.0 },
  { latitude: 0.001, longitude: 0.002 },
);

The request uses the archive profile’s default options: automobile, fastest, metric. A corrupt archive rejects with OfflineRoutingFailure. The SDK does not fall back to the archive when an online route fails; handle that failure in your own code.

What the browser surface carries

The browser surface has no SDK-owned cache: there is no SQLite tile cache, no byte budget, and no pack manager. The cache-terms and pre-warm steps of the native tabs have no counterpart here. What the WebAssembly build carries is the routing archive: archive bytes in, route records out, with no provider and no network round trip. The same compiled archive serves the native platforms, so one compile feeds every target.

Route over the archive

import { offlineRouteFromArchiveBytes } from './web/map_web_bindings.js';

const archiveResponse = await fetch('/offline-graph/routing-grid.rmog');
const archiveBytes = new Uint8Array(await archiveResponse.arrayBuffer());

const plannedRoute = await offlineRouteFromArchiveBytes(
  archiveBytes,
  originLatitude,
  originLongitude,
  endLatitude,
  endLongitude,
);

The result is the same Route/RouteLeg/RouteStep record the live route call returns, so the route overlay and framing steps from Search and routing apply unchanged. The call rejects with the reason when the bytes fail archive validation, a coordinate falls outside every node’s snap tolerance, or the two points are not connected in the graph.

Where the bytes come from is the page’s decision: ship the archive with the app, fetch it once and keep it in the browser’s own storage, or read it from <input type="file"> for a local preview.

Show the device’s location

Show the user’s position on the map: a tracking dot with the source’s accuracy ring, a camera centred on the fix, and an honest line when the permission is denied or the service is unavailable.

The host owns the operating system’s location API and its permission prompt. Every host pushes its fixes into the same Rust PositionController, which validates them, ignores stationary repeats when smoothing course and tracks staleness. The renderer draws the dot; the camera and the navigation controller read the same stream.

The shared scenario

  • Start the source after the permission is granted.
  • Draw the renderer’s tracking dot with showAccuracyRing and the controller’s smoothed course.
  • Centre the camera on each fix at follow zoom 15.
  • Stop the source when the control is turned off and clear the layer.
  • State a denied permission, a disabled service, an unavailable source and a timeout in the same words on every platform.

Android

import com.angoratek.rusticmaps.DeviceLocationSource
import uniffi.rustic_maps.LocationIndicatorState
import uniffi.rustic_maps.LocationIndicatorStyle
import uniffi.rustic_maps.LocationIndicatorVisualKind
import uniffi.rustic_maps.PositionController

val positionController = PositionController()
val deviceLocationSource = DeviceLocationSource(
    context = context,
    positionController = positionController,
    onFix = { fix ->
        mapView.setLocationIndicator(
            state = LocationIndicatorState(
                coordinate = fix.coordinate,
                courseHeadingDegrees = positionController.smoothedCourseDegrees(),
                horizontalAccuracyMeters = fix.horizontalAccuracyMeters,
            ),
            style = LocationIndicatorStyle(
                visualKind = LocationIndicatorVisualKind.TRACKING_DOT,
                radiusPixels = null,
                rgbaColor = null,
                showAccuracyRing = true,
            ),
        )
    },
)
// Request ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION at runtime first; then:
if (!deviceLocationSource.start()) {
    // Read positionController.sourceStatus() for the honest reason.
}
// Later, when the control is turned off:
deviceLocationSource.stop()

iOS

import MapNativeCoreUI
import RusticMapsSDK

let positionController = PositionController()
let deviceLocationSource = DeviceLocationSource(
    positionController: positionController,
    onFix: { fix in
        mapView.setLocationIndicator(
            state: LocationIndicatorState(
                coordinate: fix.coordinate,
                courseHeadingDegrees: positionController.smoothedCourseDegrees(),
                horizontalAccuracyMeters: fix.horizontalAccuracyMeters
            ),
            style: LocationIndicatorStyle(
                visualKind: .trackingDot,
                radiusPixels: nil,
                rgbaColor: nil,
                showAccuracyRing: true
            )
        )
    }
)
// The Info.plist declares NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription.
deviceLocationSource.requestWhenInUseAuthorization()
deviceLocationSource.start()
// Later:
deviceLocationSource.stop()

React Native

import { MapsSdk } from '@angoratek/rustic-maps-sdk';

const sdk = await MapsSdk.create();
const started = await sdk.startDeviceLocation();
if (started) {
  const fix = await sdk.latestDeviceFix();
  const smoothedCourse = await sdk.deviceLocationSmoothedCourseDegrees();
  // Present fix and smoothedCourse through the <MapView> handle's
  // setLocationIndicator and setCamera calls.
}
// The failure name, when the source could not start:
const sourceStatus = await sdk.deviceLocationSourceStatus();
await sdk.stopDeviceLocation();

Ask for the Android runtime permission with PermissionsAndroid before startDeviceLocation; the iOS authorization prompt is raised by the source.

WebAssembly

import { PositionController } from './pkg/map_web_bindings.js';

const positionController = new PositionController();
const watchIdentifier = navigator.geolocation.watchPosition(
  position => {
    positionController.feedFix(
      position.coords.latitude,
      position.coords.longitude,
      position.coords.accuracy,
    );
    // Draw the tracking dot with the controller's smoothed course and centre
    // the camera through MapView.setLocationIndicator and setCamera.
  },
  error => {
    positionController.sourceFailed(
      error.code === 1 ? 'permissionDenied' : 'unavailable',
    );
  },
);
// Later:
navigator.geolocation.clearWatch(watchIdentifier);

Rust

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use map_navigation::SimulatedTripPace;
use map_positioning::{PositionController, SimulatedPositionSource};

let source = SimulatedPositionSource::new(&route, pace, 5.0)?;
let mut controller = PositionController::new();
controller.feed_fix(source.fix_at_elapsed_seconds(0.0))?;
}

A Rust application supplies fixes from its own OS source (or the simulated source above) and reads latest_fix, smoothed_course_heading_degrees and is_stale. See Use the SDK from Rust.

Provider capabilities in Rust

The Rust crates are the SDK’s implementation layer. A provider is a struct that implements one or more of the vendor-neutral traits in geospatial-traits; the core resolves it through map_core::ProviderRegistry. The four application targets bind this same core through the contract.

The repository publishes the Rust API reference, but it does not publish a Rust application package or a public Rust MapsSdk/MapView object. The downloadable artifacts are the Android, iOS, React Native, and WebAssembly targets. If you build inside the repository, the traits, registry, provider crates, renderer, navigation reducer, and offline archive APIs are available directly.

What you need

  • Rust 1.87 or newer, with the repository’s Cargo workspace.
  • A provider credential only for the live provider APIs, read at runtime and never stored in the crate, a sample response, or a log.

Providers available in Rust

ProviderKeyCredentialForm in RustServes
MapQuestmapquestAPI keymapquest-provider implementationsGeocoding (forward and reverse), search and suggestions, routing, distance matrix, traffic incidents and flow, raster tiles
OpenStreetMap StandardopenstreetmapNoneUrlTemplateRasterTileProvider with the registry templateRaster tiles
OpenStreetMap USosmusNoneOpenStreetMapUsVectorTileProviderVector tiles with Carto Light and Carto Dark
OpenFreeMapopenfreemapNoneUrlTemplateVectorTileProvider with the registry templateVector tiles with Bright, Fiord, and Positron
ProviderAttribution lineTerms
MapQuestMap data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL) — tile imagery © MapQuestMapQuest terms apply: rate limits and a 30-day raster-tile caching ceiling.
OpenStreetMap StandardMap data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL) — raster tiles © OpenStreetMap contributorsOpenStreetMap tile usage policy applies: low-volume use only, with attribution.
OpenStreetMap USMap data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL) — vector tiles © OpenStreetMap USOpenStreetMap US tileservice terms apply: free for low-volume, non-commercial use with attribution.
OpenFreeMapMap data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL) — vector tiles © OpenFreeMap and OpenMapTilesOpenFreeMap terms apply: free public use with attribution; bulk downloads are limited to 3,000 tiles or 50 MB per download.

Each vector style also carries its own attribution line. The style ids are carto-light and carto-dark (OpenStreetMap US), and bright-light, fiord-dark, and positron-light (OpenFreeMap). The vector source’s status readback reports the active style’s line.

Whether a provider is reachable from a shipped target depends on that target’s dispatch table. The browser target registers MapQuest; the vector base reaches every target through the generic URL-template vector provider.

Implement a contract

A provider implements the trait for the contract it serves. The trait methods are async and return SDKError when the provider refuses or fails.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use async_trait::async_trait;
use geospatial_traits::RoutingProvider;
use geospatial_types::route::{RouteData, RouteOptions};
use geospatial_types::{GeographicCoordinate, SDKError};

struct MyRoutingProvider;

#[async_trait]
impl RoutingProvider for MyRoutingProvider {
    async fn calculate_route(
        &self,
        waypoints: &[GeographicCoordinate],
        route_options: &RouteOptions,
    ) -> Result<RouteData, SDKError> {
        let _ = (waypoints, route_options);
        // Build the provider request, execute it through the transport, and
        // parse the answer into RouteData.
        todo!("implement the provider request and parse")
    }
}
}

Register the provider

ProviderRegistry holds one optional slot per contract. Registering replaces that slot; require_* answers ProviderNotConfigured with the contract name when a slot is empty.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use std::sync::Arc;
use geospatial_traits::RoutingProvider;
use map_core::ProviderRegistry;

fn registry_with(provider: Arc<dyn RoutingProvider>) -> ProviderRegistry {
    let mut registry = ProviderRegistry::new();
    registry.register_routing_provider(provider);
    registry
}
}

The shipped provider crates construct the same way. A URL-template raster source takes the registry’s template, zoom span, image format, resolution, and user agent, plus the shared transport.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use geospatial_types::{RasterImageFormat, RasterTileResolution, SDKError};
use provider_transport::default_transport;
use url_template_raster_provider::{
    UrlTemplateRasterTileProvider, UrlTemplateRasterTileSource,
};

fn open_street_map_raster_source() -> Result<UrlTemplateRasterTileProvider, SDKError> {
    let transport = default_transport()?;
    UrlTemplateRasterTileProvider::new(
        UrlTemplateRasterTileSource {
            url_template: "https://tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png".to_string(),
            source_name: "openstreetmap".to_string(),
            minimum_zoom_level: 0,
            maximum_zoom_level: 19,
            image_format: RasterImageFormat::Png,
            tile_resolution: RasterTileResolution::Standard,
            user_agent: "MyMapApp/1.0 (+https://example.com)".to_string(),
        },
        transport,
    )
}
}

Route without the network

The offline routing archive is the self-describing container compiled from an OpenStreetMap extract. The helper takes the archive bytes, so the same call serves every target.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use geospatial_types::{GeographicCoordinate, SDKError};
use map_core::calculate_offline_route_from_archive_bytes;

async fn route_over_archive(archive_bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), SDKError> {
    let start = GeographicCoordinate {
        latitude: 0.001,
        longitude: 0.0,
    };
    let end = GeographicCoordinate {
        latitude: 0.001,
        longitude: 0.002,
    };
    let route =
        calculate_offline_route_from_archive_bytes(archive_bytes, &start, &end).await?;
    let _ = route.distance_meters;
    Ok(())
}
}

The request uses the archive profile’s default options: automobile, fastest, metric. A corrupt archive returns OfflineRoutingFailure; a coordinate outside the graph’s snap tolerance or a pair the graph cannot connect is refused, never guessed.

What you should see

After registering a provider, require_* answers the implementation and the contract calls run through it. An empty slot returns ProviderNotConfigured with the contract name. The offline helper returns a RouteData on a connected pair, and a typed SDKError on a corrupt archive or an unconnectable pair.

Constraints

  • A provider crate implements one or more of the traits and returns the contract’s error types. It owns its vendor URL, credential handling, status mapping, attribution, and terms.
  • Provider types must be Send + Sync; trait methods are async.
  • Use provider-transport for HTTP so the native and browser builds share one request, retry, and rate-limit path.
  • A new provider crate becomes reachable from a shipped target through that target’s dispatch table and a registry descriptor. A contract with no registration call on the FFI surface needs an addition-only contract change before a native or browser application can select it.
  • Tests never reach the network. Provider responses in tests come from committed sample data served under the provider’s key.

Where to go next

  • Add a provider for the descriptor and dispatch work around a provider crate.
  • The FFI contract for the surface the application targets bind.
  • Offline maps for the archive and tile-cache story.

Switch the base map

A styled vector base

The registry’s keyless vector base for OpenFreeMap is Bright. Install it on the shipped view; every following frame draws the styled base beneath your overlays.

import uniffi.rustic_maps.UrlTemplateVectorTileSource

val openFreeMapBright = UrlTemplateVectorTileSource(
    urlTemplate = "https://tiles.openfreemap.org/planet/latest/{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf",
    sourceName = "openfreemap",
    attributionText = "Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL) · style Bright from OpenFreeMap styles, design CC BY 4.0",
    styleId = "bright-light",
    minimumZoomLevel = 0u,
    maximumZoomLevel = 14u,
)
if (mapView.setVectorTileSource(openFreeMapBright)) {
    val status = mapView.vectorTileSourceStatus()
}

While a vector base is installed, the raster layer is hidden so its imagery and labels cannot show through the style’s translucent fills. The status readback reports isConfigured, the style id, the source name, the attribution line, the zoom ceiling, and the last frame’s drawn and failed tile counts. A failed count above zero with a lastFailureDetail means the tileset refused some tiles; the base stays installed and the next frame retries.

Return to the registered raster source with clearVectorTileSource().

mapView.clearVectorTileSource()

A URL-template raster base

Any web-mercator XYZ raster tileset with a {z}/{x}/{y} template serves without provider code. OpenStreetMap Standard is the registry’s keyless raster source.

import uniffi.rustic_maps.RasterImageFormat
import uniffi.rustic_maps.RasterTileResolution
import uniffi.rustic_maps.UrlTemplateRasterTileSource

mapSdk.registerUrlTemplateRasterTileSource(
    UrlTemplateRasterTileSource(
        urlTemplate = "https://tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png",
        sourceName = "openstreetmap",
        minimumZoomLevel = 0u,
        maximumZoomLevel = 19u,
        imageFormat = RasterImageFormat.PNG,
        tileResolution = RasterTileResolution.STANDARD,
        userAgent = "MyMapApp/1.0 (+https://example.com)",
    ),
)
mapView.reloadRasterTileSource()

The registration replaces the raster-tile slot only; geocoding, routing, search, and traffic keep serving. It drops an installed tile cache, because the cache terms belong to the provider that installed it. MapView resolves its raster provider when it attaches and keeps tiles by coordinate, so call reloadRasterTileSource() after the registration to make the new source serve the next frame.

Register a provider

MapQuest registers from one runtime credential. The contract call installs the shipped provider set with the SDK’s rate-limit and retry defaults.

import uniffi.rustic_maps.MapSdk

val mapSdk = MapSdk()
mapSdk.setProviderCredential(providerApiKey)

A refused key throws SdkException with the provider’s verbatim detail. Apply the credential through your settings surface or a launch-time automation seam; never compile it into the app.

To keep registration generic over provider keys, the shipped facade dispatches the key to the matching SDK call. The facade’s nativeSdk is the one object the map view and every provider call use.

import com.angoratek.rusticmaps.MapsSdkFacade

val facade = MapsSdkFacade()
facade.applyProviderCredential("mapquest", providerApiKey)
val mapSdk = facade.nativeSdk

A provider key with no dispatch arm is refused by name rather than pretending to work. Adding an arm is covered in Add a provider.

What you should see

After the vector install, vectorTileSourceStatus() reports isConfigured = true, the bright-light style id, and the OpenFreeMap source name. After the raster registration and the view reload, the next frame draws the OpenStreetMap tiles. After a credential registration, search, routing, and traffic answer; without one, those calls throw SdkException with ProviderNotConfigured while the keyless base still draws.

Constraints

  • setProviderCredential installs the shipped provider set; the provider key in the facade selects the registration arm, not a provider inside the SDK.
  • Only geocoding and raster tiles have host-implemented interfaces. Routing, search, distance matrix, traffic, elevation, vector tiles, and offline routing need a Rust provider crate.
  • Re-registration replaces every slot on the MapSdk object. A second MapSdk needs its own registration.
  • Tests never reach the network. Provider responses in tests come from committed sample data served under the provider’s key.

Where to go next

  • Add a provider for the two implementation routes.
  • Search and routing for the provider calls in a complete flow.
  • Offline maps for the tile cache and archive routing.

Switch the base map

A styled vector base

The registry’s keyless vector base for OpenFreeMap is Bright. Install it on the component’s handle; every following frame draws the styled base beneath your overlays.

const accepted = await mapView.setVectorTileSource({
  urlTemplate: 'https://tiles.openfreemap.org/planet/latest/{z}/{x}/{y}.pbf',
  sourceName: 'openfreemap',
  attributionText:
    'Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL) · style Bright from OpenFreeMap styles, design CC BY 4.0',
  styleId: 'bright-light',
  minimumZoomLevel: 0,
  maximumZoomLevel: 14,
});
const status = await mapView.getVectorTileSourceStatus();

While a vector base is installed, the raster layer is hidden so its imagery and labels cannot show through the style’s translucent fills. The status readback reports whether a source is configured, the style id, the source name, the attribution line, the zoom ceiling, and the last frame’s drawn and failed tile counts. A failed count above zero with a lastFailureDetail means the tileset refused some tiles; the base stays installed and the next frame retries.

Return to the registered raster source with clearVectorTileSource().

await mapView.clearVectorTileSource();

A URL-template raster base

Any web-mercator XYZ raster tileset with a {z}/{x}/{y} template serves without provider code. OpenStreetMap Standard is the registry’s keyless raster source.

const registration = await mapSdk.registerUrlTemplateRasterTileSource({
  urlTemplate: 'https://tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png',
  sourceName: 'openstreetmap',
  minimumZoomLevel: 0,
  maximumZoomLevel: 19,
  imageFormat: 0,
  tileResolution: 0,
  userAgent: 'MyMapApp/1.0 (+https://example.com)',
});
if (!registration.isApplied) {
  throw new Error(registration.detailText);
}
mapView.reloadRasterTileSource();

The imageFormat and tileResolution values are the generated enum ordinals: imageFormat: 0 is PNG and tileResolution: 0 is standard resolution. The registration replaces the raster-tile slot only; geocoding, routing, search, and traffic keep serving. It drops an installed tile cache, because the cache terms belong to the provider that installed it. The component resolves its raster provider when it attaches, so call reloadRasterTileSource() after the registration to make the new source serve the next frame.

Register a provider

The package owns one native SDK per process. Create it with MapsSdk.create() and register the provider’s credential.

import { MapsSdk } from '@angoratek/rustic-maps-sdk/MapsSdk';

const mapSdk = await MapsSdk.create();
const registration = await mapSdk.setProviderCredential(
  'mapquest',
  providerApiKey,
);
if (!registration.isApplied) {
  throw new Error(registration.detailText);
}

A refused credential resolves with isApplied: false and the provider’s verbatim detailText. Apply the credential through your settings sheet or a launch-time automation seam; never compile it into the bundle.

The provider key is part of the package handle’s call. The native controller dispatches it to the matching SDK registration, so a key with no dispatch arm is refused instead of pretending to work. Adding an arm is covered in Add a provider.

What you should see

After the vector install, getVectorTileSourceStatus() reports a configured source with the bright-light style id and the OpenFreeMap source name. After the raster registration and the view reload, the next frame draws the OpenStreetMap tiles. After a credential registration, search, routing, and traffic answer; without one, those promises reject with the typed ProviderNotConfigured failure while the keyless base still draws.

Constraints

  • Keep the package handle. Constructing the generated root’s MapsSdk creates a second native SDK with its own provider registry and tile cache.
  • The package handle does not expose host-implemented providers. Geocoding and raster tiles can be implemented in Kotlin or Swift on the native platforms; on React Native, use a compiled provider crate or a URL-template source.
  • Re-registration replaces every slot on the native SDK object.
  • Tests never reach the network. Provider responses in tests come from committed sample data served under the provider’s key.

Where to go next

  • Add a provider for the two implementation routes.
  • Search and routing for the provider calls in a complete flow.

const status = mapView.vectorTileSourceStatus();

While a vector source is installed, the canvas hides the raster layer and paints the style’s own background. The status readback reports whether a source is configured, the style id, the source name, the attribution line, the zoom ceiling, and the last frame’s drawn and failed tile counts. A failed count above zero with a lastFailureDetail means the tileset refused some tiles; the base stays installed and the next frame retries.

The install is refused while a frame is resolving. Call it outside renderFrame, or retry after the frame settles. Return to the raster layer with clearVectorTileSource().

mapView.clearVectorTileSource();

The raster fallback

The canvas draws its same-origin recorded tiles first. A registry raster template supplies a live fallback for addresses those tiles do not cover; a registered live provider is consulted before the template.

mapView.setRasterTileSource(
  'https://tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png',
  19,
);

The template must carry {z}, {x}, and {y}; the maximum zoom level must be between 1 and 24. A blank template clears the fallback.

Register a provider

Provider registration is a free call whose first argument is the provider key from the shared registry. The credential lives in module memory only; it is never persisted or logged.

import init, { MapsSdk, registerProvider } from './web/map_web_bindings.js';

await init();
const mapSdk = await MapsSdk.create();
registerProvider('mapquest', providerCredential);

registerProvider dispatches the key to a provider implementation compiled into the WebAssembly module. A key with no compiled provider is refused with a message naming the key. clearProvider() removes the registration; the page then answers from recorded data and the raster fallback.

A refused credential or a key with no dispatch arm throws with the verbatim detail. Apply the credential through a settings form or a test’s runtime environment; never compile it into the bundle.

What you should see

After the vector install, vectorTileSourceStatus() reports a configured source with the bright-light style id and the OpenFreeMap source name. After registerProvider, the live calls resolve; before it, they reject with the registration refusal. The canvas keeps drawing the keyless base and its recorded tiles in either case.

Constraints

  • The module must be initialized and MapsSdk.create() resolved before a MapView is constructed.
  • The browser surface has no reverse geocoding, no tile cache, and no host-implemented provider registration. A provider that needs those contracts is a compiled provider crate, covered in Add a provider.
  • MapView.setVectorTileSource refuses while a frame is resolving; retry after the frame settles.
  • Tests never reach the network. Recorded tiles and provider responses are served from the page’s own origin.

Where to go next

  • Add a provider for the two implementation routes.
  • Search and routing for the provider calls in a complete flow.
  • Offline maps for archive routing in the browser.

Add a provider

A provider is a set of implementations of the vendor-neutral contracts plus one descriptor in the shared provider registry. The descriptor carries the labels, availability, attribution, and tile sources; the implementations carry the vendor’s requests and status mapping. No credential is ever part of either.

There are two implementation routes and one no-code route:

RouteUse it whenWhat changes
Rust provider crateThe provider serves routing, search, distance matrix, traffic, elevation, or vector tiles, or needs its own HTTP policyA crate implementing the traits, a descriptor, a dispatch arm, and a registration call on each target
Host implementationThe provider serves geocoding or raster tiles from code that already lives in the native appA Kotlin or Swift class implementing the interface, a registration call, and a descriptor
URL-template sourceThe provider publishes ordinary {z}/{x}/{y} raster or vector tilesA descriptor only; the SDK’s generic source does the work

What every provider needs

  1. Implementations. One struct or class per contract the provider serves.
  2. A descriptor. The shared registry entry that every application reads.
  3. A dispatch arm. The one place that maps the provider key to its registration call on a target.
  4. Committed sample responses. The tests and the demo read provider payloads from committed sample data, never from the network.

Route 1: a Rust provider crate

Implement the contract

Implement the matching trait from geospatial-traits. The methods are async and return SDKError on refusal or failure.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use async_trait::async_trait;
use geospatial_traits::RoutingProvider;
use geospatial_types::route::{RouteData, RouteOptions};
use geospatial_types::{GeographicCoordinate, SDKError};

struct MyRoutingProvider;

#[async_trait]
impl RoutingProvider for MyRoutingProvider {
    async fn calculate_route(
        &self,
        waypoints: &[GeographicCoordinate],
        route_options: &RouteOptions,
    ) -> Result<RouteData, SDKError> {
        let _ = (waypoints, route_options);
        // Build the provider request, execute it through the transport, and
        // parse the answer into RouteData.
        todo!("implement the provider request and parse")
    }
}
}

The traits are GeocodingProvider, RoutingProvider, DistanceMatrixProvider, SearchPlaceProvider, TrafficIncidentProvider, TrafficFlowProvider, ElevationProvider, RasterTileProvider, VectorTileProvider, and OfflineRoutingProvider. A provider implements only the ones it serves.

Register it in the core

ProviderRegistry holds one slot per contract. Registering replaces the slot; a call into an empty slot returns ProviderNotConfigured.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use std::sync::Arc;
use geospatial_traits::RoutingProvider;
use map_core::ProviderRegistry;

fn registry_with(provider: Arc<dyn RoutingProvider>) -> ProviderRegistry {
    let mut registry = ProviderRegistry::new();
    registry.register_routing_provider(provider);
    registry
}
}

Use provider-transport for HTTP. It gives the native and browser builds one request, retry, and rate-limit path, so a provider behaves the same on every target.

Expose it to an application target

  1. Add the descriptor. One entry in the shared provider registry.
  2. Add the dispatch arm. In each native application’s credential applier and in the browser binding’s dispatch table, map the provider key to the crate’s registration call. The arm is the only provider-named code.
  3. Add a registration call when the contract has none. Compiling the crate into a binding does not make it selectable. Geocoding and raster tiles already have host-implementable interfaces; the raster and vector base maps already have URL-template calls. Routing, search, distance matrix, traffic, elevation, and vector-tile providers need an addition-only method on the FFI contract, with the Kotlin, Swift, and React Native bindings regenerated from it.
  4. Add committed sample responses. Each served API gets a route pattern and a committed response under the provider’s key. The test server and the demo use them; tests never reach the network.

Constraints

  • A provider type is Send + Sync; trait methods are async.
  • The crate owns its vendor URL, credential handling, status mapping, and error detail. It does not name another vendor.
  • Map transport failures to NetworkRequestFailed, unparseable payloads to ResponseParsingFailure, documented application refusals to ProviderRequestRejected, and an exhausted limiter to RateLimitExhausted. Keep the provider’s detail text verbatim.
  • A vector source’s source_name is its cache namespace. Two tilesets must never share one name.
  • The provider name appears only in its crate, its sample-data directory, the shared descriptor, and the dispatch arms; the provider-name guard enforces that boundary.

Route 2: a host implementation

Android and iOS can implement two contracts directly in application code: GeocodingProvider and RasterTileProvider. Register the implementation on the MapSdk object that the map view and every provider call use.

Geocoding in Kotlin

import uniffi.rustic_maps.GeocodingProvider
import uniffi.rustic_maps.GeographicCoordinate
import uniffi.rustic_maps.MapSdk
import uniffi.rustic_maps.Place

class AppGeocodingProvider : GeocodingProvider {
    override suspend fun forwardGeocode(addressText: String): List<Place> {
        return emptyList()
    }

    override suspend fun reverseGeocode(
        coordinate: GeographicCoordinate,
    ): List<Place> {
        return emptyList()
    }
}

val mapSdk = MapSdk()
mapSdk.registerGeocodingProviderFromForeign(AppGeocodingProvider())

Geocoding in Swift

import RusticMapsSDK

final class AppGeocodingProvider: GeocodingProvider {
    func forwardGeocode(addressText: String) async throws -> [Place] {
        return []
    }

    func reverseGeocode(coordinate: GeographicCoordinate) async throws -> [Place] {
        return []
    }
}

let mapSdk = MapSdk()
try mapSdk.registerGeocodingProviderFromForeign(
    geocodingProvider: AppGeocodingProvider()
)

Raster tiles in Kotlin

import uniffi.rustic_maps.MapSdk
import uniffi.rustic_maps.RasterImageFormat
import uniffi.rustic_maps.RasterTileData
import uniffi.rustic_maps.RasterTileProvider
import uniffi.rustic_maps.RasterTileResolution

class AppRasterTileProvider : RasterTileProvider {
    override suspend fun fetchRasterTile(
        tileX: UInt,
        tileY: UInt,
        zoomLevel: UByte,
        imageFormat: RasterImageFormat,
        tileResolution: RasterTileResolution,
    ): RasterTileData {
        TODO("fetch the encoded tile from your service")
    }
}

val mapSdk = MapSdk()
mapSdk.registerRasterTileProviderFromForeign(AppRasterTileProvider())

Raster tiles in Swift

import RusticMapsSDK

final class AppRasterTileProvider: RasterTileProvider {
    func fetchRasterTile(
        tileX: UInt32,
        tileY: UInt32,
        zoomLevel: UInt8,
        imageFormat: RasterImageFormat,
        tileResolution: RasterTileResolution
    ) async throws -> RasterTileData {
        fatalError("fetch the encoded tile from your service")
    }
}

let mapSdk = MapSdk()
try mapSdk.registerRasterTileProviderFromForeign(
    rasterTileProvider: AppRasterTileProvider()
)

Constraints

  • Only geocoding and raster tiles have host-implementable interfaces. Every other contract needs a Rust provider crate.
  • The implementation runs on the foreign runtime and calls back into the SDK. Do not block; hand long work to your own queue or coroutine scope.
  • A failure must be one of the contract’s SdkError variants. An unclassified failure still reaches the typed refusal at the call, and the SDK records it for latestProviderFailureDiagnostics().
  • Registration is per MapSdk object and replaces that slot. The other slots keep serving. There is no unregister call; a restart returns the registry to its empty state.
  • The package handle on React Native does not expose these interfaces, and the browser has no host-provided provider path. Use a Rust provider crate there.
  • The provider’s attribution and terms still belong in the descriptor, not in the class.

Route 3: a URL-template source

A plain XYZ tileset needs no provider code. Add a descriptor with the tileset’s template, zoom span, and terms, then register the source once at startup.

PlatformRaster sourceStyled vector base
AndroidMapSdk.registerUrlTemplateRasterTileSource(source)MapView.setVectorTileSource(source)
iOSMapSdk.registerUrlTemplateRasterTileSource(source:)MapView.setVectorTileSource(_:)
React NativeMapsSdk.registerUrlTemplateRasterTileSource(source)MapViewHandle.setVectorTileSource(source)
WebAssemblyMapView.setRasterTileSource(template, maximumZoomLevel) as the live fallbackMapView.setVectorTileSource(source)
RustUrlTemplateRasterTileProvider::new(source, transport)UrlTemplateVectorTileProvider::new(template, descriptor, transport)

A raster source declares its image format, pixel resolution, and the User-Agent its requests carry. A vector source declares the committed style id it paints with. Templates must be absolute http or https URLs carrying {z}, {x}, and {y} and no other placeholders; the zoom span must not be inverted; the style id must name a committed style. A refused source keeps the previously serving base.

The descriptor

One descriptor per provider lives in the shared registry. Every application, the test server, and the demo read it by name; none of them hardcode a provider.

FieldMeaning
provider_keyStable key used by every dispatch arm and every provider-keyed route
display_nameName the settings surface shows
credential_labelLabel for the credential field; blank for a keyless provider
registration_availableWhether each target registers the provider: android, ios, react_native, wasm
attribution_textThe line every shell displays wherever the imagery appears
terms_noteThe provider’s rate limits, caching ceiling, or usage terms
settings_hintWhere the reader creates a credential
wasm_registrationThe browser dispatch key, or null when the browser has no registration
fixture_routesThe request patterns and committed sample responses for each served API
raster_url_templateThe keyless raster source, when the provider publishes one
maximum_zoom_levelThe highest zoom the tileset serves
url_templateThe vector tileset, when the provider publishes one
glyphs_url_templateThe glyph endpoint when the tileset publishes one
vector_styleThe tile schema the vector tileset carries
vector_stylesThe style id, display name, theme, and attribution of each offered style

A descriptor never carries a credential value.

What the reader sees

  • The settings surface renders one credential row per descriptor, with the provider’s display name, credential label, hint, attribution, and terms.
  • The base-map section renders the keyless raster sources and one row per vector style.
  • A keyless start is a first-class state: the app renders the recorded demo until a credential is applied, and a provider-dependent call returns ProviderNotConfigured verbatim.
  • Clearing a credential removes it from memory and the secure store, but the running SDK keeps its registered providers; tell the reader that a restart returns the session to the keyless state.

Verify the addition

  1. The descriptor renders on every target’s settings surface.
  2. The provider’s sample responses serve through its provider key; no test reaches the network.
  3. The provider-name guard passes: the name appears only in the provider’s crate, its sample-data directory, the descriptor, and the dispatch arms.
  4. The platform builds and the provider’s own tests pass on the exact tree you ship.

  • Android, iOS, React Native, WebAssembly, and Rust list the calls each target exposes.
  • Your first map shows the runtime credential path in a complete app.
  • Offline maps covers the tile cache and archive routing a provider-backed app can add.

Downloads

Every package is published under this site’s own versioned path, /downloads/vX.Y.Z/, and mirrored to an immutable release record: the version page lists the exact files, and a new version never rewrites an existing one. There is no Maven Central, npm registry or Swift Package Manager registry entry — the files served from this site are the artifacts you install.
