Module vector_style

Vector-tile styling: a decoded [map_vector_tiles::VectorTile] becomes the renderer’s overlay primitives — filled polygons for polygon features, polylines for line features, point markers for point features — under a small explicit style.

The style is deliberately data-only: a layer entry names the source layer, the geometry kind it paints, an optional one-attribute text filter and the paint values (RGBA, line width, marker radius). A symbol layer declares the label style a text pass will use — ordered text-field fallbacks, font stack, size stops, text and halo paint, [VectorSymbolPlacement], priority and overlap — but paints no overlay primitive itself: the frame-level label pass ([crate::labels]) reads it and draws its text through the glyph atlas, either anchored at a point or run along a line feature. The style carries no expression language. The artifact [DEFAULT_VECTOR_STYLE_ARTIFACT_JSON] carries the default style; [default_vector_tile_style] parses it and [in_code_default_vector_tile_style] is the documented fallback when the artifact is missing or malformed.

Polygon features paint every exterior ring with its interior rings subtracted through the overlay’s hole-aware fill (see [crate::overlay::FilledPolygonOverlay]), and the conversion groups its primitives into one [VectorOverlayBatch] per style layer, which a dedicated vector pipeline can consume.

Coordinates convert from tile-local extent space (x right, y down, the MVT convention) through the tile’s web-mercator address to geographic degrees, so the overlays project exactly like every other map coordinate.

map_navigation

Turn-by-turn navigation for a planned route.

The crate is a pure event reducer: [reduce_navigation_event] maps [NavigationEvent]s onto a [NavigationSession] without touching the network, the clock or the GPU. Each location fix is judged for deviation ([deviation]), snapped onto the route geometry ([geometry]), and evaluated against a pluggable [StepAdvanceCondition]. When the driver leaves the route, the caller supplies a replacement route through [NavigationEvent::RerouteProvided] and the reducer swaps it in. [NavigationPhase] moves through Navigating, OffRoute and Arrived; OffRoute is a pause the driver can recover from by returning to the route.

Supporting modules compose the user-visible output:

  • [instruction] turns a trip state into plain-data banner and text-to-speech payloads. - [observer] delivers state changes to per-topic subscribers with explicit cancellation. - [reroute] applies a time-and-distance hysteresis before signalling that a recalculation is due. - [speech] decides when a spoken instruction is announced. - [course_filtering] turns a raw fix course into the trip’s reported course. - [recorder] optionally keeps a bounded log of fixes and state changes for diagnostics. - [route_walk] walks a route at a fixed pace for simulated trips.

The reducer is synchronous and deterministic: the same event history always produces the same session state. Time is supplied by the caller in the events, and nothing here spawns a thread or performs I/O.

Module course_filtering

Course filtering: how a position fix’s reported course becomes the trip’s reported course.

A coarse GNSS fix’s course over ground is often the least trustworthy field the fix carries — a momentary standstill or an urban canyon reads as an arbitrary bearing, while the trip’s own route line is a much stronger statement about the real direction of travel. The policy is chosen once per trip:

  • [CourseFiltering::Raw] reports the fix’s course verbatim — the tunnel or canyon exit hatch where a garbage route projection must not override a correct physical course. - [CourseFiltering::SnapToRoute] projects the course onto the route line: while the fix is not judged fully off route, the reported course is the bearing of the route line at the user’s snapped position — every materially disagreeing raw course is replaced in one step, and the course stops jittering against the very line the position was already snapped onto. Without a route line to trust (the fix did not snap, or the projected segment carries no direction), the fix’s own course remains the fallback, and an unreported course retains the trip’s previous course (the same degradation continuity the snapped position keeps).

The filtering is decided per trip, like the step-advance and deviation policies ([crate::reducer::NavigationEvent::StartTrip] carries it), and the reducer stamps every fix’s effective course into TripNavigationState::course_heading_degrees during the same position snap pass, so consumers (a course wedge, a follow camera) read one course field instead of re-filtering raw courses per platform.

None on either source means “not reported here”.

Module deviation

Deviation (off-route) detection, the second decision policy beside the [crate::step_advance] conditions.

A [DeviationDetector] is consulted by the reducer on every location update, with the measurements the reducer already computed. The live detector instance travels in NavigationSession beside the state, never inside the exported plain-data record.

Judgment semantics

The shipped detector is a pure per-fix predicate over the measured distance: a fix is off route when its distance to the remaining route line exceeds the configured threshold widened by the fix’s reported horizontal accuracy. Widening is deliberate: the accuracy radius is exactly the plausible gap between the raw fix and the truth, so a genuinely on-route position may legitimately read up to one accuracy radius away from the line. A widened allowance suppresses those false flags gracefully instead of failing abruptly at a hard gate. The measurement is taken against the remaining route line (the current step onward) rather than only the current step, so a lagging step — eager advance semantics, pauses at intersections — is never mistaken for a deviation.

Two grades

A fix beyond the allowance from the remaining route line is judged fully off route. A fix inside the remainder’s allowance but beyond the allowance from the current step’s own polyline projects onto a future step and is reported as [DeviationStatus::OffStepOnRoute] (“on route, wrong step”). A shortcut, a self-intersecting route, or a lagging step advance can all legitimately put a fix on a later step, so the wrong-step grade is guidance feedback: the reducer neither freezes on it nor asks for a reroute, and the step-advance condition (with a delayed condition, within the very fix that produced the grade, via the reducer’s multi-step advance loop) reconciles the step. Only [DeviationStatus::OffRoute] is the freezing grade.

Hysteresis

The shipped detector uses one threshold for both raising and clearing a deviation, so the flag can flicker around the allowance edge. Hysteresis (a wider clearance than detection, or a minimum off-route time) is not part of this detector.

The reducer’s contract with the detector, documented in [crate::reducer]: a fix without an accuracy report is never judged at all — it can neither raise nor clear a deviation.

Module geometry

Polyline snapping mathematics for route progress.

The navigation state machine repeatedly needs two measurements against the current step’s shape: the closest point on the polyline (the snapped position) and the distance from a raw position fix to the polyline (the same minimum the deviation detector consumes later). Both live here so the projection error is documented and tested in exactly one place.

Projection model

Each segment is projected into a local equirectangular plane around its own midpoint: a north/south offset of y meters becomes y / RADIUS radians of latitude and an east/west offset of x meters becomes x / (RADIUS * cos(reference_latitude)) radians of longitude. This is exact along the reference parallel and along meridians within the small-angle approximation; the residual grows with segment length and distance from the equator. For the road-scale segments a navigation step carries (well under 1 km) at inhabited latitudes the distortion is far below a meter, comfortably inside GNSS accuracy. The minimization over segments uses this planar space; the reported distance is then recomputed exactly with the haversine formula. Antimeridian-crossing shapes are not supported: longitudes are treated as a plain number line.

ItemKindSignaturePurpose

Returns None when the shape has no coordinates at all. A single-point shape snaps to that point. Projections are clipped to the segment (a position fix beyond a segment end snaps to the endpoint); see the module documentation for the projection model.

Module instruction

Runtime turn-by-turn instruction composition for an active trip.

[compose_navigation_instructions] is a pure function of the current [TripNavigationState] (whose route field supplies the provider-authored steps) plus a [UnitSystem]: it produces the plain-data [NavigationInstruction] payload a UI banner or a text-to-speech engine consumes. The record is deliberately serializable — no Arc, no trait objects — so it can cross a language boundary unchanged.

Provider text is never rewritten

The emitter performs no natural-language understanding and does not rephrase, summarize or spell-normalize the provider-authored instruction strings ([RouteStep::instruction_display_text] and [RouteStep::instruction_speech_text]). The only text it authors is the live distance prefix ("In 130 meters"), composed as "<prefix>, <provider text>". With no distance left the prefix disappears entirely and the payload is the provider text verbatim. Where the provider authored no text at all, the payload is the explicit [ManeuverInstructionText::Unavailable] state — nothing is invented to fill it. When only one of the two variants is empty, the other (still provider-authored) variant is reused for both channels rather than synthesizing text: choosing which authored string to speak is not authoring.

Off route: an explicit rerouting-required marker

While the phase is [NavigationPhase::OffRoute] the reducer freezes the whole projection, so the composed payload below the marker is the last on-route instruction, unchanged across successive deviating fixes. Rather than presenting that stale instruction as trustworthy guidance, the payload carries an explicit [NavigationInstruction::is_rerouting_required] marker; a UI uses it to swap the banner for a rerouting notice, and the marker clears as soon as the deviation lifts or a reroute replaces the route.

Off route: the frozen countdown is suppressed, not presented

A frozen projection has no trustworthy distance to the next maneuver: any countdown composed off it would read as live guidance measured from where the device is not. While the freezing (FullyOffRoute) grade holds, the active maneuver’s phrase is therefore the explicit [DistancePhrase::Suppressed] state — no magnitude is phrased and the distance prefix drops from both text channels — mirroring the [ManeuverInstructionText::Unavailable] posture of composing nothing rather than composing something false. The provider-authored text is carried verbatim beneath the rerouting-required marker exactly as before. A merely wrong-step grade (OffStepOnRoute) keeps counting down: its fix still projects onto the route line, so the measured distance is real.

Distance phrasing bands

[DistancePhrase] rounds the raw distance to a named, boundary-tested band so successive fixes phrase identically while a user walks the span (“In 130 meters” instead of “In 131 meters”, “In 127 meters”, …). The pinned bands, rounded half-up:

| Band | Metric | Imperial | |—|—|—| | Immediate | below 5 m (= half the near increment) | below 50 ft (= half the near increment) | | Near | below 100 m: nearest 10 m | below 1000 ft: nearest 100 ft | | Moderate | 100 m–1000 m: nearest 50 m | 1000 ft–1 mile: nearest 500 ft | | Far | 1 km and up: nearest 0.1 km | 1 mile and up: nearest 0.1 mile |

The immediate band exists because half-up rounding of a sub-increment distance would otherwise phrase a 4 m approach as “In 0 meters”.

Module location

ItemKindSignaturePurpose

Module observer

Per-topic observers over the navigation state machine.

The module registers listeners per topic behind one [NavigationStateChangeListener] trait, each subscription with an explicit [TopicSubscription::cancel], so a consumer subscribes to only what it needs and each subscription cancels exactly itself:

  • instructions (dispatch_* always): the composed [NavigationInstruction] payload of every dispatched state change, produced by [crate::instruction::compose_navigation_instructions]; - deviation status (on change): [DeviationStatusChange] as the detector’s judgment enters, deepens/updates or clears — the per-fix judgment stream, including measurement drift while the phase stays OffRoute; - phase (on transition): [NavigationPhaseChange] — one-shot transitions OffRoute entered/cleared, RerouteProvided applied, and Arrived.

Threading contract

Dispatch is synchronous and single-threaded by contract: callbacks run on the caller’s thread, in the dispatch’s own stack frame. A host that needs callbacks on another thread performs that hop itself. Cross-thread calls are data-race-free (the trait requires [Send] + [Sync]) and are at worst suppressed by the re-entrancy guard, but the ordering guarantee is stated for single-threaded use only.

Dispatch rules

  • No lock is held across listener callbacks. The registry lock is taken once to snapshot the (cheaply cloned) listener lists and released before the first callback runs, so a listener may freely call back into the broadcaster — including [TopicSubscription::cancel] — without deadlocking. - Delivery order: within a topic, strict registration order; across topics, instructions first, then deviation status, then phase. - One dispatch in flight. The deliberate re-entrancy bound: a dispatch that starts while another dispatch is still in flight — typically a listener driving the reducer and re-dispatching from its own callback — delivers nothing and reports [NavigationDispatchOutcome::SuppressedReentrant]. Nothing is queued (no unbounded growth, no re-entrant cascade): the state change behind a suppressed dispatch is never lost — it already happened in the reducer — but its broadcast is skipped, so a listener that re-dispatches must let the outer dispatch finish and dispatch again from the top level. The common listener shapes (recording, platform notification) are fully synchronous and unaffected. - Listener errors cannot poison the reducer. Listener methods return nothing, so there is no error channel by construction; the dispatch runs after the reducer has already produced its new state and only reads the state it is handed. A listener that panics propagates the panic to the dispatch caller and cannot corrupt the trip state or wedge the broadcaster: the in-flight guard releases on unwind. A host that must contain listener panics catches them at its callback boundary. - Snapshot semantics for cancel: a subscription cancelled during a dispatch may still receive that dispatch’s callbacks (the snapshot was taken before); cancellation is guaranteed for every dispatch started after cancel returns.

The methods have default no-op bodies: implementing only the topics a consumer needs is trivial. Registered subscriptions select which method a dispatch may call — subscribing to instructions delivers only [Self::on_navigation_instruction] to that subscription, and so on. Module recorder

Opt-in navigation recording for field diagnostics and debugging.

A [NavigationRecorder] implements the per-topic [NavigationStateChangeListener] surface and additionally records the raw position fixes delivered to the reducer through an explicit [NavigationRecorder::record_location_fix] channel (the raw fixes are not a listener topic — the listener surface starts downstream of them). Every recording is stamped with a strictly increasing sequence number and, when the clock is available, an instant in seconds since the Unix epoch, and is kept in a bounded ring that silently drops its oldest entry once full. A recorder therefore never grows unbounded and never slows the trip down beyond one short locked section per recorded item.

Recording is opt-in: nothing records unless a consumer holds a recorder and subscribes it or feeds it fixes. Recording stops when the recorder is dropped from every subscription.

The drained entries are the plain-data payload types the other navigation modules emit.

Provenance: a debugging buffer, sized so a representative trip’s whole state-change stream (one instruction payload per dispatched state, the deviation stream, phase transitions and the fix stream) stays intact while a single entry costs only its plain-data payload. Capacity is explicit at construction when a session needs a tighter or wider ring.

Module reducer

The pure event reducer driving an active trip.

[reduce_navigation_event] maps one event onto the previous session and returns the next one; it has no I/O, no clock and no mutable globals, so every outcome is reproducible from the event history. The live [StepAdvanceCondition] and [DeviationDetector] instances travel through [NavigationSession], pairing state with its decision objects because they are swapped for their [StepAdvanceCondition::fresh_instance] (or [DeviationDetector::fresh_instance]) counterparts at reset points, and the exported [crate::state::TripNavigationState] must stay free of trait objects.

Reducer semantics

  • [NavigationEvent::StartTrip] flattens the route and reports the declared step values as remaining progress until the first fix arrives. - [NavigationEvent::LocationUpdated] is judged for deviation first: a fix the detector grades fully off route freezes the session — the snapped coordinate and progress stay at the last on-route values, and neither the step-advance condition is consulted nor the step advances. Deviating positions must not drive route progress. A fix graded off the current step but on the route ([DeviationGrade::OffStepOnRoute], a projection onto a future step) never freezes on its own: the grade is recorded in the state, the trip stays Navigating — no reroute request, instructions keep counting down — and the fix is then processed normally (the step-advance condition reconciles the step; a delayed condition does so within the very fix, via the multi-step advance loop below). A fix without an accuracy report is not judged at all: it can neither raise nor clear a deviation, because one threshold rule cannot conservatively decide both directions. A graded fix inside the allowance lifts an active deviation (an OffRoute trip recovering from the route line, or a lingering wrong-step grade clearing) and the update then proceeds normally (condition consulted, position snapped, progress recomputed). [crate::state::NavigationPhase::OffRoute] is therefore a pause the user may recover from by returning to the route, not a terminal state. - Arrival-aware advance: the condition consulted for a hop is not always the trip’s own. Once the remaining steps — counted with the current step itself included — shrink to the arrival window ([ARRIVAL_CONDITION_REMAINING_STEPS_BOUND]), a separately configured arrival step-advance condition is consulted instead (falling back to the trip’s own condition when none was configured, which preserves the behavior of every trip that has none). Arrival itself is reachable only through that final-step verdict: an Advance while on the final step cannot pop another step — it declares [NavigationPhase::Arrived] and breaks the loop ahead of any further consult, so neither the loop’s defensive bound nor a still advancing condition can walk past the route’s end. - The trip’s course-filtering policy stamps an effective course ([TripNavigationState::course_heading_degrees]) during each processed fix’s position snap; see [crate::course_filtering]. - One fix may advance through several steps: after each single-hop advance — which swaps in the fresh condition instance — the freshly computed inputs decide whether the same fix advances the next hop too. The loop is bounded by [MAXIMUM_STEP_ADVANCES_PER_FIX] and terminates by construction: a hop can end the trip only by arriving, and every other break is the condition’s Remain. - [NavigationEvent::RerouteProvided] rebuilds the session for the same trip from a fresh route. Route computation policy lives at the caller’s event source; the reducer stays policy-free and pure. See the event documentation for the route-anchoring contract it implies. - Updates after the phase is Arrived are ignored; reroutes offered to an arrived trip are ignored as well.
ItemKindSignaturePurpose
MAXIMUM_STEP_ADVANCES_PER_FIXconstpub const MAXIMUM_STEP_ADVANCES_PER_FIX: usizeDefensive ceiling, in steps, on how many hops a single position fix may advance through in the multi-step advance loop. The loop’s real terminators are the advance condition itself (a Remain verdict ends the walk) and the trip’s arrival on the final step, so the bound is not what makes the loop safe — it exists to guarantee a bounded response even against a pathological condition that advances on every consult (any real fix is unboundedly faster than such a condition could run out of steps). It is set far above any legitimate fix-to-step skip: a single jump across a 1,000-step route stays well inside it.
ARRIVAL_CONDITION_REMAINING_STEPS_BOUNDconstpub const ARRIVAL_CONDITION_REMAINING_STEPS_BOUND: usizeHow few steps may remain — counted with the current step itself included — while the trip consults its separately configured arrival step-advance condition instead of its ordinary one. The bound is 2, so the arrival condition governs the final step and the one before it: arrival decisions deserve their own (typically narrower, more eager or more pedestrian-calibrated) policy well before the maneuver point. A trip that declares no arrival condition runs its ordinary condition to the end (an explicit None in the StartTrip event).

The reducer is pure and synchronous: it performs no I/O, reads no clock and spawns no thread.

Module reroute

Reroute-recalculation hysteresis: the gates a reroute request must pass before it may begin.

A fully off-route excursion asks the integrator for a replacement route, but the request itself is an expensive asynchronous calculation that must not be spammed by jittery fixes. Three hysteresis gates stand between the signal and the request, plus their observable in-flight readback:

  • Request-in-flight gate. While one recalculation is still in flight, a new one is refused; the integrator settles the request (applies or abandons it) before the gates open again. - Cooldown. A new calculation waits out [ReroutePolicy::recalculation_cooldown_seconds] of wall clock since the last one began (a fix jittering in and out of the route within the cooldown window cannot fire repeated requests). - Movement threshold. A new calculation also waits until the raw position has moved at least [ReroutePolicy::recalculation_movement_meters] from the fix current at the last calculation’s beginning (Raw fixes, not the snapped position: a fully off-route trip freezes its snap, so a movement gate read off the snap could never be satisfied while it is most needed).

The gate is stateful and wall-clock driven, deliberately outside the reducer: the navigation reducer stays a pure, clock-free event function, and the controller holds the gate beside the session and evaluates it with the fix instant, as it does for [crate::speech::SpeechInstructionPlanner]. The caller supplies now to [RerouteRecalculationGate::begin_calculation], which also makes the gates deterministic in tests.

Module route_walk

Distance-parameterised traversal of a planned route’s own geometry.

A simulated trip must follow the polyline the visitor actually planned, not a fixed demo line. [RouteWalk] flattens a [RouteData]’s legs → steps → shapes into one traversal-order polyline, collapses duplicate and zero-length segments, accumulates great-circle distances, and answers a fix either at a travelled distance or at an elapsed time. Because the SDK carries no pacing policy, the caller supplies a [SimulatedTripPace].

Traversal model

  • Distances between consecutive kept vertices are great-circle haversine distances (the same mathematics as GeographicCoordinate). - Vertices closer than [MINIMUM_SEGMENT_LENGTH_METERS] to their predecessor are collapsed, so duplicated step boundaries and repeated shape points contribute no segment and no undefined bearing. - A position between two vertices is a linear interpolation in latitude and in antimeridian-unwrapped longitude. This matches how the route polyline is drawn; over road-scale segments the difference from a great-circle arc is far below a meter. - Segment bearings are the direction of travel along the active segment, in degrees clockwise from true north (0 = north, 90 = east). At an exact interior vertex the outgoing segment’s bearing wins; the final vertex reports the last segment’s bearing. - Longitudes are unwrapped across the antimeridian before interpolation and bearings are computed, then the resulting coordinate is wrapped back into [-180, 180] the way the rest of the SDK normalizes world longitudes. A route from 179.9° to −179.9° therefore traverses 0.2° eastward rather than 359.8° westward.

Both fix functions clamp their argument into the route’s parameter range instead of failing: a negative or NaN distance/time is the trip start, anything past the end is the final fix. [SimulatedTripFix::is_arrived] is then true exactly when the fix sits at the route’s final coordinate.

ItemKindSignaturePurpose
SimulatedTripPacestructpub struct SimulatedTripPacePace chosen by the caller for a simulated trip. The SDK deliberately carries no default pace: every application picks its own numbers. The effective travel speed is [Self::speed_meters_per_second] × [Self::speed_multiplier]; both values must be finite and strictly positive, and their product must stay finite. [RouteWalk::new] enforces that.
SimulatedTripFixstructpub struct SimulatedTripFixOne position of a simulated trip along the planned route.
RouteWalkErrorenumpub enum RouteWalkErrorWhy a [RouteWalk] could not be built.
RouteWalkstructpub struct RouteWalkAn immutable distance-parameterised walk over one planned route. Construct it once per trip with [RouteWalk::new]; every fix is then a cheap read. The walk owns the flattened, deduplicated polyline and the cumulative distances, so a fix never re-flattens the route.

Module speech

Speech-instruction triggering: when a guidance line is newsworthy enough to speak.

The SDK stays out of synthesis and playback: this module only decides when a fix is worth a spoken line, and answers with the composed instruction payload’s verbatim speech text, never text this module authored. The decision reuses the display phrase’s existing distance bands, so a spoken “in 100 meters” can never disagree with the banner’s shown phrase: the thresholds below are the very bands [crate::instruction::DistancePhrase] rounds with.

Emission rules (the named behaviors)

  • Trigger bands are the distance-phrase bands. Fix N crossed below a band’s threshold (in meters) announces that band: metric 10 m, 100 m, 1 km and the immediate half-increment threshold; imperial 100 ft, 1 000 ft, 1 mile and the immediate threshold. Each band announces at most once per step, and only the strictest band crossed in one fix speaks: a fix that jumps two bands announces the nearer stage only. - Monotone per step. The band memory resets only on a step advance, so distance jitter over a threshold can never re-announce a band. - Minimum inter-utterance spacing. After any line, the next band-triggered line waits for [MINIMUM_INTER_UTTERANCE_SPACING_SECONDS]. The immediate band overrides it: a “turn now” stage always plays. - Minimum repeat distance. A ManeuverApproach line whose trigger distance lies within [MINIMUM_UTTERANCE_REPEAT_DISTANCE_METERS] of the previous emission’s trigger distance is suppressed: two turns announced from distances closer than this read as chatter instead of guidance. The planner does not chain “then”; the near band’s own silence is the honest fallback. - Transitions always speak. An off-route recovery and an arrival emit unconditionally (the composed payload’s verbatim text) — they are the guidance-resumed and you-have-arrived lines, not pacing candidates, and like every emission they refresh the spacing memory. - Every emission carries its identity. Each emitted [SpeechUtterance] is stamped with a fresh, strictly increasing [SpeechUtterance::utterance_id] at the single emission site, and the counter survives every reset — so identical text re-emitted is a new identity, and the platform speaker’s dedup and flush decisions stay keyed on its own queue state.
ItemKindSignaturePurpose
MINIMUM_INTER_UTTERANCE_SPACING_SECONDSconstpub const MINIMUM_INTER_UTTERANCE_SPACING_SECONDS: f64Minimum wall-clock spacing between two emitted utterances, in seconds. An engine cannot pipeline lines closer than this without overlapping its own audio; about 2 seconds.
MINIMUM_UTTERANCE_REPEAT_DISTANCE_METERSconstpub const MINIMUM_UTTERANCE_REPEAT_DISTANCE_METERS: f64Minimum route-progress distance between two announced lines, in meters. Two turns whose announcements sit closer than this are either chained or announced as the nearer one only.

Module state

The plain-data navigation state record produced by the reducer.

TripNavigationState is the exported half of the navigation model: it holds only serializable data (indices, distances, a snapped coordinate), never the live StepAdvanceCondition or DeviationDetector instance. Both live beside the state in a NavigationSession, which keeps this record safe to expose through a language binding.

ItemKindSignaturePurpose
NavigationPhaseenumpub enum NavigationPhaseHigh-level phase of a trip that has already been started. Rerouting is not a phase of its own: a reroute is the caller’s answer (a RerouteProvided event) and the session is simply rebuilt for the new route, so the machine flows Navigating ⇄ OffRoute within a trip and Navigating → Arrived at its end.
DeviationGradeenumpub enum DeviationGradeWhich grade of deviation a recorded deviation carries. The two grades distinguish a fix that is off the current step yet still on the route line from a fix that is completely off the route. Only the fully-off grade freezes navigation; the wrong-step grade never freezes on its own (see [crate::reducer]).
DeviationInfostructpub struct DeviationInfoPlain-data description of an active deviation from the route. The record carries the deviation’s grade beside its measurement: a [DeviationGrade::OffStepOnRoute] reading is guidance feedback (“you are on the route, on a later step”) rather than a frozen off-route trip.
RouteStepPositionstructpub struct RouteStepPositionLocation of one route step in traversal order. A route is organized as legs of steps; navigation walks the steps of all legs in order, so the reducer flattens them up front while keeping both indices so an instruction can still be attributed to its leg.
TripProgressstructpub struct TripProgressProgress along the remaining trip.
TripNavigationStatestructpub struct TripNavigationStateThe full navigable state of an active trip. The reducer is the only writer; see [crate::reducer] for the event semantics. Steps are held as traversal-ordered indices into the route (never a duplicated step list) so the record stays small and the leg attribution survives.

Module step_advance

Step-advance conditions.

A [StepAdvanceCondition] is a pure decision object consulted by the reducer on every location update. Conditions are passed into the reducer as Arc<dyn StepAdvanceCondition> parameters and never live inside the exported [TripNavigationState], which must stay plain data for a language binding.

The fresh-instance contract

[StepAdvanceCondition::fresh_instance] returns the same configuration with any internal state reset. The reducer swaps the active condition for fresh_instance() the moment it advances. This prevents a rapid double advance: a condition that tracks progress within a step (for example, one awaiting several consecutive fixes) would otherwise carry saturated internal state across the advance and immediately advance again on the next update. Stateless conditions can simply return a clone of themselves, but the contract is uniform so composite conditions can reset every nested condition recursively.

Combinators

[OrStepAdvanceCondition] and [AndStepAdvanceCondition] wrap two inner conditions and decide on their combined verdicts. Both consult every inner condition on every update (even when the outcome is already decided for And): a stateful inner condition must observe every update for its internal schedule to stay sound. fresh_instance rebuilds both inner conditions fresh, so the reducer’s whole-composite reset on advance also resets each child.

ItemKindSignaturePurpose
DEFAULT_DISTANCE_TO_END_OF_STEP_THRESHOLD_METERSconstpub const DEFAULT_DISTANCE_TO_END_OF_STEP_THRESHOLD_METERS: f64Threshold, in meters from the end of the current step, below which DistanceToEndOfStepCondition advances. It is large enough to absorb GNSS noise near the maneuver and small enough not to swallow short steps.
DEFAULT_DISTANCE_FROM_STEP_THRESHOLD_METERSconstpub const DEFAULT_DISTANCE_FROM_STEP_THRESHOLD_METERS: f64Threshold, in meters from the current step’s polyline, beyond which DistanceFromStepCondition advances.
DEFAULT_MINIMUM_HORIZONTAL_ACCURACY_METERSconstpub const DEFAULT_MINIMUM_HORIZONTAL_ACCURACY_METERS: f64Fixes with a reported horizontal accuracy worse than this, in meters, may never trigger an advance in the distance conditions.
StepAdvanceDecisionenumpub enum StepAdvanceDecisionDecision the reducer acts on after consulting a condition. Distinct from a boolean only in name: it keeps the reducer’s match explicit and leaves room for later decision kinds without changing the trait signature.
StepAdvanceInputsstructpub struct StepAdvanceInputs<'a>Geometry and accuracy context the reducer computes once per update. Conditions receive precomputed measurements instead of route internals so they stay testable against synthetic inputs and the snapping error model (see [crate::geometry]) is owned by the reducer alone. Distances use the reported position fix (before snapping).
StepAdvanceConditiontraitpub trait StepAdvanceCondition: Send + SyncDecides when the reducer moves from the current step to the next one. Implementations must be [Send] and [Sync] because Arc’d conditions are shared with platform wrappers and worker threads.
ManualStepAdvanceConditionstructpub struct ManualStepAdvanceConditionNever advances by itself: step changes happen only when driven programmatically from outside the reducer. Useful for custom behavior where a host platform owns the advance decision.
DistanceToEndOfStepConditionstructpub struct DistanceToEndOfStepConditionAdvances when the position fix comes within a threshold of the end of the current step, eager-advance semantics. The advance happens as soon as the fix is close enough to the maneuver point, which makes the instruction switch punctual but sensitive to noisy fixes near the step end (hence the accuracy gate).
DistanceFromStepConditionstructpub struct DistanceFromStepConditionAdvances when the position fix moves far enough from the current step’s polyline, delayed-advance semantics. The advance fires only once the fix has left the step neighborhood entirely, which is robust to pausing at intersections and to self-intersecting steps — but less robust on very short steps whose start sits near the previous step’s end.
OrStepAdvanceConditionstructpub struct OrStepAdvanceConditionAdvances if either inner condition advances (OR). Ideal for short-circuit strategies: for example a large-distance guard reacting to the fix leaving the step neighborhood, combined with the routine advance behavior as the second condition.
AndStepAdvanceConditionstructpub struct AndStepAdvanceConditionAdvances only if both inner conditions advance (AND).

Android API reference

Generated from the SDK contract and the generated Android bindings. Do not edit this page by hand; change the contract and regenerate the documentation.

The Android artifact exposes the provider-neutral SDK through Kotlin bindings generated from the SDK contract, together with the shipped map view. This page documents every contract type and member the Kotlin surface exposes: what it does, how it is constructed, its parameters, its return value, the failures it raises, and its async and threading rules. The shipped com.angoratek.rusticmaps map view and its facade are described in the platform guides.

MapCamera

Anchored map camera: geographic center, zoom level, bearing and pitch. The ground point under the center always sits at the viewport center; zoom and pitch are clamped to their valid ranges and bearing wraps into [0, 360).

Construction

ConstructorSignaturePurpose
constructorconstructor(center: GeographicCoordinate, zoomLevel: Double, bearingDegrees: Double, pitchDegrees: Double)Builds a camera at the given center, zoom level, bearing and pitch. # Parameters - center — geographic point placed at the viewport center. - zoom_level — zoom level, clamped to the valid range. - bearing_degrees — clockwise rotation from north, wrapped into [0, 360). - pitch_degrees — tilt from straight down, clamped to the valid range. # Errors Throws InvalidCoordinateInput when the center is not a valid coordinate or when a numeric argument is not finite.
fitBoundsfun fitBounds(boundingBox: BoundingBox, viewport: ViewportSize, edgeInsets: EdgeInsets, maximumZoomLevel: Double): MapCameraBuilds the camera that frames a bounding box inside the viewport’s inset region: top-down and north-up by construction (pitch and bearing zero), zoomed to the largest level keeping the whole box inside the inset area and clamped to maximum_zoom_level; the center is anchored on the inset region’s center. # Parameters - bounding_box — the area to frame. - viewport — viewport extent in pixels. - edge_insets — pixels kept clear on each viewport edge. - maximum_zoom_level — upper zoom bound for the fitted camera. # Errors Throws when the insets or the maximum zoom are not finite usable values, when the insets are negative or leave no inset area, or when the box spans no positive world area.

MapSdk

Provider entry point of the SDK: resolves every call through the providers registered on the object. Construct the object with no providers, then register them: native integrations through the SDK’s own registration calls and foreign integrations through the register_*_from_foreign methods (see the provider contract interfaces above). A call into a contract with no registered provider throws ProviderNotConfigured naming the contract.

The calls cover geocoding (forward and reverse), routing, distance matrix, place search, traffic incidents, traffic flow and raster tiles. Elevation and offline routing have no provider contract here: offline routing is the standalone offline_route_from_archive_bytes function.

Returns RasterTileData. setProviderCredentialfun setProviderCredential(credential: String): UnitThrows SdkException.Registers the built-in MapQuest provider set from one consumer key, with the SDK defaults for base URL, rate limiting and retries. The call installs geocoding, routing, distance matrix, place search, traffic incidents, traffic flow and raster tiles, so one call and one key enable the whole provider set. Re-registration replaces every provider. Elevation has no provider and keeps throwing ProviderNotConfigured. # Parameters - credential — the provider consumer key. # Errors Throws SdkError when the credential is empty or the registration is refused.
setProviderCredentialWithTileCachefun setProviderCredentialWithTileCache(mapquestApiKey: String, tileCacheDatabasePath: String, tileCacheAbsoluteMaximumBytes: ULong): UnitThrows SdkException.Registers the built-in MapQuest provider set from one consumer key, exactly like set_provider_credential, and wraps the raster-tile provider in a disk response cache. The cache is a SQLite database opened (or created) at tile_cache_database_path and bounded by tile_cache_absolute_maximum_bytes. Cached tile responses follow the tiles category’s time-to-live (thirty days by default, the imagery provider’s terms ceiling); a cache miss goes to the network and back-fills the cache, so pre-warmed tiles keep rendering when the network is unavailable. Re-registration replaces the providers, including the cached raster-tile provider. # Parameters - mapquest_api_key — the provider consumer key. - tile_cache_database_path — non-empty absolute path of the cache database. - tile_cache_absolute_maximum_bytes — positive byte budget of the cache. # Errors Throws SdkError when the path is empty, the byte budget is not positive, or the cache cannot be opened or refuses the quota; the detail names the reason verbatim.
registerUrlTemplateRasterTileSourcefun registerUrlTemplateRasterTileSource(source: UrlTemplateRasterTileSource): UnitThrows SdkException.Registers a provider-neutral raster base map: any web-mercator XYZ tileset that publishes a {z}/{x}/{y} URL template. The registration replaces the raster-tile contract only; every other provider keeps serving. It also drops any installed tile cache, because the cache’s terms belong to the provider that installed it; a later raster_tile_cache_terms then throws the not-configured error rather than reporting another provider’s ceiling. Re-registering replaces the source. # Parameters - source — the tile source and its terms. # Errors A malformed template, a blank source name or an inverted zoom range throws InvalidCoordinateInput with a precise detail, and the previous source keeps serving.
setRasterTileCacheTimeToLivefun setRasterTileCacheTimeToLive(timeToLiveSeconds: ULong): UnitThrows SdkException.Overrides the installed raster-tile cache’s time-to-live in seconds. A zero value is refused, because it would expire every entry on capture and store nothing. A value above the installed provider’s declared terms ceiling is accepted, and the ceiling clamps what the cache stores; raster_tile_cache_terms reports the effective value. # Parameters - time_to_live_seconds — requested time-to-live. # Errors Throws ProviderNotConfigured when no tile cache is installed, naming TileCache as the unconfigured backing store, and InvalidCoordinateInput for a zero time-to-live.
rasterTileCacheTermsfun rasterTileCacheTerms(): TileCacheTermsReturns TileCacheTerms. Throws SdkException.Reads the effective raster-tile caching terms of the installed cache, for display on a settings page. Reports the time-to-live currently in force (the category default, or the last accepted override clamped to the provider’s ceiling), the provider’s declared ceiling, and the category default. Read-only: the readback never mutates the cache. # Errors Throws ProviderNotConfigured when no tile cache is installed, naming TileCache as the unconfigured backing store.
subscribeToDiagnosticEventsfun subscribeToDiagnosticEvents(listener: SdkDiagnosticEventListener, minimumSeverity: SdkLogSeverity): Unit—Subscribes listener to the SDK’s structured log events. Only events at minimum_severity or above are delivered. Coordinates inside event messages are rounded before delivery, and API keys are never included. Listener callbacks run on the threads that produce the events and must not block. Subscribing an already subscribed listener replaces its severity threshold. # Parameters - listener — the diagnostics listener. - minimum_severity — lowest severity delivered.
flushRecentDiagnosticEventsfun flushRecentDiagnosticEvents(listener: SdkDiagnosticEventListener, minimumSeverity: SdkLogSeverity, maximumCount: UInt): UIntReturns UInt.Delivers up to maximum_count of the most recent buffered events at minimum_severity or above to the listener, oldest first, and returns how many were delivered. The flush does not remove events, so a later flush can deliver them again. The flush is bounded and synchronous; the listener must not block. # Parameters - listener — the diagnostics listener. - minimum_severity — lowest severity delivered. - maximum_count — upper bound on delivered events. # Returns The number of events delivered.
latestProviderFailureDiagnosticsfun latestProviderFailureDiagnostics(): List<ProviderFailureDiagnostic>Returns List<ProviderFailureDiagnostic>.Returns the retained diagnostics of failed provider calls made by foreign provider implementations, oldest first. A failure is recorded whether the implementation threw one of the contract’s SdkError variants or failed without a mapped error. The buffer keeps a bounded number of the most recent failures and drops older ones. Reading is non-destructive: the call neither records nor clears entries. The typed error still surfaces at the failing call; this readback lets a failure be classified after the fact. See ProviderFailureDiagnostic for the fields of an entry. # Returns The retained entries, oldest first.

NavigationListener

Navigation event listener. Implement this interface and subscribe it on Navigator; each subscription delivers only the topic it was registered for.

Threading Callbacks run synchronously on the thread that drives the controller and must not block. A callback that calls back into the controller while a dispatch is in flight is suppressed: the state change behind it is already applied, and only its broadcast is skipped.

Implement this interface in Kotlin; the SDK invokes it through the matching registration or subscription method.

Members

MemberSignatureReturns / errorsPurpose
onNavigationInstructionfun onNavigationInstruction(instruction: NavigationInstruction): Unit—Receives the composed instruction payload of every dispatched state change (the instructions topic).
onDeviationStatusChangefun onDeviationStatusChange(deviationStatusChange: DeviationStatusChange): Unit—Receives a deviation-status update (the deviation topic): off route on entry and on every recorded measurement update while the deviation persists, and on route when it clears.
onNavigationPhaseChangefun onNavigationPhaseChange(navigationPhaseChange: NavigationPhaseChange): Unit—Receives one phase transition per dispatched trip-state transition (the phase topic).
onSpeechInstructionfun onSpeechInstruction(speechInstruction: SpeechInstruction): Unit—Receives one utterance trigger when the controller’s distance-band policy judges the current fix newsworthy, for example when a trigger band is crossed. The text is the composed speech text, verbatim and never rewritten; playback and speech synthesis remain the application’s responsibility.

Subscription

Handle for exactly one (topic, listener) subscription. Cancelling is explicit and idempotent; dropping the handle does not unsubscribe.

Navigator

The navigation controller: starts and stops trips, accepts position fixes and reroutes, broadcasts every state change to the registered listeners, and answers read-only state and instruction queries. Obtain routes from MapSdk::calculate_route or offline_route_from_archive_bytes and start a trip on them with this controller.

The listener callbacks run synchronously on the thread that drives the controller call; a listener calling back into the controller while a dispatch is still in flight is suppressed, and only the broadcast is skipped. The controller never holds its state lock across a listener callback.

Construction

ConstructorSignaturePurpose
constructorconstructor()Builds the controller with no active trip and no subscriptions.

Members

MemberSignatureReturns / errorsPurpose

subscribeToDeviationStatusfun subscribeToDeviationStatus(listener: NavigationListener): SubscriptionReturns Subscription.Subscribes the listener to the deviation-status topic, in registration order.
subscribeToPhaseChangesfun subscribeToPhaseChanges(listener: NavigationListener): SubscriptionReturns Subscription.Subscribes the listener to the phase-transition topic, in registration order.
startNavigationfun startNavigation(route: Route, unitSystem: UnitSystem, stepAdvancePolicy: StepAdvancePolicy, deviationPolicy: DeviationPolicy): UnitThrows SdkException.Begins navigating route with the given policies, replacing any active trip. The initial instruction payload is dispatched; no deviation or phase transitions exist yet. A route without traversable steps represents an already-arrived trip. # Parameters - route — the route to navigate. - unit_system — units used in composed instruction text. - step_advance_policy — step-advance strategy and thresholds. - deviation_policy — off-route detection thresholds. # Errors Throws InvalidNavigationInput for policies with non-finite or negative thresholds, or for a route whose step maneuver label the SDK does not recognize.
updateLocationfun updateLocation(locationUpdate: NavigationLocationUpdate): Unit—Delivers one position fix to the active trip; without an active trip the fix is dropped. Fixes without an accuracy report never trigger a step advance and are never judged by the deviation detector.
applyReroutefun applyReroute(route: Route, stepAdvancePolicy: StepAdvancePolicy): UnitThrows SdkException.Replaces the route of the active trip (a reroute). The replacement route must be anchored at the trip’s current snapped coordinate. The step-advance strategy for the new route is configured by step_advance_policy; the deviation policy persists. A reroute offered to an arrived trip is ignored, and without an active trip the event is dropped. An in-flight reroute calculation is settled by this call whether the route is applied or ignored, so the calculation gate reopens after the integrator acts. # Errors Throws InvalidNavigationInput for an invalid policy or an unrecognized maneuver label.
beginRerouteCalculationfun beginRerouteCalculation(): BooleanReturns Boolean.Applies the reroute-recalculation gates to one reroute request. Returns true when every gate passes (no calculation in flight, outside the cooldown window and, when both fix references exist, beyond the movement threshold) and a calculation is marked as in flight, readable as the trip state’s is_calculating_new_route; returns false when the request is refused. A request without an open, still-navigable trip (no trip, or an arrived trip) is refused before the gates are consulted. A caller that receives true owes a settle: either the eventual apply_reroute (applied or ignored) or cancel_reroute_calculation. The trip’s first attempt always passes the cooldown and movement gates. # Returns True when the request passed the gates and a calculation is in flight.
cancelRerouteCalculationfun cancelRerouteCalculation(): Unit—Settles an in-flight reroute calculation without applying a route, for example when the integrator abandons the request. The calculation gate reopens; the cooldown keeps running from the calculation’s beginning and the movement reference stays where it was. Idempotent.
configureReroutePolicyfun configureReroutePolicy(reroutePolicy: ReroutePolicy): UnitThrows SdkException.Replaces the reroute-recalculation hysteresis policy in force, keeping the gate’s recorded state. # Parameters - reroute_policy — cooldown and movement thresholds. # Errors Throws InvalidNavigationInput when a threshold is not finite or is negative; the policy in force is then untouched.
currentTripStatefun currentTripState(): TripNavigationState?Returns TripNavigationState?.The state of the active trip, or null without one.
currentInstructionsfun currentInstructions(): NavigationInstruction?Returns NavigationInstruction?.The composed turn-by-turn instruction payload of the current trip state, or null without an active trip. Repeated reads of an unchanged state return the same payload.
subscribeToSpeechInstructionsfun subscribeToSpeechInstructions(listener: NavigationListener): SubscriptionReturns Subscription.Subscribes the listener to the speech-instruction trigger topic, in registration order. The controller decides when a line is worth speaking. Trigger bands reuse the display phrase’s distance bands, so a spoken “in 100 meters” matches the phrase shown in the payload; each band announces at most once per step, and a minimum inter-utterance spacing and repeat distance suppress chatter. Speech synthesis and playback remain the application’s responsibility.
addNavigationListenerfun addNavigationListener(listener: NavigationListener): SubscriptionReturns Subscription.Subscribes one listener to all four navigation topics (instructions, deviation status, phase changes and speech instructions) in one call and answers the composite subscription that cancels all four. Delivery semantics match the four individual subscribe_to_* calls: the listener receives each topic on its own method, in registration order, and cancel() removes every one of the four registrations (idempotent, like a single-topic subscription).
stopNavigationfun stopNavigation(): Unit—Ends the active trip and clears the trip state: after this call current_trip_state and current_instructions answer null, and location updates, reroutes and reroute requests are dropped until start_navigation begins a new trip. The speech-trigger band memory and the reroute-recalculation gate are reset with the trip; utterance identifiers stay monotonic across the stop and the configured reroute policy persists. Listener subscriptions are untouched and keep delivering the next trip’s events. Stopping without an active trip is a no-op.

MapView

The native map surface view: renders the camera-driven tiled map plus the overlay list onto a live platform window surface. Construct it with the MapSdk whose registered raster-tile provider the attached surface draws from; the provider is resolved at attach time, so with no registered provider attach throws ProviderNotConfigured.

Lifecycle

attach wraps the platform handle, acquires the surface-compatible graphics context, negotiates the surface format, configures the initial extent and resolves the tile provider. Each step’s failure throws: RenderingSurfaceUnavailable for the GPU or surface path, InvalidRenderInput for a bad handle or extent, and ProviderNotConfigured for the missing provider. resize, called from the platform’s surface-size callback, reconfigures the surface and rejects a zero extent. detach releases the surface state until a re-attach.

Overlay state outlives attach and detach cycles: set_overlays, add_overlay, update_overlay, remove_overlay and clear_overlays all work detached, and the next attach draws the stored list. Generated overlay identifiers also survive detach and attach, so an overlay added while detached stays addressable.

Draw model

Frames are explicit: the platform view calls draw once per rendered frame from its own cadence (a display link, a choreographer, or a resize-then-once pattern) with the current MapCamera. The SDK runs no internal render thread and no continuous redraw loop. Each draw lists the camera’s visible tiles, fetches pooled misses from the surface-attached provider within a per-frame budget, and renders tiles then overlays alpha-blended, presenting to the surface. A failed frame throws and leaves the previous frame on screen.

Draws on one view are serialized: a draw holding the view’s render state reports a concurrent draw or resize with RenderingSurfaceUnavailable, and the platform cadence retries on the next frame.

The extent must be non-zero; a platform view that is not laid out yet waits for resize. The call validates the handle, acquires the graphics context, negotiates the format, configures the surface and resolves the raster provider. Attaching an already attached view is refused. # Parameters - surface_handle — exactly one platform pointer. - width_pixels — initial surface width in physical pixels. - height_pixels — initial surface height in physical pixels. # Errors Throws InvalidRenderInput for a bad handle or a zero extent, RenderingSurfaceUnavailable for a GPU or surface failure, and ProviderNotConfigured when no raster-tile provider is registered.
resizefun resize(widthPixels: UInt, heightPixels: UInt): UnitThrows SdkException.Reconfigures the surface to the new physical-pixel extent; both extents must be non-zero. A resize during a draw reports the busy state, and the next draw or resize picks up the new extent. # Errors Throws InvalidRenderInput for a zero extent and RenderingSurfaceUnavailable when a draw owns the surface.
setDevicePixelRatiofun setDevicePixelRatio(devicePixelRatio: Double): UnitThrows SdkException.Sets the drawing buffer’s device pixels per point or CSS pixel, so labels and overlay screen sizes keep their declared point size on a 2x or 3x surface. The built-in styles declare point sizes while the surface draws device pixels; each draw multiplies every placed glyph size, route and traffic line width, and marker and pin radius by this ratio exactly once. The ratio outlives attach and detach cycles like the overlay list. The default is 1.0 until your platform code reports the surface’s own. # Parameters - device_pixel_ratio — device pixels per point. # Errors Throws InvalidRenderInput for a non-finite or non-positive ratio; the previous ratio stays in force.
detachfun detach(): Unit—Detaches: releases the surface, its renderer and its scheduler. Overlay state persists, and re-attach rebuilds the drawing machinery. Safe against a draw still in flight; that frame completes and the state is then dropped without being restored.
setOverlaysfun setOverlays(overlayDescriptors: List<MapOverlay>): UnitThrows SdkException.Replaces the drawn overlay list in one call, in order (later entries draw over earlier ones); an empty list clears. Every descriptor must be valid for its kind, and no partial list is kept. This call replaces the whole drawn list, including overlays added through add_overlay, and drops the addressed bookkeeping, so an identifier returned by add_overlay before this call no longer addresses anything afterwards. Use it for a list owned whole, and add_overlay, update_overlay and remove_overlay for individually managed overlays; a later add_overlay appends to the replaced list and works alongside its unaddressed entries. # Errors Throws InvalidRenderInput when any descriptor is invalid; the previous list stays in force.
addOverlayfun addOverlay(overlay: MapOverlay): StringReturns String. Throws SdkException.Adds one overlay to the drawn list and returns the generated opaque identifier that addresses it, such as overlay-1. Identifiers come from a monotonic per-view sequence and are never reused, not even after clear_overlays or set_overlays. Validation matches set_overlays’ all-or-nothing rule for the single descriptor: a refused descriptor throws and adds nothing, leaving the drawn list and the identifier sequence unchanged. The new overlay draws last, over the entries already in the list. # Returns The identifier addressing the added overlay. # Errors Throws InvalidRenderInput when the descriptor is invalid.
updateOverlayfun updateOverlay(overlayIdentifier: String, overlay: MapOverlay): UnitThrows SdkException.Replaces the overlay addressed by overlay_identifier. # Parameters - overlay_identifier — an identifier returned by add_overlay. - overlay — the replacement descriptor. # Errors Throws InvalidRenderInput for an unknown identifier (never generated, invalidated by a later set_overlays or clear_overlays, or already removed), with a detail naming the reason. An invalid descriptor throws and keeps the previously addressed overlay in force.
removeOverlayfun removeOverlay(overlayIdentifier: String): BooleanReturns Boolean.Removes the overlay addressed by overlay_identifier and answers whether that identifier was present. Removing an unknown identifier is not an error: it answers false and leaves the drawn list unchanged. # Returns True when the identifier was present and its overlay was removed.
clearOverlaysfun clearOverlays(): Unit—Clears the whole drawn overlay list, including the list supplied through set_overlays and every added addressed overlay, so following frames draw the tiles alone until set_overlays or add_overlay supplies new content. Identifiers generated earlier no longer address anything afterwards.
drawsuspend fun draw(camera: MapCamera): FrameStatisticsAsynchronous. Returns FrameStatistics. Throws SdkException.Draws one frame for the camera: the camera’s visible tiles fetched and rendered, then overlaid and presented. # Parameters - camera — the camera pose for this frame. # Returns The frame’s tile and overlay statistics, so the platform render loop can report exactly what a frame drew. Drawn pixels this frame come from present and fallback tiles, while the deferred and unavailable counts mark where later frames may still change pixels. # Errors Throws when the view is detached, a draw is already in flight, or the frame’s rendering failed. A thrown draw leaves the previous frame on screen. # Async Runs asynchronously; the call does not block the calling thread.
setLocationIndicatorfun setLocationIndicator(state: LocationIndicatorState, style: LocationIndicatorStyle): UnitThrows SdkException.Sets the single location layer drawn after the tile pass and the overlay pass (topmost SDK layer), replacing any earlier state. Validation is all-or-nothing: a state or style that fails validation throws and keeps the earlier indicator. The state outlives attach and detach cycles like the overlay list. Every null style field resolves to the documented default. # Parameters - state — position, course and accuracy to draw. - style — visual form and style of the layer. # Errors Throws InvalidRenderInput for a state or style the layer cannot draw.
clearLocationIndicatorfun clearLocationIndicator(): Unit—Clears the location layer; following frames draw tiles and overlays alone until set_location_indicator supplies new state.
isFrameSettledfun isFrameSettled(camera: MapCamera): BooleanReturns Boolean. Throws SdkException.Reads whether the view’s presented state would not change if draw ran again right now. Answers true when this camera value equals the last drawn camera, the overlay list and the location indicator are unchanged since that draw, and the last frame’s tile statistics resolved no pending pixels (no fallback, deferred or unavailable tiles). It answers false while a draw is in flight and before a frame has ever drawn. A pure query: it never draws, fetches or mutates state, so a platform render pump can call it every display frame and skip draw when it answers true, letting the presented frame stand and resuming on any change or on the next pending detail’s arrival. # Returns True when a redraw would not change the presented frame. # Errors Throws RenderingSurfaceUnavailable when the view is detached.
setVectorTileSourcefun setVectorTileSource(source: UrlTemplateVectorTileSource): UnitThrows SdkException.Installs a vector base map, a provider-neutral vector tileset painted with one of the SDK’s built-in styles, replacing any vector base already installed. The source is validated before anything moves (the template’s placeholders and scheme, the zoom range and the style id), so a refused call keeps the previously installed base in force. Each frame resolves the camera’s visible tiles through one shared scheduler: a tile is fetched and decoded once and restyled from its cached geometry when the style changes or the camera crosses a style zoom stop, never refetched for either. The styled base draws over the raster tiles and beneath the overlay list. A tile that fails to fetch or decode is skipped and counted; it never fails the frame. Configuring a base needs no attached surface: like the overlay list, the source outlives attach and detach cycles. # Parameters - source — the tileset, attribution and style. # Errors Throws when the source is invalid or a frame draw is in flight; install after the frame draws.
clearVectorTileSourcefun clearVectorTileSource(): UnitThrows SdkException.Removes the vector base map; following frames draw raster tiles and overlays alone until set_vector_tile_source installs a new base. Like installing, this throws while a frame draw is in flight. # Errors Throws when a frame draw is in flight.
vectorTileSourceStatusfun vectorTileSourceStatus(): VectorTileSourceStatusReturns VectorTileSourceStatus.Reads the vector base source’s status: the configured source and style plus the last resolved frame’s drawn and failed tile counts. A pure query that never fetches or draws; it answers while a frame is in flight with the previous frame’s counts. It never throws: with no source installed it answers a not-configured status.

addListenerfun addListener(listener: SdkDiagnosticEventListener, minimumSeverity: SdkLogSeverity): Unit—Subscribes the listener to the SDK’s structured log events at minimum_severity or above. Subscribing an already subscribed listener replaces its severity threshold. # Parameters - listener — the diagnostics listener. - minimum_severity — lowest severity delivered.
flushRecentfun flushRecent(listener: SdkDiagnosticEventListener, minimumSeverity: SdkLogSeverity, maximumCount: UInt): UIntReturns UInt.Delivers up to maximum_count of the most recent buffered events at minimum_severity or above to the listener, oldest first, and answers how many were delivered. The flush is non-destructive and synchronous, and the listener must not block. # Parameters - listener — the diagnostics listener. - minimum_severity — lowest severity delivered. - maximum_count — upper bound on delivered events. # Returns The number of events delivered.

PositionController

Validates and smooths one host’s position stream.

The host owns the operating system’s location API and its permission prompt, and reports the resulting fixes and failures here. The controller validates each fix, ignores stationary repeats when smoothing course, tracks staleness and records source failures, so the renderer’s location indicator, a follow camera and the navigation controller read one consistent stream.

Construction

ConstructorSignaturePurpose
constructorconstructor()Builds an empty controller with the default course-smoothing window and staleness threshold.

Members

MemberSignatureReturns / errorsPurpose
feedFixfun feedFix(fix: PositionFix): UnitThrows SdkException.Accepts one fix from the host’s source. # Parameters - fix — the coordinate and the source’s optional accuracy, course and timestamp. # Errors The coordinate must be inside its canonical ranges and every reported scalar must be finite (accuracy and timestamp also non-negative). An invalid fix throws with the validator’s detail and leaves the previous state in force.
sourceFailedfun sourceFailed(error: PositionSourceError): Unit—Records a source failure. The latest fix stays readable while the source recovers; a later successful fix clears the status.
latestFixfun latestFix(): PositionFix?Returns PositionFix?.The latest accepted fix, or null before the first accepted one.
smoothedCourseDegreesfun smoothedCourseDegrees(): Double?Returns Double?.The smoothed course across the most recent fixes that reported one, in degrees clockwise from true north, or null when no fix carried a course.
isStalefun isStale(nowSeconds: Double): BooleanReturns Boolean.Whether the latest fix is older than the staleness threshold at now_seconds. A fix without a timestamp is never stale.
sourceStatusfun sourceStatus(): PositionSourceError?Returns PositionSourceError?.The last source failure, or null when the last event was a fix.

UrlTemplateRasterTileSource

One provider-neutral base-map tile source: a web-mercator XYZ raster tileset addressed by a {z}/{x}/{y} URL template.

The SDK supplies no tile source of its own; you provide the URL template and the tileset’s terms. Every field is validated when the source is registered, so a malformed template or an inverted zoom range throws instead of failing on the first tile.

FieldTypePurpose
urlTemplateStringThe {z}/{x}/{y} URL template the tileset publishes: an absolute http/https URL carrying those three placeholders and no other.
sourceNameStringThe tileset’s name, used verbatim in every diagnostic it raises.
minimumZoomLevelUByteLowest zoom level the tileset serves.
maximumZoomLevelUByteHighest zoom level the tileset serves.
imageFormatRasterImageFormatThe image format the tileset serves. Fetched tiles report this format whatever the caller requests: the tile bytes are the truth, and the renderer decodes by the record it receives.
tileResolutionRasterTileResolutionThe pixel resolution the tileset serves (the same rule as the format: the fetched tile reports what it contains).
userAgentStringThe User-Agent header every tile request carries; empty sends none. A public tile service identifies its clients by it, and several usage policies refuse clients that send nothing.

UrlTemplateVectorTileSource

One provider-neutral vector base-map source: a web-mercator XYZ vector tileset addressed by a {z}/{x}/{y} URL template, painted with one of the SDK’s built-in styles.

The SDK supplies no tile source or style list of its own; you provide the URL template, the attribution its terms require and the style id. The style is named by an id such as bright-light, fiord-dark or positron-light, and an unknown id throws here rather than on the first frame. Every field is validated when the source is installed, so a malformed template or an inverted zoom range throws instead of failing on the first tile.

Draw order: while installed, the styled base replaces the raster tiles, and it paints beneath every overlay the view is asked to draw, so your markers, routes and location indicator stay above the base map.

The built-in styles paint fills, lines and circles only; place labels and road shields are not rendered.

FieldTypePurpose
urlTemplateStringThe {z}/{x}/{y} URL template the tileset publishes: an absolute http/https URL carrying those three placeholders and no other.
sourceNameStringThe tileset’s name, used verbatim in every diagnostic it raises.
attributionTextStringThe attribution line the tileset’s terms require wherever it is shown; the status readback reports it back for your UI to display.
styleIdStringThe built-in style id the base paints with.
minimumZoomLevelUByteLowest zoom level the tileset serves.
maximumZoomLevelUByteHighest zoom level the tileset serves.

MapOverlay

One overlay shape drawn over the map surface’s tiles in every frame, selected by kind. Each kind reads exactly its own payload fields and ignores the others. A descriptor whose kind-required payload is absent, or whose style field is unusable, rejects the whole set_overlays call and keeps the previous list in force. Absent style fields keep the documented default style; present style fields must be usable (channels in [0, 1], widths and radii positive and finite).

FieldTypePurpose
kindMapOverlayKindWhich overlay shape this descriptor configures and which payload fields carry it.
coordinatesList<GeographicCoordinate>?RoutePolyline: the traversal-order polyline; consecutive equal coordinates skip their degenerate segment. Required for the kind.
rgbaColorOverlayColor?Route polyline, filled polygon and point markers: solid color override, or null for the kind’s documented default.
widthPixelsDouble?Route polyline and traffic flow: line width in screen pixels (positive and finite), or null for the kind’s documented default.
ringCoordinatesList<GeographicCoordinate>?FilledPolygon: the outer ring in traversal order without a repeated closing vertex (a repeated one is tolerated and dropped). Required for the kind.
pointMarkerPositionsList<GeographicCoordinate>?PointMarkers and PointPins: the geographic anchor of every marker (a pin’s anchor is its tip). Required for both kinds.
pointMarkerRadiusPixelsDouble?PointMarkers and PointPins: marker radius in screen pixels (positive and finite), or null for the documented default. A pin’s radius is its head radius.
trafficFlowSegmentsList<TrafficFlowData>?TrafficFlow: the flow observations to paint, one per road segment (or polyline of segments), colored by congestion_level; the same TrafficFlowData records fetch_traffic_flow returns. Required for the kind.

SurfaceHandle

The platform window surface handle handed to MapView::attach: set exactly one platform pointer and leave the rest null. A null-or-ambiguous handle is refused with InvalidRenderInput; a null pointer is u64 0 or null, never a zeroed pointer passed through.

The object behind the pointer must outlive the attached view: the raw handles are the caller’s validity guarantee, and detach or drop releases the SDK side first, so dropping the platform view before detach is a caller bug.

FieldTypePurpose
appkitViewPointerULong?macOS: pointer to the NSView the surface renders into (Metal creates the layer from the view); null on the other platforms.
iosViewPointerULong?iOS: pointer to the UIView the surface renders into; null on the other platforms.
androidNativeWindowPointerULong?Android: pointer to the ANativeWindow obtained from the platform Surface (ANativeWindow_fromSurface); null on the other platforms.
