NavigationPhase

High-level phase of a trip that has already been started. Rerouting is not a phase of its own: the controller moves Navigating to OffRoute and back within a trip, and Navigating to Arrived at its end.

VariantPurpose
NAVIGATINGFollowing the route’s step sequence.
OFF_ROUTEThe deviation detector judged the last graded fix off route; progress is held at the last on-route values until a graded fix recovers or a reroute replaces the route.
ARRIVEDThe final step has been completed; location updates no longer change the state.

DeviationGradeKind

Which grade of deviation a recorded deviation carries: the distinction between off the current step yet still on the route line, and completely off the route. Only the fully-off grade holds navigation; the wrong-step grade never does on its own.

VariantPurpose
FULLY_OFF_ROUTEThe fix projects onto neither the current step nor any future step of the remaining route line: the holding grade. The trip’s progress is held until a graded fix recovers or a reroute replaces the route.
OFF_STEP_ON_ROUTEThe fix is off the current step but projects onto a future step of the remaining route line: “on route, wrong step”. The trip keeps navigating and counting down, and is never held by this grade alone.

DistanceUnit

Length unit a distance-phrase magnitude is expressed in.

VariantPurpose
METERSMeters, used by the metric near and moderate bands.
KILOMETERSKilometers, used by the metric far band.
FEETFeet, used by the imperial near and moderate bands.
MILESMiles, used by the imperial far band.

DistancePhraseKind

Which form a distance phrase takes.

VariantPurpose
IMMEDIATEThe position is closer than half a near-band increment to the maneuver point; no distance is phrased and composed text drops the prefix. The magnitude is null on this kind.
QUANTITYA rounded distance magnitude in a specific unit; the magnitude and unit are set on this kind.
SUPPRESSEDNo distance is phrased because the holding (fully-off-route) deviation grade applies: the projection is held, so any countdown composed from it would be a phantom measurement. The magnitude is null on this kind, and the composed text channels carry no distance prefix.

ManeuverInstructionTextKind

Which form an instruction text takes.

VariantPurpose
COMPOSEDThe provider authored instruction text for this maneuver.
UNAVAILABLEThe provider authored no instruction text for this maneuver; nothing is invented to fill it. All four text fields are null on this kind.

DeviationStatusChangeKind

Which form a deviation-status update takes.

VariantPurpose
OFF_ROUTEThe trip is judged deviating; the deviation description is set on this kind. The description’s grade kind distinguishes the holding fully-off grade from a wrong-step record, which is delivered while the trip phase stays Navigating.
ON_ROUTEA previously recorded deviation cleared; the trip is judged on route.

NavigationPhaseChange

A phase-transition event delivered on the phase topic.

VariantPurpose
OFF_ROUTE_ENTEREDThe trip entered the off-route phase from the navigating phase.
OFF_ROUTE_CLEAREDA graded fix back on the route line lifted the deviation and returned the trip to the navigating phase.
REROUTE_APPLIEDA reroute event replaced the route (delivered only when the event actually applied; an ignored reroute produces no transition).
ARRIVEDThe final step completed; the trip reached the arrived phase.

StepAdvancePolicyKind

Which step-advance strategy a navigation policy configures.

VariantPurpose
MANUALSteps change only when driven programmatically; the trip still tracks progress. The threshold fields are ignored on this kind.
DISTANCE_TO_END_OF_STEPAdvances when the position fix comes within the threshold of the end of the current step (eager advance).
DISTANCE_FROM_STEPAdvances when the position fix moves farther from the current step’s polyline than the threshold (delayed advance).

DeviationPolicyKind

Which deviation-detection strategy a deviation policy configures.

VariantPurpose
DISTANCE_THRESHOLDFlags a deviation when the raw fix is farther from the remaining route line than the configured threshold, widened by the fix’s reported accuracy.

MapOverlayKind

Which overlay shape an overlay descriptor configures.

VariantPurpose
ROUTE_POLYLINEA routed path drawn as a thick line.
FILLED_POLYGONA filled polygon: one outer ring, ear-clip triangulated.
POINT_MARKERSScreen-facing point markers (octagon fans).
TRAFFIC_FLOWCongestion-colored traffic-flow lines.
POINT_PINSScreen-facing teardrop pins anchored at their tip with a hollow head center (the A/B route-endpoint marker); uses PointMarkers’ payload fields.

LocationIndicatorVisualKind

Which visual form the location layer draws.

VariantPurpose
TRACKING_DOTPlain disc (tracking mode: no course known or no route).
GUIDED_COURSE_ARROWDisc plus course-directed heading wedge (navigation follow mode).

SpeechInstructionKind

What triggered a SpeechInstruction.

VariantPurpose
MANEUVER_APPROACHA trigger band was crossed this fix (the moderate or far threshold).
IMMEDIATE_MANEUVERThe immediate band: the maneuver is imminent.
OFF_ROUTE_RECOVERYGuidance just recovered from off route.
ARRIVALThe trip arrived.

SdkLogSeverity

Severity of a diagnostic event, ordered from most to least detailed.

VariantPurpose
TRACEVery fine-grained frame-path instrumentation (only delivered when a listener subscribed at this severity).
DEBUGFine-grained internal state transitions.
INFOCoarse-grained progress (the default minimum for a subscription).
WARNA problem this event explains.
ERRORA failure this event explains.

ProviderFailureClassification

Which shape of foreign provider failure a diagnostic captured.

VariantPurpose
UNCLASSIFIED_CALLBACK_FAILUREThe foreign implementation failed without a mapped error, for example by throwing an exception the contract does not define. The failure text is the binding runtime’s verbatim reason for it.
MAPPED_CONTRACT_ERRORThe foreign implementation threw one of the contract’s SdkError variants, which is carried as a typed error: the failure text is the thrown error’s verbatim display form.

PositionSourceError

Why a positioning source could not produce fixes.

VariantPurpose
PERMISSION_DENIEDThe user denied the permission the source needs.
SERVICE_DISABLEDLocation services are disabled on the device or by policy.
UNAVAILABLENo location provider can answer right now.
TIMEOUTThe source did not answer inside its timeout.

Errors

SdkError

Failures returned by the SDK. The detail message of a variant is always passed through verbatim from the failing component.

Each variant is a nested class of the SdkException sealed class.

VariantPayloadPurpose
InvalidCoordinateInputdetail: StringA coordinate, viewport extent or box corner failed validation.
NetworkRequestFaileddetail: StringThe network transport failed; carries the transport’s verbatim detail.
ResponseParsingFailuredetail: StringThe provider answered with a payload the parser could not use.
ProviderRequestRejecteddetail: StringThe provider returned a documented application-level failure status.
RateLimitExhaustedNoneThe token-bucket rate limiter is exhausted; retry after the next refill.
ProviderNotConfiguredcontractName: StringNo provider implementation is registered for the requested contract.
InvalidNavigationInputdetail: StringA navigation input (a route record or a navigation policy) failed validation.
InvalidRenderInputdetail: StringAn overlay descriptor did not describe a usable overlay (wrong kind payload, an out-of-range color channel, or a non-positive or non-finite width or radius), or a surface input was structurally unusable (a null, zero or ambiguous platform surface pointer, or a non-positive viewport extent).
RenderingSurfaceUnavailabledetail: StringLive rendering could not proceed on the platform surface: the platform handle or surface was unusable, the graphics context could not be acquired, the surface format could not be negotiated or configured, the frame texture could not be acquired, or the frame’s render state was busy in another draw.
CacheOperationFailuredetail: StringA cache read, write or eviction failed (an unavailable store, a corrupt entry, or a byte-budget refusal). The detail names the reason verbatim.
OfflineRoutingFailuredetail: StringAn offline routing graph failed validation or could not be read: a truncated or foreign archive, an unsupported version, or a malformed section. The detail names the reason verbatim.

Async and threading

These calls are asynchronous on Kotlin: offlineRouteFromArchiveBytes, GeocodingProvider.forwardGeocode, GeocodingProvider.reverseGeocode, RasterTileProvider.fetchRasterTile, MapSdk.forwardGeocode, MapSdk.reverseGeocode, MapSdk.calculateRoute, MapSdk.calculateDistanceMatrix, MapSdk.suggest, MapSdk.search, MapSdk.fetchTrafficIncidents, MapSdk.fetchTrafficFlow, MapSdk.fetchRasterTile, MapView.draw, SearchEngine.search, SearchEngine.suggest, SearchEngine.reverseGeocode, RoutingEngine.calculateRoute, RoutingEngine.calculateDistanceMatrix.

Asynchronous calls are suspend functions and do not block the calling thread. The shipped map view members expect the main thread.

  • MapView.draw is frame-driven: call it from the platform display callback. A concurrent draw or resize reports RenderingSurfaceUnavailable; retry the next frame.
  • Navigation listener callbacks run synchronously on the thread that drives the controller. A listener must not block, and a callback made during an in-flight dispatch has its broadcast suppressed because the state change is already applied.
  • A diagnostics listener is called fire-and-forget on the thread that produced the event; it never delays the event stream.

iOS API reference

Generated from the SDK contract and the generated Swift bindings. Do not edit this page by hand; change the contract and regenerate the documentation.

The iOS artifact exposes the provider-neutral SDK through Swift bindings generated from the SDK contract, together with the shipped map view. This page documents every contract type and member the Swift surface exposes: what it does, how it is constructed, its parameters, its return value, the failures it raises, and its async and threading rules. The shipped MapNativeCoreUI map view is described in the platform guides.

Interfaces

MapCamera

Anchored map camera: geographic center, zoom level, bearing and pitch. The ground point under the center always sits at the viewport center; zoom and pitch are clamped to their valid ranges and bearing wraps into [0, 360).

Construction

ConstructorSignaturePurpose
constructorinit(center: GeographicCoordinate, zoomLevel: Double, bearingDegrees: Double, pitchDegrees: Double) throwsBuilds a camera at the given center, zoom level, bearing and pitch. # Parameters - center — geographic point placed at the viewport center. - zoom_level — zoom level, clamped to the valid range. - bearing_degrees — clockwise rotation from north, wrapped into [0, 360). - pitch_degrees — tilt from straight down, clamped to the valid range. # Errors Throws InvalidCoordinateInput when the center is not a valid coordinate or when a numeric argument is not finite.
fitBoundsstatic func fitBounds(boundingBox: BoundingBox, viewport: ViewportSize, edgeInsets: EdgeInsets, maximumZoomLevel: Double) throws -> MapCameraBuilds the camera that frames a bounding box inside the viewport’s inset region: top-down and north-up by construction (pitch and bearing zero), zoomed to the largest level keeping the whole box inside the inset area and clamped to maximum_zoom_level; the center is anchored on the inset region’s center. # Parameters - bounding_box — the area to frame. - viewport — viewport extent in pixels. - edge_insets — pixels kept clear on each viewport edge. - maximum_zoom_level — upper zoom bound for the fitted camera. # Errors Throws when the insets or the maximum zoom are not finite usable values, when the insets are negative or leave no inset area, or when the box spans no positive world area.

Members

MemberSignatureReturns / errorsPurpose
projectToScreenfunc projectToScreen(coordinate: GeographicCoordinate, viewport: ViewportSize, fieldOfViewDegrees: Double) throws -> ScreenPoint?Returns ScreenPoint?. Throws SdkError.Projects a coordinate to viewport pixels (origin top-left, y down). # Parameters - coordinate — the point to project. - viewport — viewport extent in pixels. - field_of_view_degrees — vertical field of view of the projection. # Returns The screen position, or null when the point lies behind the camera. # Errors Throws InvalidCoordinateInput for an invalid coordinate or viewport.
screenToGroundCoordinatefunc screenToGroundCoordinate(screenPoint: ScreenPoint, viewport: ViewportSize, fieldOfViewDegrees: Double) throws -> GeographicCoordinate?Returns GeographicCoordinate?. Throws SdkError.Unprojects a viewport pixel back onto the ground plane. # Parameters - screen_point — the pixel to unproject. - viewport — viewport extent in pixels. - field_of_view_degrees — vertical field of view of the projection. # Returns The ground coordinate, or null when the ray misses the ground (typically below the horizon at steep pitch). # Errors Throws InvalidCoordinateInput for an invalid viewport.
visibleTileKeysfunc visibleTileKeys(viewport: ViewportSize, fieldOfViewDegrees: Double, tileZoomLevel: UInt8) throws -> [TileKey]Returns [TileKey]. Throws SdkError.Lists every tile at tile_zoom_level whose area intersects the visible ground, sorted row-major from the north. # Parameters - viewport — viewport extent in pixels. - field_of_view_degrees — vertical field of view of the projection. - tile_zoom_level — zoom level of the listed tiles. # Errors Throws InvalidCoordinateInput for an invalid viewport.
tileZoomLevelfunc tileZoomLevel() -> UInt8Returns UInt8.Nearest whole zoom level a tile fetch should use for this camera.
panByScreenPixelsfunc panByScreenPixels(deltaXPixels: Double, deltaYPixels: Double, viewport: ViewportSize, fieldOfViewDegrees: Double) throws -> MapCameraReturns MapCamera. Throws SdkError.Pans by a pointer travel of delta_x_pixels x delta_y_pixels (screen pixels, x right / y down): the ground point the pointer just moved over becomes the new camera center, so map content tracks the pointer exactly. Answers the camera unchanged when the delta’s ground ray misses the plane (above the horizon at steep pitch). Gesture recognition stays in your UI layer; this call performs the camera math. # Parameters - delta_x_pixels — horizontal pointer travel in pixels. - delta_y_pixels — vertical pointer travel in pixels. - viewport — viewport extent in pixels. - field_of_view_degrees — vertical field of view of the projection. # Errors Throws InvalidCoordinateInput when the viewport extent is not positive.
zoomByLevelsAroundScreenPointfunc zoomByLevelsAroundScreenPoint(deltaZoomLevels: Double, focalPoint: ScreenPoint, viewport: ViewportSize, fieldOfViewDegrees: Double) throws -> MapCameraReturns MapCamera. Throws SdkError.Zooms by delta_zoom_levels (levels; positive zooms in) keeping the world point under focal_point fixed under it. Answers the zoom without the focal correction when the focal ray misses the ground plane (above the horizon at steep pitch). Zoom clamps to the camera’s own level range before the focal correction applies, so a clamped zoom still holds the focal point. # Parameters - delta_zoom_levels — zoom change in levels. - focal_point — screen pixel that stays fixed during the zoom. - viewport — viewport extent in pixels. - field_of_view_degrees — vertical field of view of the projection. # Errors Throws InvalidCoordinateInput when the viewport extent is not positive.
rotateByDegreesAroundScreenPointfunc rotateByDegreesAroundScreenPoint(deltaBearingDegrees: Double, focalPoint: ScreenPoint, viewport: ViewportSize, fieldOfViewDegrees: Double) throws -> MapCameraReturns MapCamera. Throws SdkError.Rotates the bearing by delta_bearing_degrees (degrees clockwise, wrapping into [0, 360)) keeping the world point under focal_point fixed under it. Answers the rotation without the focal correction when the focal ray misses the ground plane, which produces the touch-point turn a two-finger gesture implies. # Parameters - delta_bearing_degrees — bearing change in degrees. - focal_point — screen pixel that stays fixed during the rotation. - viewport — viewport extent in pixels. - field_of_view_degrees — vertical field of view of the projection. # Errors Throws InvalidCoordinateInput when the viewport extent is not positive.
centerfunc center() -> GeographicCoordinateReturns GeographicCoordinate.Reads the camera’s state back as it was constructed. The getters make the framing chosen by fit_bounds readable: the fitted zoom level, its anchored center, and the constructed bearing and pitch. Read-only: the camera has no setters, so a new pose is a new camera.
zoomLevelfunc zoomLevel() -> DoubleReturns Double.The camera’s zoom level.
bearingDegreesfunc bearingDegrees() -> DoubleReturns Double.The camera’s bearing in degrees clockwise from north, within [0, 360).
pitchDegreesfunc pitchDegrees() -> DoubleReturns Double.The camera’s pitch in degrees.
groundMetersPerScreenPixelfunc groundMetersPerScreenPixel(viewport: ViewportSize, fieldOfViewDegrees: Double) throws -> DoubleReturns Double. Throws SdkError.Ground meters represented by one screen pixel at the camera’s center: the equatorial ground meters per pixel at the camera’s zoom level times the cosine of the center latitude, so the answer shrinks toward the poles exactly like the projected ground. At any nonzero pitch this is an approximation valid at the viewport’s center column: the value is computed for a flat center and does not fold pitch into the answer. # Parameters - viewport — viewport extent in pixels. - field_of_view_degrees — vertical field of view of the projection. # Errors Throws InvalidCoordinateInput for an invalid viewport.

MapSdk

Provider entry point of the SDK: resolves every call through the providers registered on the object. Construct the object with no providers, then register them: native integrations through the SDK’s own registration calls and foreign integrations through the register_*_from_foreign methods (see the provider contract interfaces above). A call into a contract with no registered provider throws ProviderNotConfigured naming the contract.

The calls cover geocoding (forward and reverse), routing, distance matrix, place search, traffic incidents, traffic flow and raster tiles. Elevation and offline routing have no provider contract here: offline routing is the standalone offline_route_from_archive_bytes function.

setProviderCredentialfunc setProviderCredential(credential: String) throwsThrows SdkError.Registers the built-in MapQuest provider set from one consumer key, with the SDK defaults for base URL, rate limiting and retries. The call installs geocoding, routing, distance matrix, place search, traffic incidents, traffic flow and raster tiles, so one call and one key enable the whole provider set. Re-registration replaces every provider. Elevation has no provider and keeps throwing ProviderNotConfigured. # Parameters - credential — the provider consumer key. # Errors Throws SdkError when the credential is empty or the registration is refused.
setProviderCredentialWithTileCachefunc setProviderCredentialWithTileCache(mapquestApiKey: String, tileCacheDatabasePath: String, tileCacheAbsoluteMaximumBytes: UInt64) throwsThrows SdkError.Registers the built-in MapQuest provider set from one consumer key, exactly like set_provider_credential, and wraps the raster-tile provider in a disk response cache. The cache is a SQLite database opened (or created) at tile_cache_database_path and bounded by tile_cache_absolute_maximum_bytes. Cached tile responses follow the tiles category’s time-to-live (thirty days by default, the imagery provider’s terms ceiling); a cache miss goes to the network and back-fills the cache, so pre-warmed tiles keep rendering when the network is unavailable. Re-registration replaces the providers, including the cached raster-tile provider. # Parameters - mapquest_api_key — the provider consumer key. - tile_cache_database_path — non-empty absolute path of the cache database. - tile_cache_absolute_maximum_bytes — positive byte budget of the cache. # Errors Throws SdkError when the path is empty, the byte budget is not positive, or the cache cannot be opened or refuses the quota; the detail names the reason verbatim.
registerUrlTemplateRasterTileSourcefunc registerUrlTemplateRasterTileSource(source: UrlTemplateRasterTileSource) throwsThrows SdkError.Registers a provider-neutral raster base map: any web-mercator XYZ tileset that publishes a {z}/{x}/{y} URL template. The registration replaces the raster-tile contract only; every other provider keeps serving. It also drops any installed tile cache, because the cache’s terms belong to the provider that installed it; a later raster_tile_cache_terms then throws the not-configured error rather than reporting another provider’s ceiling. Re-registering replaces the source. # Parameters - source — the tile source and its terms. # Errors A malformed template, a blank source name or an inverted zoom range throws InvalidCoordinateInput with a precise detail, and the previous source keeps serving.
setRasterTileCacheTimeToLivefunc setRasterTileCacheTimeToLive(timeToLiveSeconds: UInt64) throwsThrows SdkError.Overrides the installed raster-tile cache’s time-to-live in seconds. A zero value is refused, because it would expire every entry on capture and store nothing. A value above the installed provider’s declared terms ceiling is accepted, and the ceiling clamps what the cache stores; raster_tile_cache_terms reports the effective value. # Parameters - time_to_live_seconds — requested time-to-live. # Errors Throws ProviderNotConfigured when no tile cache is installed, naming TileCache as the unconfigured backing store, and InvalidCoordinateInput for a zero time-to-live.
rasterTileCacheTermsfunc rasterTileCacheTerms() throws -> TileCacheTermsReturns TileCacheTerms. Throws SdkError.Reads the effective raster-tile caching terms of the installed cache, for display on a settings page. Reports the time-to-live currently in force (the category default, or the last accepted override clamped to the provider’s ceiling), the provider’s declared ceiling, and the category default. Read-only: the readback never mutates the cache. # Errors Throws ProviderNotConfigured when no tile cache is installed, naming TileCache as the unconfigured backing store.
subscribeToDiagnosticEventsfunc subscribeToDiagnosticEvents(listener: SdkDiagnosticEventListener, minimumSeverity: SdkLogSeverity)—Subscribes listener to the SDK’s structured log events. Only events at minimum_severity or above are delivered. Coordinates inside event messages are rounded before delivery, and API keys are never included. Listener callbacks run on the threads that produce the events and must not block. Subscribing an already subscribed listener replaces its severity threshold. # Parameters - listener — the diagnostics listener. - minimum_severity — lowest severity delivered.
flushRecentDiagnosticEventsfunc flushRecentDiagnosticEvents(listener: SdkDiagnosticEventListener, minimumSeverity: SdkLogSeverity, maximumCount: UInt32) -> UInt32Returns UInt32.Delivers up to maximum_count of the most recent buffered events at minimum_severity or above to the listener, oldest first, and returns how many were delivered. The flush does not remove events, so a later flush can deliver them again. The flush is bounded and synchronous; the listener must not block. # Parameters - listener — the diagnostics listener. - minimum_severity — lowest severity delivered. - maximum_count — upper bound on delivered events. # Returns The number of events delivered.
latestProviderFailureDiagnosticsfunc latestProviderFailureDiagnostics() -> [ProviderFailureDiagnostic]Returns [ProviderFailureDiagnostic].Returns the retained diagnostics of failed provider calls made by foreign provider implementations, oldest first. A failure is recorded whether the implementation threw one of the contract’s SdkError variants or failed without a mapped error. The buffer keeps a bounded number of the most recent failures and drops older ones. Reading is non-destructive: the call neither records nor clears entries. The typed error still surfaces at the failing call; this readback lets a failure be classified after the fact. See ProviderFailureDiagnostic for the fields of an entry. # Returns The retained entries, oldest first.

NavigationListener

Navigation event listener. Implement this interface and subscribe it on Navigator; each subscription delivers only the topic it was registered for.

Threading Callbacks run synchronously on the thread that drives the controller and must not block. A callback that calls back into the controller while a dispatch is in flight is suppressed: the state change behind it is already applied, and only its broadcast is skipped.

Implement this interface in Swift; the SDK invokes it through the matching registration or subscription method.

onDeviationStatusChangefunc onDeviationStatusChange(deviationStatusChange: DeviationStatusChange)—Receives a deviation-status update (the deviation topic): off route on entry and on every recorded measurement update while the deviation persists, and on route when it clears.
onNavigationPhaseChangefunc onNavigationPhaseChange(navigationPhaseChange: NavigationPhaseChange)—Receives one phase transition per dispatched trip-state transition (the phase topic).
onSpeechInstructionfunc onSpeechInstruction(speechInstruction: SpeechInstruction)—Receives one utterance trigger when the controller’s distance-band policy judges the current fix newsworthy, for example when a trigger band is crossed. The text is the composed speech text, verbatim and never rewritten; playback and speech synthesis remain the application’s responsibility.

Handle for exactly one (topic, listener) subscription. Cancelling is explicit and idempotent; dropping the handle does not unsubscribe.

Navigator

The navigation controller: starts and stops trips, accepts position fixes and reroutes, broadcasts every state change to the registered listeners, and answers read-only state and instruction queries. Obtain routes from MapSdk::calculate_route or offline_route_from_archive_bytes and start a trip on them with this controller.

The listener callbacks run synchronously on the thread that drives the controller call; a listener calling back into the controller while a dispatch is still in flight is suppressed, and only the broadcast is skipped. The controller never holds its state lock across a listener callback.

Construction

ConstructorSignaturePurpose
constructorinit()Builds the controller with no active trip and no subscriptions.

Members

MemberSignatureReturns / errorsPurpose

subscribeToDeviationStatusfunc subscribeToDeviationStatus(listener: NavigationListener) -> SubscriptionReturns Subscription.Subscribes the listener to the deviation-status topic, in registration order.
subscribeToPhaseChangesfunc subscribeToPhaseChanges(listener: NavigationListener) -> SubscriptionReturns Subscription.Subscribes the listener to the phase-transition topic, in registration order.
startNavigationfunc startNavigation(route: Route, unitSystem: UnitSystem, stepAdvancePolicy: StepAdvancePolicy, deviationPolicy: DeviationPolicy) throwsThrows SdkError.Begins navigating route with the given policies, replacing any active trip. The initial instruction payload is dispatched; no deviation or phase transitions exist yet. A route without traversable steps represents an already-arrived trip. # Parameters - route — the route to navigate. - unit_system — units used in composed instruction text. - step_advance_policy — step-advance strategy and thresholds. - deviation_policy — off-route detection thresholds. # Errors Throws InvalidNavigationInput for policies with non-finite or negative thresholds, or for a route whose step maneuver label the SDK does not recognize.
updateLocationfunc updateLocation(locationUpdate: NavigationLocationUpdate)—Delivers one position fix to the active trip; without an active trip the fix is dropped. Fixes without an accuracy report never trigger a step advance and are never judged by the deviation detector.
applyReroutefunc applyReroute(route: Route, stepAdvancePolicy: StepAdvancePolicy) throwsThrows SdkError.Replaces the route of the active trip (a reroute). The replacement route must be anchored at the trip’s current snapped coordinate. The step-advance strategy for the new route is configured by step_advance_policy; the deviation policy persists. A reroute offered to an arrived trip is ignored, and without an active trip the event is dropped. An in-flight reroute calculation is settled by this call whether the route is applied or ignored, so the calculation gate reopens after the integrator acts. # Errors Throws InvalidNavigationInput for an invalid policy or an unrecognized maneuver label.
beginRerouteCalculationfunc beginRerouteCalculation() -> BoolReturns Bool.Applies the reroute-recalculation gates to one reroute request. Returns true when every gate passes (no calculation in flight, outside the cooldown window and, when both fix references exist, beyond the movement threshold) and a calculation is marked as in flight, readable as the trip state’s is_calculating_new_route; returns false when the request is refused. A request without an open, still-navigable trip (no trip, or an arrived trip) is refused before the gates are consulted. A caller that receives true owes a settle: either the eventual apply_reroute (applied or ignored) or cancel_reroute_calculation. The trip’s first attempt always passes the cooldown and movement gates. # Returns True when the request passed the gates and a calculation is in flight.
cancelRerouteCalculationfunc cancelRerouteCalculation()—Settles an in-flight reroute calculation without applying a route, for example when the integrator abandons the request. The calculation gate reopens; the cooldown keeps running from the calculation’s beginning and the movement reference stays where it was. Idempotent.
configureReroutePolicyfunc configureReroutePolicy(reroutePolicy: ReroutePolicy) throwsThrows SdkError.Replaces the reroute-recalculation hysteresis policy in force, keeping the gate’s recorded state. # Parameters - reroute_policy — cooldown and movement thresholds. # Errors Throws InvalidNavigationInput when a threshold is not finite or is negative; the policy in force is then untouched.
currentTripStatefunc currentTripState() -> TripNavigationState?Returns TripNavigationState?.The state of the active trip, or null without one.
currentInstructionsfunc currentInstructions() -> NavigationInstruction?Returns NavigationInstruction?.The composed turn-by-turn instruction payload of the current trip state, or null without an active trip. Repeated reads of an unchanged state return the same payload.
subscribeToSpeechInstructionsfunc subscribeToSpeechInstructions(listener: NavigationListener) -> SubscriptionReturns Subscription.Subscribes the listener to the speech-instruction trigger topic, in registration order. The controller decides when a line is worth speaking. Trigger bands reuse the display phrase’s distance bands, so a spoken “in 100 meters” matches the phrase shown in the payload; each band announces at most once per step, and a minimum inter-utterance spacing and repeat distance suppress chatter. Speech synthesis and playback remain the application’s responsibility.
addNavigationListenerfunc addNavigationListener(listener: NavigationListener) -> SubscriptionReturns Subscription.Subscribes one listener to all four navigation topics (instructions, deviation status, phase changes and speech instructions) in one call and answers the composite subscription that cancels all four. Delivery semantics match the four individual subscribe_to_* calls: the listener receives each topic on its own method, in registration order, and cancel() removes every one of the four registrations (idempotent, like a single-topic subscription).
stopNavigationfunc stopNavigation()—Ends the active trip and clears the trip state: after this call current_trip_state and current_instructions answer null, and location updates, reroutes and reroute requests are dropped until start_navigation begins a new trip. The speech-trigger band memory and the reroute-recalculation gate are reset with the trip; utterance identifiers stay monotonic across the stop and the configured reroute policy persists. Listener subscriptions are untouched and keep delivering the next trip’s events. Stopping without an active trip is a no-op.

MapView

The native map surface view: renders the camera-driven tiled map plus the overlay list onto a live platform window surface. Construct it with the MapSdk whose registered raster-tile provider the attached surface draws from; the provider is resolved at attach time, so with no registered provider attach throws ProviderNotConfigured.

Lifecycle

attach wraps the platform handle, acquires the surface-compatible graphics context, negotiates the surface format, configures the initial extent and resolves the tile provider. Each step’s failure throws: RenderingSurfaceUnavailable for the GPU or surface path, InvalidRenderInput for a bad handle or extent, and ProviderNotConfigured for the missing provider. resize, called from the platform’s surface-size callback, reconfigures the surface and rejects a zero extent. detach releases the surface state until a re-attach.

Overlay state outlives attach and detach cycles: set_overlays, add_overlay, update_overlay, remove_overlay and clear_overlays all work detached, and the next attach draws the stored list. Generated overlay identifiers also survive detach and attach, so an overlay added while detached stays addressable.

Draw model

Frames are explicit: the platform view calls draw once per rendered frame from its own cadence (a display link, a choreographer, or a resize-then-once pattern) with the current MapCamera. The SDK runs no internal render thread and no continuous redraw loop. Each draw lists the camera’s visible tiles, fetches pooled misses from the surface-attached provider within a per-frame budget, and renders tiles then overlays alpha-blended, presenting to the surface. A failed frame throws and leaves the previous frame on screen.

Draws on one view are serialized: a draw holding the view’s render state reports a concurrent draw or resize with RenderingSurfaceUnavailable, and the platform cadence retries on the next frame.

Construction

ConstructorSignaturePurpose
constructorinit(mapSdk: MapSdk)Builds the view over the SDK state it draws from.

The extent must be non-zero; a platform view that is not laid out yet waits for resize. The call validates the handle, acquires the graphics context, negotiates the format, configures the surface and resolves the raster provider. Attaching an already attached view is refused. # Parameters - surface_handle — exactly one platform pointer. - width_pixels — initial surface width in physical pixels. - height_pixels — initial surface height in physical pixels. # Errors Throws InvalidRenderInput for a bad handle or a zero extent, RenderingSurfaceUnavailable for a GPU or surface failure, and ProviderNotConfigured when no raster-tile provider is registered.

A resize during a draw reports the busy state, and the next draw or resize picks up the new extent. # Errors Throws InvalidRenderInput for a zero extent and RenderingSurfaceUnavailable when a draw owns the surface.
setDevicePixelRatiofunc setDevicePixelRatio(devicePixelRatio: Double) throwsThrows SdkError.Sets the drawing buffer’s device pixels per point or CSS pixel, so labels and overlay screen sizes keep their declared point size on a 2x or 3x surface. The built-in styles declare point sizes while the surface draws device pixels; each draw multiplies every placed glyph size, route and traffic line width, and marker and pin radius by this ratio exactly once. The ratio outlives attach and detach cycles like the overlay list. The default is 1.0 until your platform code reports the surface’s own. # Parameters - device_pixel_ratio — device pixels per point. # Errors Throws InvalidRenderInput for a non-finite or non-positive ratio; the previous ratio stays in force.
detachfunc detach()—Detaches: releases the surface, its renderer and its scheduler. Overlay state persists, and re-attach rebuilds the drawing machinery. Safe against a draw still in flight; that frame completes and the state is then dropped without being restored.
setOverlaysfunc setOverlays(overlayDescriptors: [MapOverlay]) throwsThrows SdkError.Replaces the drawn overlay list in one call, in order (later entries draw over earlier ones); an empty list clears. Every descriptor must be valid for its kind, and no partial list is kept. This call replaces the whole drawn list, including overlays added through add_overlay, and drops the addressed bookkeeping, so an identifier returned by add_overlay before this call no longer addresses anything afterwards. Use it for a list owned whole, and add_overlay, update_overlay and remove_overlay for individually managed overlays; a later add_overlay appends to the replaced list and works alongside its unaddressed entries. # Errors Throws InvalidRenderInput when any descriptor is invalid; the previous list stays in force.
addOverlayfunc addOverlay(overlay: MapOverlay) throws -> StringReturns String. Throws SdkError.Adds one overlay to the drawn list and returns the generated opaque identifier that addresses it, such as overlay-1. Identifiers come from a monotonic per-view sequence and are never reused, not even after clear_overlays or set_overlays. Validation matches set_overlays’ all-or-nothing rule for the single descriptor: a refused descriptor throws and adds nothing, leaving the drawn list and the identifier sequence unchanged. The new overlay draws last, over the entries already in the list. # Returns The identifier addressing the added overlay. # Errors Throws InvalidRenderInput when the descriptor is invalid.
updateOverlayfunc updateOverlay(overlayIdentifier: String, overlay: MapOverlay) throwsThrows SdkError.Replaces the overlay addressed by overlay_identifier. # Parameters - overlay_identifier — an identifier returned by add_overlay. - overlay — the replacement descriptor. # Errors Throws InvalidRenderInput for an unknown identifier (never generated, invalidated by a later set_overlays or clear_overlays, or already removed), with a detail naming the reason. An invalid descriptor throws and keeps the previously addressed overlay in force.
removeOverlayfunc removeOverlay(overlayIdentifier: String) -> BoolReturns Bool.Removes the overlay addressed by overlay_identifier and answers whether that identifier was present. Removing an unknown identifier is not an error: it answers false and leaves the drawn list unchanged. # Returns True when the identifier was present and its overlay was removed.
clearOverlaysfunc clearOverlays()—Clears the whole drawn overlay list, including the list supplied through set_overlays and every added addressed overlay, so following frames draw the tiles alone until set_overlays or add_overlay supplies new content. Identifiers generated earlier no longer address anything afterwards.
drawfunc draw(camera: MapCamera) async throws -> FrameStatisticsAsynchronous. Returns FrameStatistics. Throws SdkError.Draws one frame for the camera: the camera’s visible tiles fetched and rendered, then overlaid and presented. # Parameters - camera — the camera pose for this frame. # Returns The frame’s tile and overlay statistics, so the platform render loop can report exactly what a frame drew. Drawn pixels this frame come from present and fallback tiles, while the deferred and unavailable counts mark where later frames may still change pixels. # Errors Throws when the view is detached, a draw is already in flight, or the frame’s rendering failed. A thrown draw leaves the previous frame on screen. # Async Runs asynchronously; the call does not block the calling thread.
setLocationIndicatorfunc setLocationIndicator(state: LocationIndicatorState, style: LocationIndicatorStyle) throwsThrows SdkError.Sets the single location layer drawn after the tile pass and the overlay pass (topmost SDK layer), replacing any earlier state. Validation is all-or-nothing: a state or style that fails validation throws and keeps the earlier indicator. The state outlives attach and detach cycles like the overlay list. Every null style field resolves to the documented default. # Parameters - state — position, course and accuracy to draw. - style — visual form and style of the layer. # Errors Throws InvalidRenderInput for a state or style the layer cannot draw.
clearLocationIndicatorfunc clearLocationIndicator()—Clears the location layer; following frames draw tiles and overlays alone until set_location_indicator supplies new state.
isFrameSettledfunc isFrameSettled(camera: MapCamera) throws -> BoolReturns Bool. Throws SdkError.Reads whether the view’s presented state would not change if draw ran again right now. Answers true when this camera value equals the last drawn camera, the overlay list and the location indicator are unchanged since that draw, and the last frame’s tile statistics resolved no pending pixels (no fallback, deferred or unavailable tiles). It answers false while a draw is in flight and before a frame has ever drawn. A pure query: it never draws, fetches or mutates state, so a platform render pump can call it every display frame and skip draw when it answers true, letting the presented frame stand and resuming on any change or on the next pending detail’s arrival. # Returns True when a redraw would not change the presented frame. # Errors Throws RenderingSurfaceUnavailable when the view is detached.
setVectorTileSourcefunc setVectorTileSource(source: UrlTemplateVectorTileSource) throwsThrows SdkError.Installs a vector base map, a provider-neutral vector tileset painted with one of the SDK’s built-in styles, replacing any vector base already installed. The source is validated before anything moves (the template’s placeholders and scheme, the zoom range and the style id), so a refused call keeps the previously installed base in force. Each frame resolves the camera’s visible tiles through one shared scheduler: a tile is fetched and decoded once and restyled from its cached geometry when the style changes or the camera crosses a style zoom stop, never refetched for either. The styled base draws over the raster tiles and beneath the overlay list. A tile that fails to fetch or decode is skipped and counted; it never fails the frame. Configuring a base needs no attached surface: like the overlay list, the source outlives attach and detach cycles. # Parameters - source — the tileset, attribution and style. # Errors Throws when the source is invalid or a frame draw is in flight; install after the frame draws.
clearVectorTileSourcefunc clearVectorTileSource() throwsThrows SdkError.Removes the vector base map; following frames draw raster tiles and overlays alone until set_vector_tile_source installs a new base. Like installing, this throws while a frame draw is in flight. # Errors Throws when a frame draw is in flight.
vectorTileSourceStatusfunc vectorTileSourceStatus() -> VectorTileSourceStatusReturns VectorTileSourceStatus.Reads the vector base source’s status: the configured source and style plus the last resolved frame’s drawn and failed tile counts. A pure query that never fetches or draws; it answers while a frame is in flight with the previous frame’s counts. It never throws: with no source installed it answers a not-configured status.

PositionController

Validates and smooths one host’s position stream.

The host owns the operating system’s location API and its permission prompt, and reports the resulting fixes and failures here. The controller validates each fix, ignores stationary repeats when smoothing course, tracks staleness and records source failures, so the renderer’s location indicator, a follow camera and the navigation controller read one consistent stream.

RasterTileData

One fetched web-mercator XYZ raster tile.

UrlTemplateRasterTileSource

One provider-neutral base-map tile source: a web-mercator XYZ raster tileset addressed by a {z}/{x}/{y} URL template.

The SDK supplies no tile source of its own; you provide the URL template and the tileset’s terms. Every field is validated when the source is registered, so a malformed template or an inverted zoom range throws instead of failing on the first tile.

FieldTypePurpose
urlTemplateStringThe {z}/{x}/{y} URL template the tileset publishes: an absolute http/https URL carrying those three placeholders and no other.
sourceNameStringThe tileset’s name, used verbatim in every diagnostic it raises.
minimumZoomLevelUInt8Lowest zoom level the tileset serves.
maximumZoomLevelUInt8Highest zoom level the tileset serves.
imageFormatRasterImageFormatThe image format the tileset serves. Fetched tiles report this format whatever the caller requests: the tile bytes are the truth, and the renderer decodes by the record it receives.
tileResolutionRasterTileResolutionThe pixel resolution the tileset serves (the same rule as the format: the fetched tile reports what it contains).
userAgentStringThe User-Agent header every tile request carries; empty sends none. A public tile service identifies its clients by it, and several usage policies refuse clients that send nothing.

UrlTemplateVectorTileSource

One provider-neutral vector base-map source: a web-mercator XYZ vector tileset addressed by a {z}/{x}/{y} URL template, painted with one of the SDK’s built-in styles.

The SDK supplies no tile source or style list of its own; you provide the URL template, the attribution its terms require and the style id. The style is named by an id such as bright-light, fiord-dark or positron-light, and an unknown id throws here rather than on the first frame. Every field is validated when the source is installed, so a malformed template or an inverted zoom range throws instead of failing on the first tile.

Draw order: while installed, the styled base replaces the raster tiles, and it paints beneath every overlay the view is asked to draw, so your markers, routes and location indicator stay above the base map.

The built-in styles paint fills, lines and circles only; place labels and road shields are not rendered.

FieldTypePurpose
urlTemplateStringThe {z}/{x}/{y} URL template the tileset publishes: an absolute http/https URL carrying those three placeholders and no other.
sourceNameStringThe tileset’s name, used verbatim in every diagnostic it raises.
attributionTextStringThe attribution line the tileset’s terms require wherever it is shown; the status readback reports it back for your UI to display.
styleIdStringThe built-in style id the base paints with.
minimumZoomLevelUInt8Lowest zoom level the tileset serves.
maximumZoomLevelUInt8Highest zoom level the tileset serves.

VectorTileSourceStatus

FieldTypePurpose

MapOverlay

One overlay shape drawn over the map surface’s tiles in every frame, selected by kind. Each kind reads exactly its own payload fields and ignores the others. A descriptor whose kind-required payload is absent, or whose style field is unusable, rejects the whole set_overlays call and keeps the previous list in force. Absent style fields keep the documented default style; present style fields must be usable (channels in [0, 1], widths and radii positive and finite).

SurfaceHandle

The platform window surface handle handed to MapView::attach: set exactly one platform pointer and leave the rest null. A null-or-ambiguous handle is refused with InvalidRenderInput; a null pointer is u64 0 or null, never a zeroed pointer passed through.

The object behind the pointer must outlive the attached view: the raw handles are the caller’s validity guarantee, and detach or drop releases the SDK side first, so dropping the platform view before detach is a caller bug.

FieldTypePurpose

androidNativeWindowPointerUInt64?Android: pointer to the ANativeWindow obtained from the platform Surface (ANativeWindow_fromSurface); null on the other platforms.

NavigationPhase

High-level phase of a trip that has already been started. Rerouting is not a phase of its own: the controller moves Navigating to OffRoute and back within a trip, and Navigating to Arrived at its end.

VariantPurpose

DeviationGradeKind

Which grade of deviation a recorded deviation carries: the distinction between off the current step yet still on the route line, and completely off the route. Only the fully-off grade holds navigation; the wrong-step grade never does on its own.

VariantPurpose
fullyOffRouteThe fix projects onto neither the current step nor any future step of the remaining route line: the holding grade. The trip’s progress is held until a graded fix recovers or a reroute replaces the route.
offStepOnRouteThe fix is off the current step but projects onto a future step of the remaining route line: “on route, wrong step”. The trip keeps navigating and counting down, and is never held by this grade alone.

Which form a distance phrase takes.

VariantPurpose

Errors

SdkError

Failures returned by the SDK. The detail message of a variant is always passed through verbatim from the failing component.

Each variant is a case of the SdkError enum.

VariantPayloadPurpose
invalidCoordinateInputdetail: StringA coordinate, viewport extent or box corner failed validation.
networkRequestFaileddetail: StringThe network transport failed; carries the transport’s verbatim detail.
responseParsingFailuredetail: StringThe provider answered with a payload the parser could not use.
providerRequestRejecteddetail: StringThe provider returned a documented application-level failure status.
rateLimitExhaustedNoneThe token-bucket rate limiter is exhausted; retry after the next refill.
providerNotConfiguredcontractName: StringNo provider implementation is registered for the requested contract.
invalidNavigationInputdetail: StringA navigation input (a route record or a navigation policy) failed validation.
invalidRenderInputdetail: StringAn overlay descriptor did not describe a usable overlay (wrong kind payload, an out-of-range color channel, or a non-positive or non-finite width or radius), or a surface input was structurally unusable (a null, zero or ambiguous platform surface pointer, or a non-positive viewport extent).
renderingSurfaceUnavailabledetail: StringLive rendering could not proceed on the platform surface: the platform handle or surface was unusable, the graphics context could not be acquired, the surface format could not be negotiated or configured, the frame texture could not be acquired, or the frame’s render state was busy in another draw.
cacheOperationFailuredetail: StringA cache read, write or eviction failed (an unavailable store, a corrupt entry, or a byte-budget refusal). The detail names the reason verbatim.
offlineRoutingFailuredetail: StringAn offline routing graph failed validation or could not be read: a truncated or foreign archive, an unsupported version, or a malformed section. The detail names the reason verbatim.

Async and threading

These calls are asynchronous on Swift: offlineRouteFromArchiveBytes, GeocodingProvider.forwardGeocode, GeocodingProvider.reverseGeocode, RasterTileProvider.fetchRasterTile, MapSdk.forwardGeocode, MapSdk.reverseGeocode, MapSdk.calculateRoute, MapSdk.calculateDistanceMatrix, MapSdk.suggest, MapSdk.search, MapSdk.fetchTrafficIncidents, MapSdk.fetchTrafficFlow, MapSdk.fetchRasterTile, MapView.draw, SearchEngine.search, SearchEngine.suggest, SearchEngine.reverseGeocode, RoutingEngine.calculateRoute, RoutingEngine.calculateDistanceMatrix.

Asynchronous calls are async throws functions and do not block the calling thread. The shipped map view members expect the main thread.

  • MapView.draw is frame-driven: call it from the platform display callback. A concurrent draw or resize reports RenderingSurfaceUnavailable; retry the next frame.
  • Navigation listener callbacks run synchronously on the thread that drives the controller. A listener must not block, and a callback made during an in-flight dispatch has its broadcast suppressed because the state change is already applied.
  • A diagnostics listener is called fire-and-forget on the thread that produced the event; it never delays the event stream.

React Native API reference

Generated from the SDK contract and the generated React Native bindings. Do not edit this page by hand; change the contract and regenerate the documentation.

The React Native package exposes the provider-neutral SDK through TypeScript bindings generated from the SDK contract, together with the shipped map component. This page documents every contract type and member the generated TypeScript surface exposes: what it does, how it is constructed, its parameters, its return value, the failures it raises, and its async and threading rules. The package MapsSdk handle and MapView component are described in the platform guides.

Returns Route. Throws SdkError.Calculates a route between two coordinates over an offline routing graph supplied as archive bytes. Interfaces

MapCamera

Anchored map camera: geographic center, zoom level, bearing and pitch. The ground point under the center always sits at the viewport center; zoom and pitch are clamped to their valid ranges and bearing wraps into [0, 360).

Construction

ConstructorSignaturePurpose
constructorconstructor(center: GeographicCoordinate, zoomLevel: number, bearingDegrees: number, pitchDegrees: number)Builds a camera at the given center, zoom level, bearing and pitch. # Parameters - center — geographic point placed at the viewport center. - zoom_level — zoom level, clamped to the valid range. - bearing_degrees — clockwise rotation from north, wrapped into [0, 360). - pitch_degrees — tilt from straight down, clamped to the valid range. # Errors Throws InvalidCoordinateInput when the center is not a valid coordinate or when a numeric argument is not finite.
fitBoundsstatic fitBounds(boundingBox: BoundingBox, viewport: ViewportSize, edgeInsets: EdgeInsets, maximumZoomLevel: number): MapCameraBuilds the camera that frames a bounding box inside the viewport’s inset region: top-down and north-up by construction (pitch and bearing zero), zoomed to the largest level keeping the whole box inside the inset area and clamped to maximum_zoom_level; the center is anchored on the inset region’s center. # Parameters - bounding_box — the area to frame. - viewport — viewport extent in pixels. - edge_insets — pixels kept clear on each viewport edge. - maximum_zoom_level — upper zoom bound for the fitted camera. # Errors Throws when the insets or the maximum zoom are not finite usable values, when the insets are negative or leave no inset area, or when the box spans no positive world area.

visibleTileKeysvisibleTileKeys(viewport: ViewportSize, fieldOfViewDegrees: number, tileZoomLevel: number): TileKey[]Returns TileKey[]. Throws SdkError.Lists every tile at tile_zoom_level whose area intersects the visible ground, sorted row-major from the north. # Parameters - viewport — viewport extent in pixels. - field_of_view_degrees — vertical field of view of the projection. - tile_zoom_level — zoom level of the listed tiles. # Errors Throws InvalidCoordinateInput for an invalid viewport.
tileZoomLeveltileZoomLevel(): numberReturns number.Nearest whole zoom level a tile fetch should use for this camera.
panByScreenPixelspanByScreenPixels(deltaXPixels: number, deltaYPixels: number, viewport: ViewportSize, fieldOfViewDegrees: number): MapCameraReturns MapCamera. Throws SdkError.Pans by a pointer travel of delta_x_pixels x delta_y_pixels (screen pixels, x right / y down): the ground point the pointer just moved over becomes the new camera center, so map content tracks the pointer exactly. Answers the camera unchanged when the delta’s ground ray misses the plane (above the horizon at steep pitch). Gesture recognition stays in your UI layer; this call performs the camera math. # Parameters - delta_x_pixels — horizontal pointer travel in pixels. - delta_y_pixels — vertical pointer travel in pixels. - viewport — viewport extent in pixels. - field_of_view_degrees — vertical field of view of the projection. # Errors Throws InvalidCoordinateInput when the viewport extent is not positive.
zoomByLevelsAroundScreenPointzoomByLevelsAroundScreenPoint(deltaZoomLevels: number, focalPoint: ScreenPoint, viewport: ViewportSize, fieldOfViewDegrees: number): MapCameraReturns MapCamera. Throws SdkError.Zooms by delta_zoom_levels (levels; positive zooms in) keeping the world point under focal_point fixed under it. Answers the zoom without the focal correction when the focal ray misses the ground plane (above the horizon at steep pitch). Zoom clamps to the camera’s own level range before the focal correction applies, so a clamped zoom still holds the focal point. # Parameters - delta_zoom_levels — zoom change in levels. - focal_point — screen pixel that stays fixed during the zoom. - viewport — viewport extent in pixels. - field_of_view_degrees — vertical field of view of the projection. # Errors Throws InvalidCoordinateInput when the viewport extent is not positive.
rotateByDegreesAroundScreenPointrotateByDegreesAroundScreenPoint(deltaBearingDegrees: number, focalPoint: ScreenPoint, viewport: ViewportSize, fieldOfViewDegrees: number): MapCameraReturns MapCamera. Throws SdkError.Rotates the bearing by delta_bearing_degrees (degrees clockwise, wrapping into [0, 360)) keeping the world point under focal_point fixed under it. Answers the rotation without the focal correction when the focal ray misses the ground plane, which produces the touch-point turn a two-finger gesture implies. # Parameters - delta_bearing_degrees — bearing change in degrees. - focal_point — screen pixel that stays fixed during the rotation. - viewport — viewport extent in pixels. - field_of_view_degrees — vertical field of view of the projection. # Errors Throws InvalidCoordinateInput when the viewport extent is not positive.
centercenter(): GeographicCoordinateReturns GeographicCoordinate.Reads the camera’s state back as it was constructed. The getters make the framing chosen by fit_bounds readable: the fitted zoom level, its anchored center, and the constructed bearing and pitch. Read-only: the camera has no setters, so a new pose is a new camera.
zoomLevelzoomLevel(): numberReturns number.The camera’s zoom level.
bearingDegreesbearingDegrees(): numberReturns number.The camera’s bearing in degrees clockwise from north, within [0, 360).
pitchDegreespitchDegrees(): numberReturns number.The camera’s pitch in degrees.
groundMetersPerScreenPixelgroundMetersPerScreenPixel(viewport: ViewportSize, fieldOfViewDegrees: number): numberReturns number. Throws SdkError.Ground meters represented by one screen pixel at the camera’s center: the equatorial ground meters per pixel at the camera’s zoom level times the cosine of the center latitude, so the answer shrinks toward the poles exactly like the projected ground. At any nonzero pitch this is an approximation valid at the viewport’s center column: the value is computed for a flat center and does not fold pitch into the answer. # Parameters - viewport — viewport extent in pixels. - field_of_view_degrees — vertical field of view of the projection. # Errors Throws InvalidCoordinateInput for an invalid viewport.

MapSdk

Provider entry point of the SDK: resolves every call through the providers registered on the object. Construct the object with no providers, then register them: native integrations through the SDK’s own registration calls and foreign integrations through the register_*_from_foreign methods (see the provider contract interfaces above). A call into a contract with no registered provider throws ProviderNotConfigured naming the contract.

The calls cover geocoding (forward and reverse), routing, distance matrix, place search, traffic incidents, traffic flow and raster tiles. Elevation and offline routing have no provider contract here: offline routing is the standalone offline_route_from_archive_bytes function.

setProviderCredentialsetProviderCredential(credential: string): voidThrows SdkError.Registers the built-in MapQuest provider set from one consumer key, with the SDK defaults for base URL, rate limiting and retries. The call installs geocoding, routing, distance matrix, place search, traffic incidents, traffic flow and raster tiles, so one call and one key enable the whole provider set. Re-registration replaces every provider. Elevation has no provider and keeps throwing ProviderNotConfigured. # Parameters - credential — the provider consumer key. # Errors Throws SdkError when the credential is empty or the registration is refused.
setProviderCredentialWithTileCachesetProviderCredentialWithTileCache(mapquestApiKey: string, tileCacheDatabasePath: string, tileCacheAbsoluteMaximumBytes: bigint): voidThrows SdkError.Registers the built-in MapQuest provider set from one consumer key, exactly like set_provider_credential, and wraps the raster-tile provider in a disk response cache. The cache is a SQLite database opened (or created) at tile_cache_database_path and bounded by tile_cache_absolute_maximum_bytes. Cached tile responses follow the tiles category’s time-to-live (thirty days by default, the imagery provider’s terms ceiling); a cache miss goes to the network and back-fills the cache, so pre-warmed tiles keep rendering when the network is unavailable. Re-registration replaces the providers, including the cached raster-tile provider. # Parameters - mapquest_api_key — the provider consumer key. - tile_cache_database_path — non-empty absolute path of the cache database. - tile_cache_absolute_maximum_bytes — positive byte budget of the cache. # Errors Throws SdkError when the path is empty, the byte budget is not positive, or the cache cannot be opened or refuses the quota; the detail names the reason verbatim.
registerUrlTemplateRasterTileSourceregisterUrlTemplateRasterTileSource(source: UrlTemplateRasterTileSource): voidThrows SdkError.Registers a provider-neutral raster base map: any web-mercator XYZ tileset that publishes a {z}/{x}/{y} URL template. The registration replaces the raster-tile contract only; every other provider keeps serving. It also drops any installed tile cache, because the cache’s terms belong to the provider that installed it; a later raster_tile_cache_terms then throws the not-configured error rather than reporting another provider’s ceiling. Re-registering replaces the source. # Parameters - source — the tile source and its terms. # Errors A malformed template, a blank source name or an inverted zoom range throws InvalidCoordinateInput with a precise detail, and the previous source keeps serving.
setRasterTileCacheTimeToLivesetRasterTileCacheTimeToLive(timeToLiveSeconds: bigint): voidThrows SdkError.Overrides the installed raster-tile cache’s time-to-live in seconds. A zero value is refused, because it would expire every entry on capture and store nothing. A value above the installed provider’s declared terms ceiling is accepted, and the ceiling clamps what the cache stores; raster_tile_cache_terms reports the effective value. # Parameters - time_to_live_seconds — requested time-to-live. # Errors Throws ProviderNotConfigured when no tile cache is installed, naming TileCache as the unconfigured backing store, and InvalidCoordinateInput for a zero time-to-live.
rasterTileCacheTermsrasterTileCacheTerms(): TileCacheTermsReturns TileCacheTerms. Throws SdkError.Reads the effective raster-tile caching terms of the installed cache, for display on a settings page. Reports the time-to-live currently in force (the category default, or the last accepted override clamped to the provider’s ceiling), the provider’s declared ceiling, and the category default. Read-only: the readback never mutates the cache. # Errors Throws ProviderNotConfigured when no tile cache is installed, naming TileCache as the unconfigured backing store.
subscribeToDiagnosticEventssubscribeToDiagnosticEvents(listener: SdkDiagnosticEventListener, minimumSeverity: SdkLogSeverity): void—Subscribes listener to the SDK’s structured log events. Only events at minimum_severity or above are delivered. Coordinates inside event messages are rounded before delivery, and API keys are never included. Listener callbacks run on the threads that produce the events and must not block. Subscribing an already subscribed listener replaces its severity threshold. # Parameters - listener — the diagnostics listener. - minimum_severity — lowest severity delivered.
flushRecentDiagnosticEventsflushRecentDiagnosticEvents(listener: SdkDiagnosticEventListener, minimumSeverity: SdkLogSeverity, maximumCount: number): numberReturns number.Delivers up to maximum_count of the most recent buffered events at minimum_severity or above to the listener, oldest first, and returns how many were delivered. The flush does not remove events, so a later flush can deliver them again. The flush is bounded and synchronous; the listener must not block. # Parameters - listener — the diagnostics listener. - minimum_severity — lowest severity delivered. - maximum_count — upper bound on delivered events. # Returns The number of events delivered.
latestProviderFailureDiagnosticslatestProviderFailureDiagnostics(): ProviderFailureDiagnostic[]Returns ProviderFailureDiagnostic[].Returns the retained diagnostics of failed provider calls made by foreign provider implementations, oldest first. A failure is recorded whether the implementation threw one of the contract’s SdkError variants or failed without a mapped error. The buffer keeps a bounded number of the most recent failures and drops older ones. Reading is non-destructive: the call neither records nor clears entries. The typed error still surfaces at the failing call; this readback lets a failure be classified after the fact. See ProviderFailureDiagnostic for the fields of an entry. # Returns The retained entries, oldest first.

NavigationListener

Navigation event listener. Implement this interface and subscribe it on Navigator; each subscription delivers only the topic it was registered for.

Threading Callbacks run synchronously on the thread that drives the controller and must not block. A callback that calls back into the controller while a dispatch is in flight is suppressed: the state change behind it is already applied, and only its broadcast is skipped.

Implement this interface in TypeScript; the SDK invokes it through the matching registration or subscription method.

Members

MemberSignatureReturns / errorsPurpose
onNavigationInstructiononNavigationInstruction(instruction: NavigationInstruction): void—Receives the composed instruction payload of every dispatched state change (the instructions topic).
onDeviationStatusChangeonDeviationStatusChange(deviationStatusChange: DeviationStatusChange): void—Receives a deviation-status update (the deviation topic): off route on entry and on every recorded measurement update while the deviation persists, and on route when it clears.
onNavigationPhaseChangeonNavigationPhaseChange(navigationPhaseChange: NavigationPhaseChange): void—Receives one phase transition per dispatched trip-state transition (the phase topic).
onSpeechInstructiononSpeechInstruction(speechInstruction: SpeechInstruction): void—Receives one utterance trigger when the controller’s distance-band policy judges the current fix newsworthy, for example when a trigger band is crossed. The text is the composed speech text, verbatim and never rewritten; playback and speech synthesis remain the application’s responsibility.

Subscription

Handle for exactly one (topic, listener) subscription. Cancelling is explicit and idempotent; dropping the handle does not unsubscribe.

Members

MemberSignatureReturns / errorsPurpose
cancelcancel(): void—Cancels this subscription, so the listener stops receiving the subscription’s topic from the next dispatch on. Idempotent.

Navigator

The navigation controller: starts and stops trips, accepts position fixes and reroutes, broadcasts every state change to the registered listeners, and answers read-only state and instruction queries. Obtain routes from MapSdk::calculate_route or offline_route_from_archive_bytes and start a trip on them with this controller.

The listener callbacks run synchronously on the thread that drives the controller call; a listener calling back into the controller while a dispatch is still in flight is suppressed, and only the broadcast is skipped. The controller never holds its state lock across a listener callback.

Construction

ConstructorSignaturePurpose
constructorconstructor()Builds the controller with no active trip and no subscriptions.

Members

MemberSignatureReturns / errorsPurpose
subscribeToNavigationInstructionssubscribeToNavigationInstructions(listener: NavigationListener): SubscriptionReturns Subscription.Subscribes the listener to the instructions topic: the composed instruction payload of every dispatched state change, in registration order.
subscribeToDeviationStatussubscribeToDeviationStatus(listener: NavigationListener): SubscriptionReturns Subscription.Subscribes the listener to the deviation-status topic, in registration order.
subscribeToPhaseChangessubscribeToPhaseChanges(listener: NavigationListener): SubscriptionReturns Subscription.Subscribes the listener to the phase-transition topic, in registration order.
startNavigationstartNavigation(route: Route, unitSystem: UnitSystem, stepAdvancePolicy: StepAdvancePolicy, deviationPolicy: DeviationPolicy): voidThrows SdkError.Begins navigating route with the given policies, replacing any active trip. The initial instruction payload is dispatched; no deviation or phase transitions exist yet. A route without traversable steps represents an already-arrived trip. # Parameters - route — the route to navigate. - unit_system — units used in composed instruction text. - step_advance_policy — step-advance strategy and thresholds. - deviation_policy — off-route detection thresholds. # Errors Throws InvalidNavigationInput for policies with non-finite or negative thresholds, or for a route whose step maneuver label the SDK does not recognize.
updateLocationupdateLocation(locationUpdate: NavigationLocationUpdate): void—Delivers one position fix to the active trip; without an active trip the fix is dropped. Fixes without an accuracy report never trigger a step advance and are never judged by the deviation detector.
applyRerouteapplyReroute(route: Route, stepAdvancePolicy: StepAdvancePolicy): voidThrows SdkError.Replaces the route of the active trip (a reroute). The replacement route must be anchored at the trip’s current snapped coordinate. The step-advance strategy for the new route is configured by step_advance_policy; the deviation policy persists. A reroute offered to an arrived trip is ignored, and without an active trip the event is dropped. An in-flight reroute calculation is settled by this call whether the route is applied or ignored, so the calculation gate reopens after the integrator acts. # Errors Throws InvalidNavigationInput for an invalid policy or an unrecognized maneuver label.
beginRerouteCalculationbeginRerouteCalculation(): booleanReturns boolean.Applies the reroute-recalculation gates to one reroute request. Returns true when every gate passes (no calculation in flight, outside the cooldown window and, when both fix references exist, beyond the movement threshold) and a calculation is marked as in flight, readable as the trip state’s is_calculating_new_route; returns false when the request is refused. A request without an open, still-navigable trip (no trip, or an arrived trip) is refused before the gates are consulted. A caller that receives true owes a settle: either the eventual apply_reroute (applied or ignored) or cancel_reroute_calculation. The trip’s first attempt always passes the cooldown and movement gates. # Returns True when the request passed the gates and a calculation is in flight.
cancelRerouteCalculationcancelRerouteCalculation(): void—Settles an in-flight reroute calculation without applying a route, for example when the integrator abandons the request. The calculation gate reopens; the cooldown keeps running from the calculation’s beginning and the movement reference stays where it was. Idempotent.
configureReroutePolicyconfigureReroutePolicy(reroutePolicy: ReroutePolicy): voidThrows SdkError.Replaces the reroute-recalculation hysteresis policy in force, keeping the gate’s recorded state. # Parameters - reroute_policy — cooldown and movement thresholds. # Errors Throws InvalidNavigationInput when a threshold is not finite or is negative; the policy in force is then untouched.
currentTripStatecurrentTripState(): TripNavigationState | undefinedReturns TripNavigationState | undefined.The state of the active trip, or null without one.
currentInstructionscurrentInstructions(): NavigationInstruction | undefinedReturns NavigationInstruction | undefined.The composed turn-by-turn instruction payload of the current trip state, or null without an active trip. Repeated reads of an unchanged state return the same payload.
subscribeToSpeechInstructionssubscribeToSpeechInstructions(listener: NavigationListener): SubscriptionReturns Subscription.Subscribes the listener to the speech-instruction trigger topic, in registration order. The controller decides when a line is worth speaking. Trigger bands reuse the display phrase’s distance bands, so a spoken “in 100 meters” matches the phrase shown in the payload; each band announces at most once per step, and a minimum inter-utterance spacing and repeat distance suppress chatter. Speech synthesis and playback remain the application’s responsibility.
addNavigationListeneraddNavigationListener(listener: NavigationListener): SubscriptionReturns Subscription.Subscribes one listener to all four navigation topics (instructions, deviation status, phase changes and speech instructions) in one call and answers the composite subscription that cancels all four. Delivery semantics match the four individual subscribe_to_* calls: the listener receives each topic on its own method, in registration order, and cancel() removes every one of the four registrations (idempotent, like a single-topic subscription).
stopNavigationstopNavigation(): void—Ends the active trip and clears the trip state: after this call current_trip_state and current_instructions answer null, and location updates, reroutes and reroute requests are dropped until start_navigation begins a new trip. The speech-trigger band memory and the reroute-recalculation gate are reset with the trip; utterance identifiers stay monotonic across the stop and the configured reroute policy persists. Listener subscriptions are untouched and keep delivering the next trip’s events. Stopping without an active trip is a no-op.

MapView

The native map surface view: renders the camera-driven tiled map plus the overlay list onto a live platform window surface. Construct it with the MapSdk whose registered raster-tile provider the attached surface draws from; the provider is resolved at attach time, so with no registered provider attach throws ProviderNotConfigured.

Lifecycle

attach wraps the platform handle, acquires the surface-compatible graphics context, negotiates the surface format, configures the initial extent and resolves the tile provider. Each step’s failure throws: RenderingSurfaceUnavailable for the GPU or surface path, InvalidRenderInput for a bad handle or extent, and ProviderNotConfigured for the missing provider. resize, called from the platform’s surface-size callback, reconfigures the surface and rejects a zero extent. detach releases the surface state until a re-attach.

Overlay state outlives attach and detach cycles: set_overlays, add_overlay, update_overlay, remove_overlay and clear_overlays all work detached, and the next attach draws the stored list. Generated overlay identifiers also survive detach and attach, so an overlay added while detached stays addressable.

Draw model

Frames are explicit: the platform view calls draw once per rendered frame from its own cadence (a display link, a choreographer, or a resize-then-once pattern) with the current MapCamera. The SDK runs no internal render thread and no continuous redraw loop. Each draw lists the camera’s visible tiles, fetches pooled misses from the surface-attached provider within a per-frame budget, and renders tiles then overlays alpha-blended, presenting to the surface. A failed frame throws and leaves the previous frame on screen.

Draws on one view are serialized: a draw holding the view’s render state reports a concurrent draw or resize with RenderingSurfaceUnavailable, and the platform cadence retries on the next frame.

Construction

ConstructorSignaturePurpose
constructorconstructor(mapSdk: MapSdk)Builds the view over the SDK state it draws from.

attachattach(surfaceHandle: SurfaceHandle, widthPixels: number, heightPixels: number): voidThrows SdkError.Attaches the platform surface at the given initial physical-pixel extent. The extent must be non-zero; a platform view that is not laid out yet waits for resize. The call validates the handle, acquires the graphics context, negotiates the format, configures the surface and resolves the raster provider. Attaching an already attached view is refused. # Parameters - surface_handle — exactly one platform pointer. - width_pixels — initial surface width in physical pixels. - height_pixels — initial surface height in physical pixels. # Errors Throws InvalidRenderInput for a bad handle or a zero extent, RenderingSurfaceUnavailable for a GPU or surface failure, and ProviderNotConfigured when no raster-tile provider is registered.
