A resize during a draw reports the busy state, and the next draw or resize picks up the new extent. # Errors Throws InvalidRenderInput for a zero extent and RenderingSurfaceUnavailable when a draw owns the surface.
setDevicePixelRatiosetDevicePixelRatio(devicePixelRatio: number): voidThrows SdkError.Sets the drawing buffer’s device pixels per point or CSS pixel, so labels and overlay screen sizes keep their declared point size on a 2x or 3x surface. The built-in styles declare point sizes while the surface draws device pixels; each draw multiplies every placed glyph size, route and traffic line width, and marker and pin radius by this ratio exactly once. The ratio outlives attach and detach cycles like the overlay list. The default is 1.0 until your platform code reports the surface’s own. # Parameters - device_pixel_ratio — device pixels per point. # Errors Throws InvalidRenderInput for a non-finite or non-positive ratio; the previous ratio stays in force.
detachdetach(): void—Detaches: releases the surface, its renderer and its scheduler. Overlay state persists, and re-attach rebuilds the drawing machinery. Safe against a draw still in flight; that frame completes and the state is then dropped without being restored.
setOverlayssetOverlays(overlayDescriptors: MapOverlay[]): voidThrows SdkError.Replaces the drawn overlay list in one call, in order (later entries draw over earlier ones); an empty list clears. Every descriptor must be valid for its kind, and no partial list is kept. This call replaces the whole drawn list, including overlays added through add_overlay, and drops the addressed bookkeeping, so an identifier returned by add_overlay before this call no longer addresses anything afterwards. Use it for a list owned whole, and add_overlay, update_overlay and remove_overlay for individually managed overlays; a later add_overlay appends to the replaced list and works alongside its unaddressed entries. # Errors Throws InvalidRenderInput when any descriptor is invalid; the previous list stays in force.
addOverlayaddOverlay(overlay: MapOverlay): stringReturns string. Throws SdkError.Adds one overlay to the drawn list and returns the generated opaque identifier that addresses it, such as overlay-1. Identifiers come from a monotonic per-view sequence and are never reused, not even after clear_overlays or set_overlays. Validation matches set_overlays’ all-or-nothing rule for the single descriptor: a refused descriptor throws and adds nothing, leaving the drawn list and the identifier sequence unchanged. The new overlay draws last, over the entries already in the list. # Returns The identifier addressing the added overlay. # Errors Throws InvalidRenderInput when the descriptor is invalid.
updateOverlayupdateOverlay(overlayIdentifier: string, overlay: MapOverlay): voidThrows SdkError.Replaces the overlay addressed by overlay_identifier. # Parameters - overlay_identifier — an identifier returned by add_overlay. - overlay — the replacement descriptor. # Errors Throws InvalidRenderInput for an unknown identifier (never generated, invalidated by a later set_overlays or clear_overlays, or already removed), with a detail naming the reason. An invalid descriptor throws and keeps the previously addressed overlay in force.
removeOverlayremoveOverlay(overlayIdentifier: string): booleanReturns boolean.Removes the overlay addressed by overlay_identifier and answers whether that identifier was present. Removing an unknown identifier is not an error: it answers false and leaves the drawn list unchanged. # Returns True when the identifier was present and its overlay was removed.
clearOverlaysclearOverlays(): void—Clears the whole drawn overlay list, including the list supplied through set_overlays and every added addressed overlay, so following frames draw the tiles alone until set_overlays or add_overlay supplies new content. Identifiers generated earlier no longer address anything afterwards.
drawasync draw(camera: MapCamera, asyncOpts_?: { signal: AbortSignal }): Promise<FrameStatistics>Asynchronous. Returns FrameStatistics. Throws SdkError.Draws one frame for the camera: the camera’s visible tiles fetched and rendered, then overlaid and presented. # Parameters - camera — the camera pose for this frame. # Returns The frame’s tile and overlay statistics, so the platform render loop can report exactly what a frame drew. Drawn pixels this frame come from present and fallback tiles, while the deferred and unavailable counts mark where later frames may still change pixels. # Errors Throws when the view is detached, a draw is already in flight, or the frame’s rendering failed. A thrown draw leaves the previous frame on screen. # Async Runs asynchronously; the call does not block the calling thread.
setLocationIndicatorsetLocationIndicator(state: LocationIndicatorState, style: LocationIndicatorStyle): voidThrows SdkError.Sets the single location layer drawn after the tile pass and the overlay pass (topmost SDK layer), replacing any earlier state. Validation is all-or-nothing: a state or style that fails validation throws and keeps the earlier indicator. The state outlives attach and detach cycles like the overlay list. Every null style field resolves to the documented default. # Parameters - state — position, course and accuracy to draw. - style — visual form and style of the layer. # Errors Throws InvalidRenderInput for a state or style the layer cannot draw.
clearLocationIndicatorclearLocationIndicator(): void—Clears the location layer; following frames draw tiles and overlays alone until set_location_indicator supplies new state.
isFrameSettledisFrameSettled(camera: MapCamera): booleanReturns boolean. Throws SdkError.Reads whether the view’s presented state would not change if draw ran again right now. Answers true when this camera value equals the last drawn camera, the overlay list and the location indicator are unchanged since that draw, and the last frame’s tile statistics resolved no pending pixels (no fallback, deferred or unavailable tiles). It answers false while a draw is in flight and before a frame has ever drawn. A pure query: it never draws, fetches or mutates state, so a platform render pump can call it every display frame and skip draw when it answers true, letting the presented frame stand and resuming on any change or on the next pending detail’s arrival. # Returns True when a redraw would not change the presented frame. # Errors Throws RenderingSurfaceUnavailable when the view is detached.
setVectorTileSourcesetVectorTileSource(source: UrlTemplateVectorTileSource): voidThrows SdkError.Installs a vector base map, a provider-neutral vector tileset painted with one of the SDK’s built-in styles, replacing any vector base already installed. The source is validated before anything moves (the template’s placeholders and scheme, the zoom range and the style id), so a refused call keeps the previously installed base in force. Each frame resolves the camera’s visible tiles through one shared scheduler: a tile is fetched and decoded once and restyled from its cached geometry when the style changes or the camera crosses a style zoom stop, never refetched for either. The styled base draws over the raster tiles and beneath the overlay list. A tile that fails to fetch or decode is skipped and counted; it never fails the frame. Configuring a base needs no attached surface: like the overlay list, the source outlives attach and detach cycles. # Parameters - source — the tileset, attribution and style. # Errors Throws when the source is invalid or a frame draw is in flight; install after the frame draws.
clearVectorTileSourceclearVectorTileSource(): voidThrows SdkError.Removes the vector base map; following frames draw raster tiles and overlays alone until set_vector_tile_source installs a new base. Like installing, this throws while a frame draw is in flight. # Errors Throws when a frame draw is in flight.
vectorTileSourceStatusvectorTileSourceStatus(): VectorTileSourceStatusReturns VectorTileSourceStatus.Reads the vector base source’s status: the configured source and style plus the last resolved frame’s drawn and failed tile counts. A pure query that never fetches or draws; it answers while a frame is in flight with the previous frame’s counts. It never throws: with no source installed it answers a not-configured status.

SdkDiagnosticEventListener

Diagnostics listener contract. The SDK delivers its structured log events fire-and-forget: it copies an event and moves on immediately without awaiting the listener, so a slow listener can never slow the events it observes and a frame-path event never blocks on a foreign callback.

Implement this interface in TypeScript; the SDK invokes it through the matching registration or subscription method.

PositionController

Validates and smooths one host’s position stream.

The host owns the operating system’s location API and its permission prompt, and reports the resulting fixes and failures here. The controller validates each fix, ignores stationary repeats when smoothing course, tracks staleness and records source failures, so the renderer’s location indicator, a follow camera and the navigation controller read one consistent stream.

UrlTemplateRasterTileSource

One provider-neutral base-map tile source: a web-mercator XYZ raster tileset addressed by a {z}/{x}/{y} URL template.

The SDK supplies no tile source of its own; you provide the URL template and the tileset’s terms. Every field is validated when the source is registered, so a malformed template or an inverted zoom range throws instead of failing on the first tile.

FieldTypePurpose
urlTemplatestringThe {z}/{x}/{y} URL template the tileset publishes: an absolute http/https URL carrying those three placeholders and no other.
sourceNamestringThe tileset’s name, used verbatim in every diagnostic it raises.
minimumZoomLevelnumberLowest zoom level the tileset serves.
maximumZoomLevelnumberHighest zoom level the tileset serves.
imageFormatRasterImageFormatThe image format the tileset serves. Fetched tiles report this format whatever the caller requests: the tile bytes are the truth, and the renderer decodes by the record it receives.
tileResolutionRasterTileResolutionThe pixel resolution the tileset serves (the same rule as the format: the fetched tile reports what it contains).
userAgentstringThe User-Agent header every tile request carries; empty sends none. A public tile service identifies its clients by it, and several usage policies refuse clients that send nothing.

UrlTemplateVectorTileSource

One provider-neutral vector base-map source: a web-mercator XYZ vector tileset addressed by a {z}/{x}/{y} URL template, painted with one of the SDK’s built-in styles.

The SDK supplies no tile source or style list of its own; you provide the URL template, the attribution its terms require and the style id. The style is named by an id such as bright-light, fiord-dark or positron-light, and an unknown id throws here rather than on the first frame. Every field is validated when the source is installed, so a malformed template or an inverted zoom range throws instead of failing on the first tile.

Draw order: while installed, the styled base replaces the raster tiles, and it paints beneath every overlay the view is asked to draw, so your markers, routes and location indicator stay above the base map.

The built-in styles paint fills, lines and circles only; place labels and road shields are not rendered.

FieldTypePurpose
urlTemplatestringThe {z}/{x}/{y} URL template the tileset publishes: an absolute http/https URL carrying those three placeholders and no other.
sourceNamestringThe tileset’s name, used verbatim in every diagnostic it raises.
attributionTextstringThe attribution line the tileset’s terms require wherever it is shown; the status readback reports it back for your UI to display.
styleIdstringThe built-in style id the base paints with.
minimumZoomLevelnumberLowest zoom level the tileset serves.
maximumZoomLevelnumberHighest zoom level the tileset serves.

MapOverlay

One overlay shape drawn over the map surface’s tiles in every frame, selected by kind. Each kind reads exactly its own payload fields and ignores the others. A descriptor whose kind-required payload is absent, or whose style field is unusable, rejects the whole set_overlays call and keeps the previous list in force. Absent style fields keep the documented default style; present style fields must be usable (channels in [0, 1], widths and radii positive and finite).

FieldTypePurpose

SurfaceHandle

The platform window surface handle handed to MapView::attach: set exactly one platform pointer and leave the rest null. A null-or-ambiguous handle is refused with InvalidRenderInput; a null pointer is u64 0 or null, never a zeroed pointer passed through.

The object behind the pointer must outlive the attached view: the raw handles are the caller’s validity guarantee, and detach or drop releases the SDK side first, so dropping the platform view before detach is a caller bug.

FieldTypePurpose

High-level phase of a trip that has already been started. Rerouting is not a phase of its own: the controller moves Navigating to OffRoute and back within a trip, and Navigating to Arrived at its end.

VariantPurpose
NavigatingFollowing the route’s step sequence.

ArrivedThe final step has been completed; location updates no longer change the state.

DeviationGradeKind

Which grade of deviation a recorded deviation carries: the distinction between off the current step yet still on the route line, and completely off the route. Only the fully-off grade holds navigation; the wrong-step grade never does on its own.

VariantPurpose
FullyOffRouteThe fix projects onto neither the current step nor any future step of the remaining route line: the holding grade. The trip’s progress is held until a graded fix recovers or a reroute replaces the route.
OffStepOnRouteThe fix is off the current step but projects onto a future step of the remaining route line: “on route, wrong step”. The trip keeps navigating and counting down, and is never held by this grade alone.

VariantPurpose

MilesMiles, used by the imperial far band.

Which form a distance phrase takes.

VariantPurpose
ImmediateThe position is closer than half a near-band increment to the maneuver point; no distance is phrased and composed text drops the prefix. The magnitude is null on this kind.

SuppressedNo distance is phrased because the holding (fully-off-route) deviation grade applies: the projection is held, so any countdown composed from it would be a phantom measurement. The magnitude is null on this kind, and the composed text channels carry no distance prefix.

Errors

SdkError

Failures returned by the SDK. The detail message of a variant is always passed through verbatim from the failing component.

Each variant is a tag of the SdkError class.

VariantPayloadPurpose
InvalidCoordinateInputdetail: stringA coordinate, viewport extent or box corner failed validation.
NetworkRequestFaileddetail: stringThe network transport failed; carries the transport’s verbatim detail.
ResponseParsingFailuredetail: stringThe provider answered with a payload the parser could not use.
ProviderRequestRejecteddetail: stringThe provider returned a documented application-level failure status.
RateLimitExhaustedNoneThe token-bucket rate limiter is exhausted; retry after the next refill.
ProviderNotConfiguredcontractName: stringNo provider implementation is registered for the requested contract.
InvalidNavigationInputdetail: stringA navigation input (a route record or a navigation policy) failed validation.
InvalidRenderInputdetail: stringAn overlay descriptor did not describe a usable overlay (wrong kind payload, an out-of-range color channel, or a non-positive or non-finite width or radius), or a surface input was structurally unusable (a null, zero or ambiguous platform surface pointer, or a non-positive viewport extent).
RenderingSurfaceUnavailabledetail: stringLive rendering could not proceed on the platform surface: the platform handle or surface was unusable, the graphics context could not be acquired, the surface format could not be negotiated or configured, the frame texture could not be acquired, or the frame’s render state was busy in another draw.
CacheOperationFailuredetail: stringA cache read, write or eviction failed (an unavailable store, a corrupt entry, or a byte-budget refusal). The detail names the reason verbatim.
OfflineRoutingFailuredetail: stringAn offline routing graph failed validation or could not be read: a truncated or foreign archive, an unsupported version, or a malformed section. The detail names the reason verbatim.

Async and threading

These calls are asynchronous on TypeScript: offlineRouteFromArchiveBytes, GeocodingProvider.forwardGeocode, GeocodingProvider.reverseGeocode, RasterTileProvider.fetchRasterTile, MapSdk.forwardGeocode, MapSdk.reverseGeocode, MapSdk.calculateRoute, MapSdk.calculateDistanceMatrix, MapSdk.suggest, MapSdk.search, MapSdk.fetchTrafficIncidents, MapSdk.fetchTrafficFlow, MapSdk.fetchRasterTile, MapView.draw, SearchEngine.search, SearchEngine.suggest, SearchEngine.reverseGeocode, RoutingEngine.calculateRoute, RoutingEngine.calculateDistanceMatrix.

Asynchronous calls return a Promise and accept an optional AbortSignal; they do not block the JavaScript thread.

  • MapView.draw is frame-driven: call it from the platform display callback. A concurrent draw or resize reports RenderingSurfaceUnavailable; retry the next frame.
  • Navigation listener callbacks run synchronously on the thread that drives the controller. A listener must not block, and a callback made during an in-flight dispatch has its broadcast suppressed because the state change is already applied.
  • A diagnostics listener is called fire-and-forget on the thread that produced the event; it never delays the event stream.

WebAssembly API reference

Generated from the SDK contract and the generated WebAssembly bindings. Do not edit this page by hand; change the contract and regenerate the documentation.

The WebAssembly package gives a browser page a WebGPU map canvas, camera math, search and routing calls, an offline routing seam, diagnostics and a turn-by-turn controller. There is no native view: you supply an HTMLCanvasElement, and the canvas owns the surface and the frame. Values cross the boundary as plain JavaScript objects in camelCase; failures are thrown as verbatim strings.

Before you start

RequirementValue
BrowserWebGPU: Chromium 113 or newer, Safari 26 or newer, Firefox 141 or newer
Package@angoratek/rustic-maps-sdk-web
Modulemap_web_bindings.js with its .d.ts and .wasm
ServingA static server over HTTPS or localhost
Provider credentialPassed at runtime; never bundled

MapsSdk

The browser SDK root (MapsSdk.create()): the object a page creates once and hands to its [crate::canvas::MapView], mirroring the native MapSdk construction shape. The wasm runtime is module-global, so this root carries the readiness result and the compiled version rather than a second runtime; provider and engine members will hang off it as the wasm seam grows.

Properties

PropertyTypePurpose
compiledVersionstringThe compiled SDK version (the workspace package version).

Members

MemberSignatureReturns / errorsPurpose
createstatic async create(): Promise<MapsSdk>Asynchronous. Returns MapsSdk. Throws the verbatim failure message as a string.Creates the SDK root and resolves once the browser runtime is ready (the same work the legacy [start_sdk] performs). The returned root is what new MapView(canvas, maps) expects.

MapView

The browser GPU map canvas the page owns. Construct it over an HTMLCanvasElement, [MapView::initialize] it once (acquiring the adapter and device and building the tile pipeline), then call [MapView::render_frame] per wanted frame; each call re-schedules the visible tiles and redraws.

Construction

ConstructorSignaturePurpose
constructorconstructor(canvas: HTMLCanvasElement, maps: MapsSdk, tileResolution: TileResolution | null)Builds the canvas renderer over the page’s canvas element, bound to the SDK root it was created with (new MapView(canvas, maps)). The tile pixel resolution is optional: omitted, it follows the same device-pixel-ratio rule as retinaDevicePixelRatioThreshold(); supplied, it is honoured verbatim (the golden harness pins it). Fails when the element cannot host a GPU surface (for example after another context already claimed the element). Call [MapView::initialize] before the first [MapView::render_frame].

Properties

PropertyTypePurpose
sdkCompiledVersionstringCompiled version of the SDK root this view was constructed with.

Members

MemberSignatureReturns / errorsPurpose
initializeasync initialize(): Promise<string>Asynchronous. Returns string. Throws the verbatim failure message as a string.Acquires the adapter and device, picks the pass-through surface format, and builds the tile pipeline. Resolves to the adapter description (graphics backend and adapter name) for the page’s status line, or fails when no WebGPU adapter supports this canvas — the page then degrades to the 2D tile grid overlay. Never callable twice on the same canvas.
renderFrameasync renderFrame(camera: MapCamera, fieldOfViewDegrees: number): Promise<object>Asynchronous. Returns object. Throws the verbatim failure message as a string.Renders one map frame for the camera pose into the canvas, resolving freshly visible tiles from the same-origin /tiles route first. Resolves to a statistics object the page’s readout consumes: requestedTiles (tiles the camera listed at the fetch zoom), drawnTiles (tiles with pooled imagery over their span this frame), drawnFragments (draw quads after world-copy fragment splitting), missingTiles (requested tiles with no pooled imagery this frame), tileZoomLevel (the fetch zoom, clamped to the recorded fixtures), tileResolution (the resolution the frame’s fixtures were fetched and sampled at) and overlayTriangles (triangles in the cached world-space overlay layer drawn over the tiles this frame; zero without overlays; the GPU clips copies and near-plane fragments). With the raster tile layer hidden through [MapView::set_tile_layer_visible] the frame skips the whole tile pipeline and reports requestedTiles, drawnTiles, drawnFragments and missingTiles as zero while still presenting the overlay and indicator layers. The camera binding is consumed by value (the wasm-bindgen class parameter semantics); the page builds a fresh camera per changed pose, exactly as it already does. Two overlapping calls are a construction-time borrow violation — the page serializes its frames behind a busy flag and never overlaps.
stageParentTileasync stageParentTile(fallbackTileX: number, fallbackTileY: number, fallbackZoomLevel: number, parentTileX: number, parentTileY: number, parentZoomLevel: number): Promise<void>Asynchronous. Throws the verbatim failure message as a string.Stages a deliberate parent-fallback for one requested tile, mirroring the native golden image harness (fill_pool_and_prepare in map-rendering’s golden test): the fallback tile is evicted from the pool and marked unavailable forever, and its coarser parent’s recorded fixture is pooled instead, so the scheduler resolves the fallback tile as FallsBackTo { parent } every frame and the frame samples the parent texture. The committed golden frames were produced with the last visible scene tile resolved exactly this way, so the browser golden-compare page calls this before rendering a golden scene to reproduce the reference imagery byte-for-byte. Fetches the parent fixture from the same-origin /tiles route. A missing or undecodable parent fixture is an error, not a silent skip: the caller wants the fallback imagery or nothing. The parent coordinates must describe the fallback tile’s direct parent.
setOverlayssetOverlays(overlays: any[]): voidThrows the verbatim failure message as a string.Sets the overlay list drawn over the tiles in every following [MapView::render_frame], replacing any earlier list in order (later list entries draw over earlier ones); an empty array clears. Each entry is a plain JavaScript object describing one overlay shape, selected by its kind field: * {kind: "routePolyline", coordinates: [{latitude, longitude}...], color?, widthPixels?} — a routed path drawn as a thick line, * {kind: "filledPolygon", ringCoordinates: [{latitude, longitude}...], color?} — an ear-clip triangulated ring fill, * {kind: "pointMarkers", positions: [{latitude, longitude}...], color?, radiusPixels?} — screen-facing octagon markers, * {kind: "pointPins", positions: [{latitude, longitude}...], color?, radiusPixels?} — teardrop pins anchored at their tip with a hollow head center, * {kind: "trafficFlow", segments: [{shapeCoordinates: [{latitude, longitude}...], congestionLevel: CanvasTrafficFlowCongestionLevel}...], widthPixels?} — congestion-colored traffic lines. An absent color/widthPixels/radiusPixels override keeps the documented map-rendering default style; the fields exist exactly where the native overlay structs have them. Colors are {red, green, blue, alpha} in 0.0..=1.0; widths and radii are positive finite screen pixel values. Every invalid descriptor (wrong shape, missing or wrong-typed field, out-of-range coordinate or channel, unknown kind or congestion value) rejects the whole call with a string-valued error and keeps the previous list in force; nothing panics.
addOverlayaddOverlay(overlay: any): stringReturns string. Throws the verbatim failure message as a string.Adds one overlay descriptor to the drawn list and answers the generated opaque identifier addressing it (overlay-1, overlay-2, …; monotonic per view, never reused). Validation is exactly set_overlays’ single-descriptor rule: a refused descriptor throws and adds nothing. The new overlay draws last, over the entries already in the list.
updateOverlayupdateOverlay(identifier: string, overlay: any): voidThrows the verbatim failure message as a string.Replaces the overlay addressed by identifier in its draw position. An invalid descriptor throws and keeps the previous overlay; an unknown identifier throws a string-valued error naming it.
removeOverlayremoveOverlay(identifier: string): booleanReturns boolean.Removes the overlay addressed by identifier; answers whether the identifier was present (an unknown identifier is not an error).
clearOverlaysclearOverlays(): void—Clears the overlay list; following frames draw the tiles alone until [MapView::set_overlays] or [MapView::add_overlay] supplies a new list. Clears the bulk list and every addressed overlay alike.
setLabelssetLabels(labels: any[]): numberReturns number. Throws the verbatim failure message as a string.Replaces the label candidates drawn over the overlays in every following [MapView::render_frame], and answers how many the call accepted. Each descriptor carries its text, geographic anchor, paint, halos, size and collision fields; [MapView::set_glyph_range] must supply the glyphs before anything draws. Every invalid descriptor rejects the whole call with a string-valued error and keeps the previous list in force; nothing panics.
clearLabelsclearLabels(): void—Clears the label candidate list; following frames draw no labels until [MapView::set_labels] supplies a new list.
setGlyphRangesetGlyphRange(glyphRangeBytes: Uint8Array): objectReturns object. Throws the verbatim failure message as a string.Decodes one Mapbox glyph-protocol range and packs it into the R8Unorm atlas the label layer draws with. Answers the decoded font stack name, glyph count and page dimensions for the page’s status readout. A malformed payload or an un-packable range is a string-valued rejection and keeps the previous font in force.
setLocationIndicatorsetLocationIndicator(stateValue: any, styleValue: any): voidThrows the verbatim failure message as a string.Sets the location-indicator layer drawn over the overlays in every following [MapView::render_frame] (the native surface’s top layer, round 10), replacing any earlier layer. The state descriptor is {coordinate: {latitude, longitude}, courseHeadingDegrees?, horizontalAccuracyMeters?}; the style descriptor is {visualKind: "trackingDot" \| "guidedCourseArrow", radiusPixels?, rgbaColor?, showAccuracyRing?}, where every omitted style field keeps the documented map-rendering default. Colors are {red, green, blue, alpha} in 0.0..=1.0; the radius is a positive finite screen-pixel value. The optional scalars pass through verbatim (the native indicator state’s rule) while the style’s own range rules mirror the native record conversion. Every invalid descriptor rejects the whole call with a string-valued error and keeps the previous layer in force; nothing panics.
clearLocationIndicatorclearLocationIndicator(): void—Clears the location-indicator layer; following frames draw no indicator until [MapView::set_location_indicator] supplies a new one.
setVectorTileSourcesetVectorTileSource(source: any): voidThrows the verbatim failure message as a string.Installs a styled vector base map (M31 — the UDL MapView.set_vector_tile_source contract member, now served by the browser canvas too). The descriptor is one plain JavaScript object carrying the UDL UrlTemplateVectorTileSource fields in lower camel case: {urlTemplate, sourceName, attributionText, styleId, minimumZoomLevel, maximumZoomLevel}. The template must be an absolute http/https URL carrying {z}, {x} and {y}; the style id must name one of the committed style artifacts (bright-light, fiord-dark, …). The whole source builds before this view changes, so a refused call (a malformed template, an empty name, an inverted zoom range or an unknown style id) throws a string-valued error and leaves the previous base in force. While a source is installed the canvas hides the raster base and paints the style’s own background, exactly like the native surface; the source’s overlays and place names draw beneath every overlay the page supplies. Installing while a frame resolves is refused.
clearVectorTileSourceclearVectorTileSource(): voidThrows the verbatim failure message as a string.Removes the vector base map (M31 — the UDL MapView.clear_vector_tile_source contract member): following frames draw raster tiles and overlays alone. Refused while a frame resolves, like installing.
vectorTileSourceStatusvectorTileSourceStatus(): objectReturns object. Throws the verbatim failure message as a string.Reads the vector base source’s status (M31 — the UDL MapView.vector_tile_source_status contract member): the configured source’s style, name, attribution and zoom ceiling plus the last resolved frame’s drawn and failed tile counts. A pure query — it never fetches or draws — and it answers an honest not-configured status with no source installed.
setBaseMapVisiblesetBaseMapVisible(visible: boolean): void—Shows or hides the raster tile base layer in every following [MapView::render_frame]. Hidden frames still clear the surface and draw the overlay and location-indicator layers, so the page can paint a vector base map through [MapView::set_overlays] while this raster layer is hidden. A hidden frame skips the tile listing, same-origin fetches, scheduler warm/resolve, texture uploads and tile draws, and reports requestedTiles: 0, drawnTiles: 0 and missingTiles: 0 while keeping the current tileZoomLevel, tileResolution and overlayTriangles statistics. Showing the layer again resolves tiles normally on the next frame (the texture cache survives hidden frames).
setRasterTileSourcesetRasterTileSource(urlTemplate: string, maximumZoomLevel: number): voidThrows the verbatim failure message as a string.Sets (or clears, with a blank template) the live raster fallback: a {z}/{x}/{y} URL template from a provider registry descriptor that the frame fetches when no recorded fixture exists at an address, so a camera over unrecorded ground still draws imagery. The template must carry all three placeholders; the maximum zoom level caps the fetch zoom to what the tile service actually serves. The fallback runs only after the recorded-fixture fetch fails, so the local harness keeps its deterministic fixture demo, and a registered live provider (a runtime credential) is consulted before the template.
setBackgroundColorsetBackgroundColor(red: number, green: number, blue: number, alpha: number): voidThrows the verbatim failure message as a string.Sets the frame pass’s clear color (each channel 0..=1), the background behind any tiles or overlays that do not cover the surface. The default is the shared dark clear; the page paints a light clear around a vector base so the gaps between its fills do not read as a black map. A channel outside 0..=1 or a non-finite value is refused.

Navigator

Turn-by-turn navigation over a planned route, mirroring the driving and readback core of the contract’s Navigator.

Build it with new Navigator(); startNavigation(route, unitSystem) begins a trip over a Route exactly as calculateRoute answers it (unitSystem is "metric" or "imperial"), updateLocation(update) consumes one NavigationLocationUpdate and answers the trip snapshot (or null without a trip), applyReroute(route) swaps the active trip’s route, stopNavigation() clears it, and currentTripState() answers the latest snapshot (null without a trip).

The snapshot’s phase is "navigating", "offRoute" or "arrived" (the contract’s Navigating/OffRoute/Arrived); instruction is the composed payload (activeManeuver with distancePhraseText and displayText, an optional upcomingManeuver, progress, and the isArrival/isReroutingRequired markers); deviation is {statusChangeKind, distanceFromRouteMeters} exactly while the phase is off route; snappedCoordinate is {latitude, longitude} once a fix has been processed. The listener, speech and reroute-recalculation members of the contract’s Navigator stay native until the wasm seam carries a foreign-listener contract; hasActiveTrip() is the wasm-only helper.

This is the wasm seam’s event bridge (the contract’s foreign-listener trait cannot cross the wasm-bindgen boundary); the topics and payloads mirror the native navigation listener’s.

Vector tile helpers

Throws the verbatim failure message as a string.Decodes and styles one vector tile into the overlay descriptor list the WebGPU canvas consumes. tile_bytes is the wire body a provider served — plain MVT protobuf or a gzip-wrapped body, which is sniffed and unwrapped here — and the tile address is validated against the zoom grid before decoding. The result is a plain JavaScript array of set_overlays descriptors in style-layer order (later style layers paint over earlier ones). A malformed payload, an out-of-grid address, an empty body or an undecompressable gzip envelope rejects with a string-valued error; nothing throws across the wasm boundary as a panic.

Throws the verbatim failure message as a string.The same decode-and-style conversion, painted with the committed style a style id names (carto-light, carto-dark, openmaptiles-light, openmaptiles-dark). The page joins a registry descriptor’s style schema with the active theme, so one provider can serve a light and a dark base map without a page-side style table. An unknown style id rejects with the documented list of known ids.

Throws the verbatim failure message as a string.Decodes and styles one vector tile into the label descriptors the WebGPU canvas’ [crate::canvas::MapView::set_labels] consumes. A point-placed symbol candidate carries its anchor; a line-placed one (a road name) also carries the line geometry the canvas runs the text along. The address and wire bytes are validated exactly like the overlay export, and the labels come from the same style conversion (the symbol layers’ text fallbacks, paint, size stops, priority, rank and overlap rule), so the overlay and label halves of one tile cannot disagree. Size stops evaluate at the tile’s own integer zoom level — the page lists tiles at the camera’s rounded zoom — and the canvas places the labels at the exact frame camera pose. A malformed payload or an out-of-grid address rejects with a string-valued error; nothing throws across the wasm boundary as a panic.

Throws the verbatim failure message as a string.The geographic bounds of one web-mercator tile, as {northWest: {latitude, longitude}, southEast: {latitude, longitude}}. The demo uses this to focus its camera on a fetched tile and the browser suites use it to check decoded overlay coordinates against the tile they came from. The conversion is the same [tile_local_point_to_coordinate] the overlay seam applies, so bounds and geometry share one source of truth. An out-of-grid address rejects with a string-valued error.

Union and alias shapes

SdkError

Failures the contract throws across the binding surface, mirroring the UDL SdkError variants one to one with their payload fields. On the wasm seam the failures are currently thrown as the plain, verbatim detail string (see the failure helper in map-web-bindings exports.rs), so a wasm catch handler compares messages; the discriminated union below is the structured contract shape the native surfaces receive.

\| { readonly variant: "InvalidCoordinateInput"; readonly detail: string } \| { readonly variant: "NetworkRequestFailed"; readonly detail: string } \| { readonly variant: "ResponseParsingFailure"; readonly detail: string } \| { readonly variant: "ProviderRequestRejected"; readonly detail: string } \| { readonly variant: "RateLimitExhausted" } \| { readonly variant: "ProviderNotConfigured"; readonly contractName: string } \| { readonly variant: "InvalidNavigationInput"; readonly detail: string } \| { readonly variant: "InvalidRenderInput"; readonly detail: string } \| { readonly variant: "RenderingSurfaceUnavailable"; readonly detail: string } \| { readonly variant: "CacheOperationFailure"; readonly detail: string } \| { readonly variant: "OfflineRoutingFailure"; readonly detail: string }

NavigatorEventTopic

One navigation event delivered to a listener registered through the wasm Navigator.addNavigationListener (M31): the contract’s foreign NavigationListener topics modelled over wasm-bindgen. instruction arrives for every dispatched fix, phase once per transition (with its phaseChange name), deviation when the deviation judgment changes, speech when a new non-empty instruction carries speech text, and the wasm-only stop when the trip ends (with a null snapshot).

\| "instruction" \| "phase" \| "deviation" \| "speech" \| "stop"

Errors

The WebAssembly surface throws plain strings, not typed objects. A catch handler compares the message; the message is the verbatim reason, and the native surfaces carry the same reasons as typed error variants.

VariantPayloadMeaning
InvalidCoordinateInputdetail: stringA coordinate, viewport extent or box corner failed validation.
NetworkRequestFaileddetail: stringThe network transport failed; carries the transport’s verbatim detail.
ResponseParsingFailuredetail: stringThe provider answered with a payload the parser could not use.
ProviderRequestRejecteddetail: stringThe provider returned a documented application-level failure status.
RateLimitExhaustedNoneThe token-bucket rate limiter is exhausted; retry after the next refill.
ProviderNotConfiguredcontractName: stringNo provider implementation is registered for the requested contract.
InvalidNavigationInputdetail: stringA navigation input (a route record or a navigation policy) failed validation.
InvalidRenderInputdetail: stringAn overlay descriptor did not describe a usable overlay (wrong kind payload, an out-of-range color channel, or a non-positive or non-finite width or radius), or a surface input was structurally unusable (a null, zero or ambiguous platform surface pointer, or a non-positive viewport extent).
RenderingSurfaceUnavailabledetail: stringLive rendering could not proceed on the platform surface: the platform handle or surface was unusable, the graphics context could not be acquired, the surface format could not be negotiated or configured, the frame texture could not be acquired, or the frame’s render state was busy in another draw.
CacheOperationFailuredetail: stringA cache read, write or eviction failed (an unavailable store, a corrupt entry, or a byte-budget refusal). The detail names the reason verbatim.
OfflineRoutingFailuredetail: stringAn offline routing graph failed validation or could not be read: a truncated or foreign archive, an unsupported version, or a malformed section. The detail names the reason verbatim.

Async and threading

  • The wasm runtime is module-global; create one root and one MapView per canvas.
  • Asynchronous calls return a Promise and reject with a verbatim string.
  • Frames are explicit and serialized. A second overlapping renderFrame is a borrow violation; keep a busy flag.
  • renderFrame consumes its MapCamera by value; build a fresh camera for each changed pose.
  • The navigation listener callback and diagnostics delivery are synchronous on the calling thread; do not block.

  • Turn-by-turn navigation drives the controller.

Rustic Maps SDK contract

The SDK has one API surface. A single UniFFI UDL contract defines every type and call, and the Android, iOS, React Native and WebAssembly bindings are built against that contract. This page explains what the contract contains, how each target binds it, and how to read the UDL. For member-by-member signatures and return records, use the API reference; the contract file itself is also published as a plain-text download.

What the contract is

The contract is one file written in UniFFI’s interface definition language. It declares the namespace, the records and enums that cross the language boundary, the objects that own state, the interfaces your own code can implement, and the error type every call can raise. It carries the doc comments the generated bindings show, so the contract is both the implementation source and the reference for the surface.

The contract is pre-1.0 and addition-only: an existing member keeps its signature and its meaning, and a release adds members rather than removing or renaming them. An upgrade therefore does not rewrite your calls. The changelog records what each area adds, and the versions and support page explains how releases are numbered.

Every target answers getSdkCompiledVersion, which reports the version of the loaded core. Compare it with the artifact you shipped; a mismatch means your dependency declaration and the loaded library disagree.

How each target binds it

The native targets are generated from the contract. The browser target is a hand-maintained TypeScript façade over the same Rust core, kept aligned with the contract by a parity check.

TargetBindingWhat you call
Android (Kotlin)Generated by UniFFI into uniffi.rustic_mapsSuspend functions, typed records, SdkException subclasses
iOS (Swift)Generated by UniFFI into the RusticMapsSDK moduleAsync throwing methods, typed records, an SdkError enum
React NativeA Turbo Module generated from the same contractPromise-returning methods, lower camel case field names
WebAssemblyA hand-maintained TypeScript façade over the wasm-bindgen moduleClasses, plain records, lower camel case field names

The contract namespace is rustic_maps. The generated Kotlin package carries that name, and the Swift bindings ship in the RusticMapsSDK module. The UDL writes members and fields in snake_case; the generated bindings camelCase them. Enum spellings follow the platform: Kotlin uses UPPER_SNAKE constants, Swift lowerCamel cases, and the TypeScript surfaces use the spelling of their generated or hand-maintained declaration. One concept keeps one name across platforms: MapView, MapCamera, MapSdk, Navigator, search, calculateRoute, startNavigation.

The namespace and core types

The namespace rustic_maps holds the free functions and the object types. The objects group the surface by capability.

Free functions

  • getSdkCompiledVersion — the compiled SDK version.
  • coordinateToNormalizedWorld, tileKeyForCoordinate, tilesCovering — projection and web-mercator tile addressing.
  • offlineRouteFromArchiveBytes — a route over an offline graph archive held in memory, with no provider registered.
  • defaultStepAdvancePolicy, defaultDeviationPolicy, defaultReroutePolicy — the SDK defaults a navigation session starts from.

Value records

Coordinates and geometry cross as GeographicCoordinate, BoundingBox, ScreenPoint, NormalizedWorldCoordinate, TileKey, ViewportSize and EdgeInsets. Provider results cross as Place, Route, RouteLeg, RouteStep, DistanceMatrix, TrafficIncident, TrafficFlowData and RasterTileData. Configuration crosses as RouteOptions, AvoidOptions, UrlTemplateRasterTileSource, UrlTemplateVectorTileSource, MapOverlay, OverlayColor and TileCacheTerms. Navigation crosses as NavigationLocationUpdate, TripNavigationState, NavigationInstruction, DeviationStatusChange, SimulatedTripPace, SimulatedTripFix and the policy records.

Objects

  • MapSdk — the provider registry and the provider-backed calls: geocoding, search, routing, distance matrix, traffic and raster tiles.
  • MapView — the native map surface: attach, resize, detach, per-frame draw, overlays, the location indicator, a vector base map and frame statistics.
  • Navigator — the navigation session: start, location updates, reroutes, topic subscriptions and read-only state.
  • RouteSimulator — deterministic interpolation along a planned route at a pace you choose.
  • SearchEngine, RoutingEngine, OfflineManager, Diagnostics — thin facades over the matching MapSdk members, so a capability has one object.
  • MapCamera — an immutable camera pose with projection, fit-bounds and gesture math.
  • Subscription — the handle that cancels one listener subscription.

Interfaces your code implements

  • GeocodingProvider and RasterTileProvider — register your own provider implementation on MapSdk.
  • NavigationListener — receive the instruction, deviation, phase and speech topics.
  • SdkDiagnosticEventListener — receive the SDK’s structured diagnostic events.

The error model

Every failure the contract declares is one variant of SdkError. A variant that carries a detail field carries the provider’s or the validator’s reason verbatim: surface that text as it arrives, because it names the condition support needs.

VariantMeaning
InvalidCoordinateInputA coordinate, viewport extent or box corner failed validation.
NetworkRequestFailedThe network transport failed.
ResponseParsingFailureThe provider answered with a payload the parser could not use.
ProviderRequestRejectedThe provider returned a documented application-level failure.
RateLimitExhaustedThe SDK’s token bucket is empty.
ProviderNotConfiguredNo implementation is registered for the requested contract.
InvalidNavigationInputA route record or navigation policy failed validation.
InvalidRenderInputAn overlay or surface input is structurally unusable.
RenderingSurfaceUnavailableThe platform surface could not present the frame.
CacheOperationFailureA cache read, write or eviction failed.
OfflineRoutingFailureAn offline routing archive failed validation or could not be read.

ProviderNotConfigured carries the contract name instead of a detail string; RateLimitExhausted carries no payload.

Retry NetworkRequestFailed with backoff, RateLimitExhausted after the next refill, and RenderingSurfaceUnavailable on the next frame. The other variants report a condition you must change: fix the input, register a provider, repair the archive or the cache, or report the verbatim detail.

The generated Kotlin, Swift and React Native bindings expose the typed variant, so you can branch on it. The WebAssembly façade throws a failure as its verbatim message string, so a browser handler matches the message or the condition it describes.

Async rules

Members that wait on the network or on other asynchronous work carry [Async] in the contract. The platform binding presents them in its own idiom: a suspend function in Kotlin, an async throwing method in Swift, a promise in React Native and WebAssembly. The SDK drives the I/O on its own runtime, so a call from the main thread does not block your event loop.

The same rule applies to the interfaces your code implements. GeocodingProvider and RasterTileProvider methods are async. Listener callbacks are synchronous: they run on the thread that produced the event and must not block. Hand work to your UI layer instead.

MapView.draw is async and single-flight. One frame may be in flight per view; a concurrent draw or resize reports RenderingSurfaceUnavailable, and the next frame retries. Call isFrameSettled first and skip the draw when nothing has changed.

A subscription is cancelled explicitly with Subscription.cancel. The call is idempotent, and dropping the handle does not unsubscribe.

How to read the UDL

The contract uses a small set of UniFFI constructs. Read the file with this table in hand.

You seeIt declares
namespace rustic_maps { ... }The free functions of the contract.
dictionary Name { ... }A record: a plain value with the listed fields.
enum Name { "Variant", ... }A closed set of values. UDL writes enum variants as quoted names.
interface Name { ... }An object with methods; some declare constructors.
[Error] interface SdkError { ... }The error type and its variants; each variant lists its payload fields.
[Trait, WithForeign] interface Name { ... }An interface your foreign code implements and registers.
[Throws=SdkError]The member can raise an SdkError variant.
[Async]The member returns a future. Per-member attributes are the only async form the UDL parser accepts.
[Name=fit_bounds]The constructor or method is exposed under the given name.

Field types read as follows: string, double, boolean, u8, u32 and u64 are the scalar types; bytes is a byte sequence; sequence<T> is a list; a trailing ? marks an optional value. A dictionary field may name another dictionary or an enum. The /// comments in the file are the doc comments the generated bindings carry.

This excerpt shows the four shapes together: a free function, a record, an enum, and a provider interface your code implements.

namespace rustic_maps {
    string get_sdk_compiled_version();

    [Throws=SdkError]
    TileKey tile_key_for_coordinate(GeographicCoordinate coordinate, u8 zoom_level);
};

dictionary TileKey {
    u32 tile_x;
    u32 tile_y;
    u8 zoom_level;
};

enum UnitSystem {
    "Metric",
    "Imperial",
};

[Trait, WithForeign]
interface GeocodingProvider {
    [Async, Throws=SdkError]
    sequence<Place> reverse_geocode(GeographicCoordinate coordinate);
};

Read a member’s name twice: the UDL spelling is what the Rust implementation uses, and the camelCase spelling is what you type in Kotlin, Swift, React Native or the browser. A member without [Async] returns its value directly.
